--!strict
-- Dos.lua -- INT 21h subset + INT 20h/27h; console, handles, vectors, arena.

const band, bor, lshift, rshift = bit32.band, bit32.bor, bit32.lshift, bit32.rshift

const CF = 1
const ZF = 64

const Dos = {}
Dos.__index = Dos

export type Host = {
	mem: any,
	cpu: any,
	xms: any,
	vfs: any,
	bios: any,
	keys: { number },
	waiting: string?,
	pendingInt: number?,
	pspSeg: number?,
	deps: any,
	memBlocks: { { start: number, size: number, owner: number } },
	lastChildCode: number?,
	exit: (self: any, code: number) -> (),
	dosTerminate: (self: any, cpu: any, code: number) -> boolean,
	dosAlloc: (self: any, paras: number) -> number?,
	dosReserve: (self: any, start: number, paras: number) -> boolean,
	dosSetOwner: (self: any, seg: number, owner: number) -> boolean,
	dosFree: (self: any, seg: number) -> boolean,
	dosLargest: (self: any) -> number,
	syncArena: (self: any) -> (),
	log: (self: any, message: string) -> (),
}

export type Handle = {
	console: boolean,
	stdin: boolean?,
	device: boolean?,
	nul: boolean?,
	path: string?,
	data: string?,
	pos: number?,
	ownerPsp: number?,
}

export type Handler = (self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -> ()

export type Dos = {
	machine: Host,
	handles: { [number]: Handle },
	nextHandle: number,
	cwd: string,
	allocStrategy: number,
	execFrames: { [number]: any },
	sessionPsps: { [number]: boolean },
	kernelSessionPsps: { [number]: boolean },
	wswapPsps: { [number]: boolean },
	savedKernel: { { linear: number, data: buffer } }?,
	kernelPsp: number?,
	umbLink: number,
	pendingLine: string?,
	currentPsp: number?,
	createdPsps: { [number]: number },
	defaultDrive: number,
	countryCode: number,
	dtaSeg: number?,
	dtaOff: number?,
	find: {
		entries: { { name: string, size: number, dir: boolean } },
		index: number,
		fcbMode: boolean,
	}?,
	ctrlBreak: boolean?,
	FN: { [number]: Handler },
	initLowMemory: (self: Dos) -> (),
	deviceName: (self: Dos, path: string) -> string?,
	readRawAsciz: (self: Dos, cpu: any) -> string,
	readAsciz: (self: Dos, cpu: any) -> string,
	int21: (self: Dos) -> (),
	int20: (self: Dos) -> (),
	divideOverflow: (self: Dos) -> (),
}

function Dos.new(machine: Host): Dos
	const self = setmetatable({}, Dos) :: any
	self.machine = machine
	self.handles = {
		[0] = { console = true, stdin = true }, -- stdin
		[1] = { console = true }, -- stdout
		[2] = { console = true }, -- stderr
	}
	self.nextHandle = 3
	self.cwd = "C:\\"
	self.allocStrategy = 0
	self.execFrames = {}
	self.sessionPsps = {}
	self.kernelSessionPsps = {}
	self.wswapPsps = {}
	self.savedKernel = nil
	self.kernelPsp = nil
	self.umbLink = 0
	self.pendingLine = nil -- partial AH=0A input across keyboard waits
	self.currentPsp = nil
	self.createdPsps = {}
	self.defaultDrive = 2 -- C:
	self.countryCode = 1 -- United States
	self.ctrlBreak = false
	self:initLowMemory()
	return self
end

-- DOS data area: system file table, list of lists, DPB and device headers.
-- Windows 3.0 locates the SFT by scanning low memory for three equally spaced
-- "CON " names (stdin/stdout/stderr); the 59-byte entry size is what it reels
-- in, so these tables must sit in memory exactly like real DOS.
Dos.DATA_SEG = 0x0060
Dos.SFT_ENTRY_SIZE = 59
Dos.SFT_OFF = 0x0000
Dos.LOL_OFF = 0x0100
Dos.DPB_OFF = 0x0180
Dos.DEV_OFF = 0x01C0
Dos.INDOS_OFF = 0x01D0
Dos.DEV_STUB_OFF = 0x01E0

function Dos.initLowMemory(self: Dos)
	const mem = self.machine.mem
	const seg = Dos.DATA_SEG
	const base = lshift(seg, 4)

	-- System file table: header then 59-byte entries for CON stdin/out/err.
	mem:write16(base + Dos.SFT_OFF, 0xFFFF) -- next SFT: end of chain
	mem:write16(base + Dos.SFT_OFF + 2, 0xFFFF)
	mem:write16(base + Dos.SFT_OFF + 4, 3) -- entries in this table
	for index = 0, 2 do
		const entry = base + Dos.SFT_OFF + 6 + index * Dos.SFT_ENTRY_SIZE
		mem:write16(entry + 0x00, 1) -- handles referring to this entry
		mem:write16(entry + 0x02, 2) -- open mode: read/write
		mem:write8(entry + 0x04, 0x80) -- attribute: device
		mem:write16(entry + 0x05, 0x80D3) -- CON device info: in+out, special
		mem:write16(entry + 0x07, Dos.DEV_OFF) -- device header pointer
		mem:write16(entry + 0x09, seg)
		mem:writeString(entry + 0x1E, "CON        ") -- 11-byte name field
	end

	-- Device header for CON (next device = end of chain, char device). The
	-- strategy/interrupt offsets must point at executable RETF stubs inside
	-- this segment; the request header in ES:BX is left with status 0.
	const dev = base + Dos.DEV_OFF
	mem:write16(dev + 0x00, 0xFFFF)
	mem:write16(dev + 0x02, 0xFFFF)
	mem:write16(dev + 0x04, 0x8013) -- char, CONIN, CONOUT, special
	mem:write16(dev + 0x06, Dos.DEV_STUB_OFF)
	mem:write16(dev + 0x08, Dos.DEV_STUB_OFF)
	mem:writeString(dev + 0x0A, "CON     ") -- 8-byte device name
	mem:write8(base + Dos.DEV_STUB_OFF, 0xCB) -- RETF (strategy + interrupt)

	-- Disk parameter block: one drive, chain terminated.
	const dpb = base + Dos.DPB_OFF
	mem:write8(dpb + 0x00, 0) -- drive A:
	mem:write8(dpb + 0x01, 0)
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x02, 512) -- bytes per sector
	mem:write8(dpb + 0x04, 1) -- sectors per cluster - 1
	mem:write8(dpb + 0x05, 0) -- cluster shift
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x06, 1) -- first FAT sector
	mem:write8(dpb + 0x08, 2) -- number of FATs
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x09, 112) -- root dir entries
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x0B, 14) -- first data sector
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x0D, 354) -- clusters
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x0F, 9) -- sectors per FAT
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x11, 19) -- first root dir sector
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x13, Dos.DEV_OFF) -- device driver
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x15, seg)
	mem:write8(dpb + 0x17, 0xF9) -- media descriptor
	mem:write8(dpb + 0x18, 0)
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x19, 0xFFFF) -- next DPB: end of chain
	mem:write16(dpb + 0x1B, 0xFFFF)

	-- List of lists. AH=52 returns a pointer to the first DPB field, so the
	-- first MCB sits at ptr-2 and the first SFT at ptr+4.
	const lol = base + Dos.LOL_OFF
	mem:write16(lol + 0x00, 0x0050) -- first MCB segment
	mem:write16(lol + 0x02, Dos.DPB_OFF) -- first DPB
	mem:write16(lol + 0x04, seg)
	mem:write16(lol + 0x06, Dos.SFT_OFF) -- first SFT
	mem:write16(lol + 0x08, seg)
	mem:write16(lol + 0x0A, Dos.DEV_OFF) -- CLOCK$ (placeholder)
	mem:write16(lol + 0x0C, seg)
	mem:write16(lol + 0x0E, Dos.DEV_OFF) -- CON
	mem:write16(lol + 0x10, seg)
	mem:write16(lol + 0x12, 512) -- max bytes per sector
	mem:write16(lol + 0x20, 1) -- block devices
	mem:write8(lol + 0x22, 0) -- last drive
	mem:write16(lol + 0x24, Dos.DEV_OFF) -- NUL device chain head
	mem:write16(lol + 0x26, seg)

	mem:write8(base + Dos.INDOS_OFF, 0)
end

-- device names short-circuit file opens ("CON" and friends)
function Dos.deviceName(_self: Dos, path: string): string?
	const name = string.upper(path):gsub("%s+$", ""):gsub(":$", "")
	if name == "CON" or name == "NUL" or name == "AUX" or name == "PRN" then
		return name
	end
	return nil
end

-- helpers over cpu registers (r: AX CX DX BX SP BP SI DI)
local function al(cpu: any): number
	return band(cpu.r[1], 0xFF)
end

local function ah(cpu: any): number
	return band(rshift(cpu.r[1], 8), 0xFF)
end

local function setAX(cpu: any, value: number)
	cpu.r[1] = band(value, 0xFFFF)
end

local function ok(cpu: any)
	cpu:setbits(CF, false)
end

-- Last DOS error code set by `fail`, reported by INT 21h AH=59.
local lastErrorCode = 0

local function fail(cpu: any, code: number)
	lastErrorCode = code
	cpu:setbits(CF, true)
	setAX(cpu, code)
end

function Dos.readRawAsciz(self: Dos, cpu: any): string
	const base = lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[3]
	local chars: { string } = {}
	for index = 0, 255 do
		const ch = self.machine.mem:read8(base + index)
		if ch == 0 then
			break
		end
		chars[#chars + 1] = string.char(ch)
	end
	return table.concat(chars)
end

function Dos.readAsciz(self: Dos, cpu: any): string
	return self.machine.vfs:resolve(self:readRawAsciz(cpu), self.cwd)
end

function Dos.int21(self: Dos)
	const machine = self.machine
	const cpu = machine.cpu
	const number = ah(cpu)
	const handler = Dos.FN[number]
	if not handler then
		-- Functions >= B0 are Windows-internal hooks probing the DOS layer;
		-- fail them gracefully so the caller decides, and keep the loud error
		-- for genuinely expected DOS calls during development.
		if number >= 0xB0 then
			fail(cpu, 1) -- invalid function
			return
		end
		error(("unsupported INT 21h function AH=%02X at %04X:%04X"):format(number, cpu.cs, cpu.ip))
	end
	handler(self, cpu, machine)
end

function Dos.int20(self: Dos)
	self.machine:exit(0)
end

-- divide error default: print message, terminate (real DOS behavior)
function Dos.divideOverflow(self: Dos)
	self.machine.bios:write("Divide overflow\r\n")
	self.machine:exit(0)
end

Dos.FN = {} :: { [number]: Handler }

Dos.FN[0x00] = function(_self, cpu, machine)
	machine:dosTerminate(cpu, 0)
end

Dos.FN[0x01] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- read key with echo
	if #machine.keys == 0 then
		cpu.halted = true
		machine.waiting = "keyboard"
		machine.pendingInt = 0x21
		return
	end
	const key = table.remove(machine.keys, 1) :: number
	machine.bios:teletype(key)
	setAX(cpu, key)
end

Dos.FN[0x02] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- write DL
	const dl = band(cpu.r[3], 0xFF)
	machine.bios:teletype(dl)
	cpu:wb(0, dl) -- AL = DL per documented return
end

Dos.FN[0x06] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- direct console I/O
	const dl = band(cpu.r[3], 0xFF)
	if dl == 0xFF then
		if #machine.keys == 0 then
			cpu:setbits(ZF, true)
			setAX(cpu, 0)
		else
			cpu:setbits(ZF, false)
			const key = table.remove(machine.keys, 1) :: number
			setAX(cpu, key)
		end
	else
		machine.bios:teletype(dl)
		setAX(cpu, dl)
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x07] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host)
	Dos.FN[0x08](self, cpu, machine)
end

Dos.FN[0x08] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- read key, no echo
	if #machine.keys == 0 then
		cpu.halted = true
		machine.waiting = "keyboard"
		machine.pendingInt = 0x21
		return
	end
	setAX(cpu, table.remove(machine.keys, 1) :: number)
end

Dos.FN[0x09] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- print $-terminated string at DS:DX
	const mem = machine.mem
	const base = lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[3]
	local parts: { string } = {}
	for index = 0, 4095 do
		const ch = mem:read8(base + index)
		if ch == 0x24 then
			break
		end
		parts[#parts + 1] = string.char(ch)
	end
	machine.bios:write(table.concat(parts))
end

Dos.FN[0x0A] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- buffered line input
	const mem = machine.mem
	const base = lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[3]
	const maxLength = mem:read8(base)
	local buffer = self.pendingLine or ""
	while #buffer < maxLength - 1 do
		if #machine.keys == 0 then
			cpu.halted = true
			machine.waiting = "keyboard"
			machine.pendingInt = 0x21
			self.pendingLine = buffer
			return
		end
		const key = table.remove(machine.keys, 1) :: number
		if key == 13 then
			break
		end
		buffer ..= string.char(key)
	end
	self.pendingLine = nil
	mem:write8(base + 1, #buffer)
	mem:writeString(base + 2, buffer)
	mem:write8(base + 2 + #buffer, 13)
	machine.bios:write(buffer)
	machine.bios:teletype(13)
	machine.bios:teletype(10)
end

Dos.FN[0x0B] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host)
	setAX(cpu, (#machine.keys > 0) and 0x00FF or 0)
end

Dos.FN[0x0C] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- flush input, then AL function
	table.clear(machine.keys)
	const sub = al(cpu)
	if sub == 0x01 or sub == 0x06 or sub == 0x07 or sub == 0x08 or sub == 0x0A then
		cpu.r[1] = bor(band(cpu.r[1], 0x00FF), lshift(sub, 8))
		Dos.FN[sub](self, cpu, machine)
	else
		self.pendingLine = nil
		setAX(cpu, sub)
		ok(cpu)
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x19] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any)
	-- AL = current default drive (0 = A, 1 = B, 2 = C); AH = 0
	setAX(cpu, self.defaultDrive)
end

Dos.FN[0x0D] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any) -- disk reset: flush buffers
	ok(cpu)
end

-- select default drive (DL). The VFS is a single C: tree, but DOS programs
-- still probe/select drives, so accept the standard three and report success.
Dos.FN[0x0E] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any)
	const drive = band(cpu.r[3], 0xFF)
	if drive > 2 then
		fail(cpu, 0x0F) -- invalid drive
		return
	end
	self.defaultDrive = drive
	setAX(cpu, 3) -- number of logical drives
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x25] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- set interrupt vector AL <- DS:DX
	const vector = lshift(al(cpu), 2)
	machine.mem:write16(vector, cpu.r[3])
	machine.mem:write16(vector + 2, cpu.ds)
end

-- Parse an ASCIIZ filename into an FCB (INT 21h AH=29h). WIN.CNF/WSWAP use
-- this to split a path before opening it. AL=0 plain name, 1 wildcards,
-- 0FFh invalid drive; DS:SI advances to the terminating character.
Dos.FN[0x29] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host)
	const mem = machine.mem
	local si = cpu.r[7]
	const base = lshift(cpu.ds, 4)
	const fcb = lshift(cpu.es, 4) + cpu.r[8]
	for index = 0, 36 do
		mem:write8(fcb + index, 0)
	end
	local function peek(): number
		return mem:read8(base + si)
	end
	local function advance()
		si = band(si + 1, 0xFFFF)
	end
	local drive = 0
	if peek() ~= 0 and mem:read8(base + band(si + 1, 0xFFFF)) == 0x3A then
		const letter = peek()
		if letter >= 0x61 and letter <= 0x7A then
			drive = letter - 0x60
		else
			drive = letter - 0x40
		end
		si = band(si + 2, 0xFFFF)
		if drive < 1 or drive > 2 then
			cpu:wb(0, 0xFF)
			return
		end
	end
	mem:write8(fcb, drive)
	local name, ext = {}, {}
	local wildcard = false
	local inExt = false
	while true do
		const ch = peek()
		if
			ch == 0
			or ch == 0x5C
			or ch == 0x2F
			or ch == 0x20
			or ch == 0x09
			or ch == 0x3B
			or ch == 0x2C
			or ch == 0x3D
			or ch == 0x2B
		then
			break
		end
		if ch == 0x2E then
			inExt = true
		else
			local upper = ch
			if upper >= 0x61 and upper <= 0x7A then
				upper -= 0x20
			end
			if upper == 0x2A then
				wildcard = true
			end
			if inExt then
				if #ext < 3 then
					ext[#ext + 1] = string.char(upper)
				end
			elseif #name < 8 then
				name[#name + 1] = string.char(upper)
			end
		end
		advance()
	end
	const nameText = table.concat(name)
	const extText = table.concat(ext)
	mem:writeString(fcb + 1, nameText .. string.rep(" ", 8 - #nameText))
	if nameText:find("?") or nameText:find("*") then
		wildcard = true
	end
	mem:writeString(fcb + 9, extText .. string.rep(" ", 3 - #extText))
	if extText:find("?") or extText:find("*") then
		wildcard = true
	end
	cpu.r[7] = si
	cpu:wb(0, if wildcard then 1 else 0)
end

Dos.FN[0x2A] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any) -- get date (fixed): 1990-01-01, Monday
	cpu:wb(0, 1) -- AL day of week (0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday)
	cpu.r[2] = 1990 -- CX year
	cpu:wb(6, 1) -- DH month
	cpu:wb(2, 1) -- DL day
end

Dos.FN[0x2B] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any) -- set date: accept and report success
	cpu:wb(0, 0)
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x2C] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- get time
	-- Keep the noon baseline but advance with the BDA tick. CLOCK polls this
	-- until the second changes; a frozen clock spins forever before SetTimer.
	const ticks = machine.mem:read16(0x46C)
	const seconds = 12 * 3600 + math.floor(ticks / 18.2065)
	const hundredths = math.floor((ticks % 18.2065) * 100 / 18.2065)
	cpu:wb(5, math.floor(seconds / 3600) % 24) -- CH hour
	cpu:wb(1, math.floor(seconds / 60) % 60) -- CL minute
	cpu:wb(6, seconds % 60) -- DH second
	cpu:wb(2, hundredths) -- DL hundredths
end

Dos.FN[0x30] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any) -- DOS version 5.0
	setAX(cpu, 0x0005)
	cpu.r[4] = 0
	cpu.r[2] = 0
end

Dos.FN[0x35] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- get interrupt vector AL -> ES:BX
	const vector = lshift(al(cpu), 2)
	cpu.r[4] = machine.mem:read16(vector)
	cpu.es = machine.mem:read16(vector + 2)
end

-- Country information (INT 21h AH=38h). WIN.CNF sets country 1 and then reads
-- the block before it hands off to DOSX. Only the US layout is modelled, but
-- the returned 34-byte structure is complete enough for DOS/Win16 callers.
Dos.FN[0x38] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host)
	const mem = machine.mem
	const sub = al(cpu)
	if sub == 1 or sub == 0xFF then
		const requested = cpu.r[4]
		if requested ~= 0 then
			self.countryCode = requested
		end
	end
	const base = lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[3]
	for index = 0, 33 do
		mem:write8(base + index, 0)
	end
	mem:write8(base + 0, 0) -- date format: m/d/y
	mem:write8(base + 1, 0x24) -- currency symbol "$"
	mem:write8(base + 2, 0)
	mem:write8(base + 3, 0)
	mem:write8(base + 4, 0)
	mem:write8(base + 5, 0)
	mem:write8(base + 6, 0x2C) -- thousands separator ","
	mem:write8(base + 7, 0x2E) -- decimal separator "."
	mem:write8(base + 8, 0x2F) -- date separator "/"
	mem:write8(base + 9, 0x3A) -- time separator ":"
	mem:write8(base + 10, 0) -- currency format
	mem:write8(base + 11, 2) -- digits after decimal
	mem:write8(base + 12, 0) -- 12-hour clock
	mem:write8(base + 17, 0x2C) -- data list separator ","
	setAX(cpu, self.countryCode)
	cpu.r[4] = self.countryCode
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x39] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host)
	const made, err = machine.vfs:mkdir(self:readAsciz(cpu))
	if not made then
		fail(cpu, err or 3)
	else
		ok(cpu)
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x3B] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host)
	const good, err = machine.vfs:setCwd(self:readAsciz(cpu), self.cwd)
	if not good then
		fail(cpu, err or 3)
	else
		self.cwd = machine.vfs.cwd
		ok(cpu)
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x3C] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- create/truncate file
	const path = self:readAsciz(cpu)
	if not machine.vfs:writeFile(path, "") then
		fail(cpu, 3)
		return
	end
	self.handles[self.nextHandle] = {
		console = false,
		path = path,
		data = "",
		pos = 0,
		ownerPsp = self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0,
	}
	setAX(cpu, self.nextHandle)
	self.nextHandle += 1
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x5B] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- create new file
	const path = machine.vfs:resolve(self:readRawAsciz(cpu), self.cwd)
	if machine.vfs:exists(path) then
		fail(cpu, 0x50) -- file already exists
		return
	end
	if not machine.vfs:writeFile(path, "") then
		fail(cpu, 3)
		return
	end
	self.handles[self.nextHandle] = {
		console = false,
		path = path,
		data = "",
		pos = 0,
		ownerPsp = self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0,
	}
	setAX(cpu, self.nextHandle)
	self.nextHandle += 1
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x3D] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- open file
	machine:log(("OPEN [%s]"):format(self:readRawAsciz(cpu)))
	const raw = self:readRawAsciz(cpu)
	const device = self:deviceName(raw)
	if device then
		if device == "NUL" then
			self.handles[self.nextHandle] = {
				console = false,
				device = true,
				nul = true,
				ownerPsp = self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0,
			}
		elseif device == "CON" then
			self.handles[self.nextHandle] = {
				console = true,
				stdin = true,
				device = true,
				ownerPsp = self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0,
			}
		else
			fail(cpu, 2) -- AUX/PRN are not present on this machine
			return
		end
		setAX(cpu, self.nextHandle)
		self.nextHandle += 1
		ok(cpu)
		return
	end
	const path = machine.vfs:resolve(raw, self.cwd)
	const data = machine.vfs:readFile(path)
	if data == nil then
		fail(cpu, 2)
		return
	end
	self.handles[self.nextHandle] = {
		console = false,
		path = path,
		data = data,
		pos = 0,
		ownerPsp = self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0,
	}
	setAX(cpu, self.nextHandle)
	self.nextHandle += 1
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x3E] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- close handle BX
	const handle = self.handles[cpu.r[4]]
	if not handle then
		fail(cpu, 6)
		return
	end
	-- A child PSP inherits a copy of the parent's JFT. Closing that copy must
	-- not free the shared entry while the owner/parent still has it open; this
	-- bit KERNEL's lazily-read VGA.DRV/ VGA font handles (CALENDAR/REVERSI).
	const psp = self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0
	if handle.ownerPsp and psp ~= handle.ownerPsp then
		ok(cpu)
		return
	end
	if not handle.console and handle.path and handle.data then
		machine.vfs:writeFile(handle.path, handle.data)
	end
	self.handles[cpu.r[4]] = nil
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x3F] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- read from handle
	const handle = self.handles[cpu.r[4]]
	if not handle then
		fail(cpu, 6)
		return
	end
	const want = cpu.r[2]
	if handle.nul then
		setAX(cpu, 0)
		ok(cpu)
		return
	end
	if handle.console then
		if handle.stdin and #machine.keys == 0 then
			cpu.halted = true
			machine.waiting = "keyboard"
			machine.pendingInt = 0x21
			return
		end
		local got: { string } = {}
		while #machine.keys > 0 and #got < want do
			got[#got + 1] = string.char(table.remove(machine.keys, 1) :: number)
		end
		const text = table.concat(got)
		machine.mem:writeString(lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[3], text)
		setAX(cpu, #text)
	else
		const data = handle.data or ""
		const pos = handle.pos or 0
		const text = string.sub(data, pos + 1, pos + want)
		handle.pos = pos + #text
		machine.mem:writeString(lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[3], text)
		setAX(cpu, #text)
	end
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x40] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- write to handle
	const handle = self.handles[cpu.r[4]]
	if not handle then
		fail(cpu, 6)
		return
	end
	const text = machine.mem:readString(lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[3], cpu.r[2])
	if handle.nul then
		setAX(cpu, #text)
		ok(cpu)
		return
	end
	if handle.console then
		machine.bios:write(text)
	else
		const data = handle.data or ""
		const pos = handle.pos or 0
		-- DOS fills the gap with zeros when a write follows a seek past EOF
		const gap = if pos > #data then string.rep("\0", pos - #data) else ""
		handle.data = string.sub(data, 1, pos) .. gap .. text .. string.sub(data, pos + #text + 1)
		handle.pos = pos + #text
		if handle.path then
			machine.vfs:writeFile(handle.path, handle.data)
		end
	end
	setAX(cpu, #text)
	ok(cpu)
end

-- Put back the extended-memory stand-in saved when DSWAP was handed it.
local function restoreKernel(self: Dos, machine: Host)
	const saved = self.savedKernel
	if saved then
		self.savedKernel = nil
		for _, item in saved do
			buffer.copy(machine.mem.buf, item.linear, item.data, 0, buffer.len(item.data))
		end
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x41] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- delete file
	-- The swap-in (WSWAP after DSWAP) deletes its swap file as its last act and
	-- then enters the resumed DOSX, which never returns through AH=4C: this is
	-- the point where Windows' memory is back, so return the kernel block.
	if self.currentPsp and self.wswapPsps[self.currentPsp] then
		restoreKernel(self, machine)
	end
	const gone, err = machine.vfs:delete(self:readAsciz(cpu))
	if not gone then
		fail(cpu, err or 2)
	else
		ok(cpu)
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x56] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- rename/move file (DS:DX old, ES:DI new)
	const oldPath = self:readAsciz(cpu)
	local chars: { string } = {}
	const base = lshift(cpu.es, 4) + band(cpu.r[8], 0xFFFF)
	for index = 0, 255 do
		const ch = machine.mem:read8(base + index)
		if ch == 0 then
			break
		end
		chars[#chars + 1] = string.char(ch)
	end
	const newPath = machine.vfs:resolve(table.concat(chars), self.cwd)
	const moved, err = machine.vfs:rename(oldPath, newPath)
	if not moved then
		fail(cpu, err or 2)
	else
		ok(cpu)
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x42] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, _machine: Host) -- lseek
	const handle = self.handles[cpu.r[4]]
	if not handle or handle.console then
		fail(cpu, 6)
		return
	end
	const offset = band(cpu.r[2], 0xFFFF) * 65536 + cpu.r[3]
	const origin = al(cpu)
	const size = #(handle.data or "")
	local base = 0
	if origin == 1 then
		base = handle.pos or 0
	elseif origin ~= 0 then
		base = size
	end
	local position = base + offset
	if position < 0 then
		position = 0
	end
	handle.pos = position
	setAX(cpu, band(position, 0xFFFF))
	cpu:wr(2, band(rshift(position, 16), 0xFFFF))
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x43] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- get/set file attributes
	const path = self:readAsciz(cpu)
	const node = machine.vfs:lookup(path)
	if not node then
		fail(cpu, 2)
		return
	end
	if al(cpu) == 0 then
		cpu.r[2] = node.type == "dir" and 0x10 or 0x20 -- CX: directory / archive
		ok(cpu)
	elseif al(cpu) == 1 then
		ok(cpu) -- attributes are not modelled; accept the request
	else
		fail(cpu, 1)
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x57] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, _machine: Host) -- file date/time
	if al(cpu) == 0 then
		const handle = cpu.r[4] -- BX
		if handle == 0 then
			fail(cpu, 6)
			return
		end
		cpu.r[2] = 0x1421 -- CX: 1990-01-01
		cpu.r[3] = 0x6000 -- DX: 12:00:00
		ok(cpu)
	elseif al(cpu) == 1 then
		ok(cpu) -- timestamps are not modelled
	else
		fail(cpu, 1)
	end
end

-- IOCTL. Windows uses this to classify handles and drives: CON must report a
-- character device (bit 7) or KERNEL treats the console as a file and never
-- starts the shell. The rest of the subfunctions are the harmless single-drive
-- answers a plain DOS box gives.
Dos.FN[0x44] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host)
	const sub = al(cpu)
	if sub == 0 then -- get device info
		const handle = self.handles[cpu.r[4]]
		if not handle then
			fail(cpu, 6)
			return
		end
		cpu.r[3] = handle.console and 0x80D3 or 0x0002
		ok(cpu)
	elseif sub == 1 then -- set device info (not modelled)
		ok(cpu)
	elseif sub == 6 then -- input status
		cpu:wb(0, (#machine.keys > 0) and 0xFF or 0x00)
		ok(cpu)
	elseif sub == 7 then -- output status
		cpu:wb(0, 0xFF)
		ok(cpu)
	elseif sub == 8 then -- is drive removable -> A:/B: floppy, C: fixed
		local drive = band(cpu.r[4], 0xFF)
		if drive == 0 then
			drive = self.defaultDrive + 1
		end
		if drive < 1 or drive > 3 then
			fail(cpu, 0x0F)
			return
		end
		-- DOS: AX=0 removable, AX=1 fixed. This was inverted (A:/B: fixed, C:
		-- removable), so WIN.COM/WSWAP picked A: as the fixed swap drive.
		setAX(cpu, drive <= 2 and 0 or 1)
		ok(cpu)
	elseif sub == 9 then -- is drive remote -> this machine has only local drives
		local drive = band(cpu.r[4], 0xFF)
		if drive == 0 then
			drive = self.defaultDrive + 1
		end
		if drive < 1 or drive > 3 then
			fail(cpu, 0x0F)
			return
		end
		cpu.r[3] = 0 -- DX: no remote/network attributes
		setAX(cpu, 0)
		ok(cpu)
	elseif sub == 0x0E then -- get logical drive map -> no mapped drive
		local drive = band(cpu.r[4], 0xFF)
		if drive == 0 then
			drive = self.defaultDrive + 1
		end
		if drive < 1 or drive > 3 then
			fail(cpu, 0x0F)
			return
		end
		setAX(cpu, 0)
		ok(cpu)
	elseif sub == 0x0A then -- is handle remote -> local
		cpu.r[3] = 0
		ok(cpu)
	else
		fail(cpu, 1)
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x47] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- get cwd -> DS:SI
	-- DOS convention: path from the root, no drive, NO trailing backslash
	-- (the root itself is the empty string), NUL-terminated.
	local path = string.sub(self.cwd, 4) -- strip "C:\"
	if string.sub(path, -1) == "\\" then
		path = string.sub(path, 1, -2)
	end
	machine.mem:writeString(lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[7], path)
	machine.mem:write8(lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[7] + #path, 0)
	-- DOS returns AH=1, AL=0 on success. WRITE's path helper scans for the
	-- terminator by comparing bytes to AL, so leaving AL='A' wraps the segment
	-- and turns its startup into a false "Insufficient memory" dialog.
	setAX(cpu, 0x0100)
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x48] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- allocate block (BX paras) -> AX base
	const segment = machine:dosAlloc(cpu.r[4])
	if not segment then
		fail(cpu, 8) -- INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY
		cpu:wr(3, machine:dosLargest()) -- BX = largest available
		return
	end
	-- blocks a running EXEC child allocates belong to it, so AH=4C frees them
	const owner = self.currentPsp
	if owner and self.execFrames[owner] and cpu.r[4] ~= 0 then
		machine:dosSetOwner(segment, owner)
	end
	setAX(cpu, segment)
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x49] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- free block (ES = base)
	if machine:dosFree(cpu.es) then
		ok(cpu)
	else
		fail(cpu, 9) -- invalid memory block address
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x4A] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- resize block (ES = base, BX = new size)
	const segment = cpu.es
	const newSize = cpu.r[4]
	for index, block in machine.memBlocks do
		if block.start == segment then
			if block.size >= newSize then
				-- shrink / same: carve the remainder into a free block and
				-- merge it with a following free block, like DOS does
				if block.size >= newSize + 2 then
					const rest = {
						start = block.start + newSize + 1,
						size = block.size - newSize - 1,
						owner = 0,
					}
					block.size = newSize
					table.insert(machine.memBlocks, index + 1, rest)
					const after = machine.memBlocks[index + 2]
					if after and after.owner == 0 then
						rest.size += after.size + 1
						table.remove(machine.memBlocks, index + 2)
					end
					machine:syncArena()
				end
				ok(cpu)
			else
				-- grow: only if the next block is free and big enough
				const next = machine.memBlocks[index + 1]
				if next and next.owner == 0 and block.size + 1 + next.size >= newSize then
					const spare = next.size + block.size - newSize
					if spare >= 1 then
						block.size = newSize
						next.start = block.start + newSize + 1
						-- the neighbour keeps the paragraphs from its new MCB
						-- paragraph through its old end: exactly `spare` of
						-- them, or the chain ends one paragraph short of the
						-- arena top
						next.size = spare
					else
						-- the request takes the whole neighbour including its
						-- MCB paragraph (spare is 0 or -1): DOS hands the whole
						-- region over. Leaving block.size alone for spare == -1
						-- dropped the neighbour's paragraphs from the arena, so
						-- DSWAP's grow back to its full size lost ~140 KB and
						-- WSWAP could no longer load for the swap-in.
						block.size = block.size + 1 + next.size
						table.remove(machine.memBlocks, index + 1)
					end
					machine:syncArena()
					ok(cpu)
				else
					fail(cpu, 8)
					cpu:wr(3, machine:dosLargest())
				end
			end
			return
		end
	end
	fail(cpu, 9) -- invalid memory block address
end

Dos.FN[0x4B] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- EXEC
	const mode = band(cpu.r[1], 0xFF)
	const path = self:readAsciz(cpu)
	const data: string? = machine.vfs:readFile(path)
	machine:log(("EXEC %s (%s bytes)"):format(path, data and tostring(#data) or "missing"))
	if not data then
		fail(cpu, 2)
		return
	end
	if mode == 3 then
		error("EXEC load-overlay (AL=3) not implemented for " .. path)
	end
	if mode ~= 0 then
		error(("unsupported EXEC mode AL=%d for %s"):format(mode, path))
	end

	-- A child of the DOS-box swapper (WINOLDAP's WSWAP.EXE for the
	-- MS-DOS Prompt, and anything it starts) must hand control back to the EXEC caller when it ends;
	-- remember where the caller stands. Without DOSX (WIN.COM's own start of
	-- the kernel) the child keeps the load-and-run behaviour.
	local callerFrame: any = nil
	if
		cpu.dosxResident
		or self.kernelPsp ~= nil
		or string.find(string.upper(path), "WSWAP%.EXE$")
		or string.find(string.upper(path), "DSWAP%.EXE$")
		or next(self.execFrames) ~= nil
	then
		callerFrame = {
			cs = cpu.cs,
			ip = cpu.ip,
			ss = cpu.ss,
			sp = cpu.r[5],
			ds = cpu.ds,
			es = cpu.es,
			regs = table.clone(cpu.r),
			viaStub = cpu.stubSeg ~= nil and cpu.cs == cpu.stubSeg,
			parent = self.currentPsp,
		}
	end

	const esbx = lshift(cpu.es, 4) + cpu.r[4]
	const envSeg = machine.mem:read16(esbx)
	const cmdOff = machine.mem:read16(esbx + 2)
	const cmdSeg = machine.mem:read16(esbx + 4)

	const isMZ = string.byte(data, 1) == 0x4D and string.byte(data, 2) == 0x5A
	const buf = buffer.fromstring(data)
	-- XMS ownership handoff: DOSX claims all extended memory while it relocates
	-- its PM image, and releases the hold when the kernel EXEC happens (real
	-- DOSX frees before WSWAP allocates its swap block). Without this the
	-- kernel's swap allocations fail; with low-first allocation they used to
	-- land on the PM image instead (now top-first in Xms.allocate).
	if machine.xms then
		machine.xms:releaseAll()
	end

	-- Inherit the parent environment strings unless the caller supplied one.
	const parentPsp = self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0x1000
	const parentEnv = machine.mem:read16(lshift(parentPsp, 4) + 0x2C)
	const inherited = envSeg ~= 0 and envSeg or parentEnv

	-- DOS allocates a fresh environment block and a fresh program block.
	const newEnv = machine:dosAlloc(0x40)
	if not newEnv then
		machine:log("EXEC failed: no memory for environment")
		fail(cpu, 8)
		return
	end
	-- The DOSX / KRNL286 session this EXEC chain started has ended once the
	-- caller (WIN.COM) is running again, but DOSX leaves for WIN.COM without a
	-- DOS terminate, so its blocks were never released. DOS would have freed
	-- them on AH=4C; a swapper / DOS box EXEC needs that memory.
	local function reclaimSession(saveKernel: boolean): boolean
		if next(self.sessionPsps) == nil then
			return false
		end
		const stale: { number } = {}
		const saved: { { linear: number, data: buffer } } = {}
		for _, block in machine.memBlocks do
			if self.sessionPsps[block.owner] then
				stale[#stale + 1] = block.start
				if saveKernel and self.kernelSessionPsps[block.owner] then
					-- real KRNL286 keeps its memory in extended memory, out
					-- of DSWAP's reach and not part of the WSWAP swap file;
					-- here it is a conventional block DSWAP will overwrite,
					-- so keep a copy for the swap-in to put back
					const linear = lshift(block.start, 4)
					const data = buffer.create(block.size * 16)
					buffer.copy(data, 0, machine.mem.buf, linear, block.size * 16)
					saved[#saved + 1] = { linear = linear, data = data }
				end
			end
		end
		if #saved > 0 then
			self.savedKernel = saved
		end
		self.kernelSessionPsps = {}
		for _, start in stale do
			machine:dosFree(start)
		end
		self.sessionPsps = {}
		return true
	end
	-- DSWAP runs after WSWAP has swapped Windows out and loads the DOS app
	-- inside its own block: its header asks for maximum allocation (maxalloc
	-- FFFF), so DOS hands it every free paragraph. Windows' memory is already
	-- on the swap file at that point, so free it first. A small block made
	-- DSWAP's own "app needs more than the block holds" check fail (error 3),
	-- which WIN.COM reads as a failed DOS app.
	const isDswap = string.find(string.upper(path), "DSWAP%.EXE$") ~= nil
	local programParas: number
	if isMZ then
		const cblp = buffer.readu16(buf, 2)
		const cp = buffer.readu16(buf, 4)
		const cparhdr = buffer.readu16(buf, 8)
		local fileLen = cp * 512
		if cblp > 0 then
			fileLen -= 512 - cblp
		end
		const imageParas = math.ceil(math.max(fileLen - cparhdr * 16, 0) / 16)
		-- A bound NE image is mapped at the top of the program block and its
		-- own loader copies the NE segments down below the image. Reserve a
		-- second image-sized area for that copy plus 0x1000 paragraphs of
		-- heap. With only 0x1000 below the image, KERNEL's relocated segments
		-- and local heap collide with its stack (the AnsiUpper code gets
		-- overwritten from a module-data read).
		--
		-- A bound-NE KERNEL self-relocates and builds its global heap inside
		-- the program block, then loads NE segments from that heap. If the
		-- block ends where the image was mapped, the leftover memory above it
		-- becomes a separate heap arena; KERNEL's first-fit scan stops at that
		-- arena boundary before it can reach GDI's 21 KB segment hole, and the
		-- load fails. Reserve the whole free run for the program block, as DOS
		-- does when an EXE asks for maximum allocation, so the heap arena
		-- covers the segment area.
		const neOff = buffer.readu32(buf, 0x3C)
		const boundNE = neOff + 1 < buffer.len(buf)
			and buffer.readu8(buf, neOff) == 0x4E
			and buffer.readu8(buf, neOff + 1) == 0x45
		const minimumParas = 0x10 + imageParas + (if boundNE then imageParas else 0) + 0x1000
		programParas = if boundNE
			then math.max(minimumParas, machine:dosLargest())
			else minimumParas
		if isDswap and buffer.readu16(buf, 0x0C) == 0xFFFF then
			reclaimSession(true)
			programParas = math.max(minimumParas, machine:dosLargest())
		end
	else
		programParas = math.max(0x100 + math.ceil(buffer.len(buf) / 16), 0x1000)
	end
	local pspSeg = machine:dosAlloc(programParas)
	if not pspSeg and reclaimSession(false) then
		pspSeg = machine:dosAlloc(programParas)
	end
	if not pspSeg then
		const layout: { string } = {}
		for _, block in machine.memBlocks do
			layout[#layout + 1] = ("%X+%X/%X"):format(block.start, block.size, block.owner)
		end
		machine:log(
			("EXEC failed: no %X paragraphs (largest %X) blocks %s"):format(
				programParas,
				machine:dosLargest(),
				table.concat(layout, " ")
			)
		)
		machine:dosFree(newEnv)
		fail(cpu, 8)
		return
	end
	machine:dosSetOwner(newEnv, pspSeg)
	machine:dosSetOwner(pspSeg, pspSeg)
	if
		string.find(string.upper(path), "DOSX%.EXE$")
		or string.find(string.upper(path), "KRNL286%.EXE$")
	then
		self.sessionPsps[pspSeg] = true
		if string.find(string.upper(path), "KRNL286%.EXE$") then
			self.kernelSessionPsps[pspSeg] = true
		end
	end
	if string.find(string.upper(path), "WSWAP%.EXE$") then
		self.wswapPsps[pspSeg] = true
	end
	if string.find(string.upper(path), "KERNEL%.EXE$") and self.kernelPsp == nil then
		-- the real-mode Windows kernel is running from here on: every later
		-- EXEC (the MS-DOS Prompt's COMMAND.COM via WINOLDAP) is a normal DOS
		-- child that must return to its caller when it ends
		self.kernelPsp = pspSeg
	end

	if isMZ then
		-- Bound NE images self-relocate, so the MZ image is mapped at the top
		-- of the block and no eager NE fixups are applied here.
		machine.deps.Executables.loadMZ(machine, buf, path, pspSeg, newEnv, inherited, programParas)
	else
		machine.deps.Executables.loadCOM(
			machine,
			buf,
			pspSeg,
			path,
			newEnv,
			inherited,
			programParas
		)
	end

	-- PSP:2 is the top of the program's memory block.
	const pspBase = lshift(pspSeg, 4)
	machine.mem:write16(pspBase + 2, pspSeg + programParas)

	-- command tail -> child PSP:80
	local tail = ""
	if cmdSeg ~= 0 then
		const cmdBase = lshift(cmdSeg, 4) + cmdOff
		const length = machine.mem:read8(cmdBase)
		for index = 1, length do
			tail ..= string.char(machine.mem:read8(cmdBase + index))
		end
	end
	machine:log(("EXEC tail [%s] env %X"):format(tail, inherited))
	machine.mem:write8(pspBase + 0x80, #tail)
	if #tail > 0 then
		machine.mem:writeString(pspBase + 0x81, tail)
	end
	machine.mem:write8(pspBase + 0x81 + #tail, 0x0D)
	if callerFrame then
		self.execFrames[pspSeg] = callerFrame
		self.currentPsp = pspSeg
	end
	ok(cpu)
end

-- A PSP made by AH=55h (KERNEL's per-task PSP) is not an EXEC child: its
-- PSP:000A is the parent's return address (WIN.COM), so a real jump there
-- would end the whole Windows session whenever any app exits (Calculator
-- Alt+F4 exited with code 0). KERNEL only terminates the task PSP so DOS
-- frees its memory and expects control back after the INT 21h.
Dos.FN[0x4C] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host)
	const psp = self.currentPsp
	const frame = if psp then self.execFrames[psp] else nil
	if psp and frame then
		-- EXEC child ends: free its blocks and resume the caller just after
		-- its INT 21h (through the stub's IRET when the call was chained).
		self.execFrames[psp] = nil
		if self.wswapPsps[psp] then
			self.wswapPsps[psp] = nil
			restoreKernel(self, machine)
		end
		const owned: { number } = {}
		for _, block in machine.memBlocks do
			if block.owner == psp then
				owned[#owned + 1] = block.start
			end
		end
		for _, start in owned do
			machine:dosFree(start)
		end
		machine.lastChildCode = al(cpu)
		self.currentPsp = frame.parent
		cpu.cs, cpu.ip, cpu.ss, cpu.ds, cpu.es = frame.cs, frame.ip, frame.ss, frame.ds, frame.es
		for index = 1, 8 do
			cpu.r[index] = frame.regs[index]
		end
		cpu.r[5] = frame.sp
		if frame.viaStub then
			const word = machine.mem:read16(lshift(cpu.ss, 4) + band(frame.sp + 4, 0xFFFF))
			machine.mem:write16(lshift(cpu.ss, 4) + band(frame.sp + 4, 0xFFFF), band(word, 0xFFFE))
		end
		ok(cpu)
		return
	end
	const parent = if psp then self.createdPsps[psp] else nil
	if psp and parent then
		self.createdPsps[psp] = nil
		const owned: { number } = {}
		for _, block in machine.memBlocks do
			if block.owner == psp then
				owned[#owned + 1] = block.start
			end
		end
		for _, start in owned do
			machine:dosFree(start)
		end
		machine.lastChildCode = al(cpu)
		self.currentPsp = parent
		ok(cpu)
		return
	end
	machine:dosTerminate(cpu, al(cpu))
end

-- AH=4D: get the last child's return code.
-- AL = the exit code the child passed to AH=4Ch / INT 20h, AH = the
-- termination manner (00h normal, 01h ctrl-break, 03h stay-resident).
Dos.FN[0x4D] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host)
	-- real DOS: AL = the child's return code, AH = termination type (0 normal)
	setAX(cpu, band(machine.lastChildCode or 0, 0xFF))
end

-- Undocumented DOS "create child PSP" (used by EXEC and by KERNEL's own
-- loader): copy the current PSP to DX, put SI in the new PSP:0002, and record
-- the parent. No handle-table split is modelled; the child shares the JFT.
Dos.FN[0x55] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host)
	const childSeg = cpu.r[3] -- DX
	const parentSeg = self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0x1000
	const src = lshift(parentSeg, 4)
	const dst = lshift(childSeg, 4)
	for index = 0, 0xFF do
		machine.mem:write8(dst + index, machine.mem:read8(src + index))
	end
	machine.mem:write16(dst + 0x02, cpu.r[7]) -- SI: top of memory
	machine.mem:write16(dst + 0x16, parentSeg) -- parent PSP
	self.createdPsps[childSeg] = parentSeg
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x33] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, _machine: Host) -- ctrl-break flag
	if al(cpu) == 1 then
		self.ctrlBreak = band(cpu.r[3], 0xFF) ~= 0 -- DL
	end
	cpu:wb(2, self.ctrlBreak and 1 or 0) -- DL = current state
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x34] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- get InDOS flag address -> ES:BX
	const address = lshift(Dos.DATA_SEG, 4) + Dos.INDOS_OFF
	machine.mem:write8(address, 0) -- never inside DOS
	cpu.es = Dos.DATA_SEG
	cpu.r[4] = Dos.INDOS_OFF
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x52] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, _machine: Host) -- get list of lists -> ES:BX
	-- BX points at the first-DPB field: [BX-2] is the first MCB, [BX+4] the
	-- first SFT, [BX+22h] the NUL device header (standard DOS layout).
	cpu.es = Dos.DATA_SEG
	cpu.r[4] = Dos.LOL_OFF + 2
	ok(cpu)
end

-- Get extended error information: AX = last error, BH = class, BL = suggested
-- action, CH = locus. KRNL286 calls this after a failed file operation.
Dos.FN[0x59] = function(_self: Dos, cpu: any, _machine: Host)
	const code = lastErrorCode
	local class = 13 -- unknown
	local action = 1 -- retry
	if code == 2 or code == 3 or code == 18 then
		class = 8 -- not found
		action = 3 -- ask user to re-enter
	elseif code == 4 or code == 8 then
		class = 1 -- out of resource
		action = 4
	elseif code == 5 then
		class = 3 -- authorization
		action = 3
	elseif code == 6 or code == 1 then
		class = 7 -- application error
		action = 3
	end
	setAX(cpu, code)
	cpu.r[4] = bor(lshift(class, 8), action) -- BH:BL
	cpu.r[2] = bor(band(cpu.r[2], 0x00FF), lshift(2, 8)) -- CH = block device locus
	cpu:setbits(CF, false)
end

-- Get/set memory allocation strategy (AL=0/1) and UMB link state (AL=2/3).
-- WINOLDAP saves and restores both around the DOS box it starts.
Dos.FN[0x58] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, _machine: Host)
	const sub = al(cpu)
	if sub == 0 then
		setAX(cpu, self.allocStrategy)
	elseif sub == 1 then
		self.allocStrategy = band(cpu.r[4], 0xFFFF)
	elseif sub == 2 then
		setAX(cpu, self.umbLink)
	elseif sub == 3 then
		self.umbLink = band(cpu.r[4], 0xFF)
	else
		fail(cpu, 1)
		return
	end
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x50] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, _machine: Host) -- set PSP
	self.currentPsp = cpu.r[4]
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x51] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- get PSP
	const psp = self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0
	setAX(cpu, psp)
	cpu.r[4] = psp -- DOS documents BX=PSP; some callers read AX
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x62] = Dos.FN[0x51]

Dos.FN[0x1A] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, _machine: Host) -- set DTA (DS:DX)
	self.dtaSeg = cpu.ds
	self.dtaOff = cpu.r[3]
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x2F] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- get DTA -> ES:BX
	cpu.es = self.dtaSeg or self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0
	cpu.r[4] = self.dtaOff or 0x80
	ok(cpu)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------- find first/next
-- DOS directory searches come in two layouts: FCB searches (AH=11/12) fill a
-- 43-byte FCB-style entry in the DTA, while DOS 3+ searches (AH=4E/4F) fill
-- the 43-byte DTA entry with the attribute at +21h and the ASCIIZ name at
-- +20h.  Both share the same wildcard matcher and VFS listing.

local function splitName(name: string): (string, string)
	const base, ext = string.match(name, "^([^%.]*)%.?(.*)$")
	return base or name, ext or ""
end

local function padded11(name: string): string
	const base, ext = splitName(name)
	return (base .. "        "):sub(1, 8) .. (ext .. "   "):sub(1, 3)
end

local function fcbPattern(text: string): string
	text = string.upper(text)
	const base, ext = splitName(text)
	local function field(value: string, width: number): string
		local out = {}
		for index = 1, width do
			const ch = string.sub(value, index, index)
			if ch == "*" then
				for _ = index, width do
					out[#out + 1] = "?"
				end
				break
			elseif ch == "" then
				out[#out + 1] = " "
			else
				out[#out + 1] = ch
			end
		end
		return table.concat(out)
	end
	return field(base, 8) .. field(ext, 3)
end

local function matchesFcb(pattern: string, name: string): boolean
	if #pattern ~= 11 or #name ~= 11 then
		return false
	end
	for index = 1, 11 do
		const want = string.sub(pattern, index, index)
		if want ~= "?" and want ~= string.sub(name, index, index) then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

local function writeFixed(mem: any, address: number, text: string, width: number)
	for index = 1, width do
		mem:write8(address + index - 1, string.byte(text, index) or 0x20)
	end
end

local function writeFindEntry(
	self: Dos,
	machine: Host,
	entry: { name: string, size: number, dir: boolean },
	fcbMode: boolean
)
	const mem = machine.mem
	const dtaSeg = self.dtaSeg or self.currentPsp or machine.pspSeg or 0
	const dtaOff = self.dtaOff or 0x80
	const base = lshift(dtaSeg, 4) + dtaOff
	const baseName, ext = splitName(entry.name)
	const attr = entry.dir and 0x10 or 0x20
	if fcbMode then
		mem:write8(base, 0) -- default drive
		writeFixed(mem, base + 1, (baseName .. "        "):sub(1, 8), 8)
		writeFixed(mem, base + 9, (ext .. "   "):sub(1, 3), 3)
		mem:write8(base + 12, attr)
		for offset = 13, 22 do
			mem:write8(base + offset, 0)
		end
		mem:write16(base + 23, 0)
		mem:write16(base + 25, 0x21) -- 1980-01-01
		mem:write16(base + 27, 0)
		mem:write16(base + 29, entry.size % 65536)
		mem:write16(base + 31, math.floor(entry.size / 65536))
	else
		for offset = 0, 20 do
			mem:write8(base + offset, 0)
		end
		mem:write8(base + 21, attr)
		mem:write16(base + 22, 0) -- time
		mem:write16(base + 24, 0x21) -- 1980-01-01
		mem:write16(base + 26, entry.size % 65536) -- size low
		mem:write16(base + 28, math.floor(entry.size / 65536)) -- size high
		const display = if ext == "" then baseName else baseName .. "." .. ext
		mem:writeString(base + 30, display)
		mem:write8(base + 30 + #display, 0)
	end
end

local function matchesSearchAttr(entry: { dir: boolean }, mask: number): boolean
	if entry.dir then
		return band(mask, 0x10) ~= 0
	end
	-- The VFS has no volume labels. A volume-only search must not return a
	-- normal file; that is what WINFILE was displaying as its bogus [TXT] label.
	return not (band(mask, 0x08) ~= 0 and band(mask, 0x10) == 0)
end

local function beginFind(
	self: Dos,
	machine: Host,
	pattern: string,
	fcbMode: boolean,
	directory: string?,
	attrMask: number?
)
	if self.defaultDrive > 2 then
		self.find = { entries = {}, index = 0, fcbMode = fcbMode }
		return
	end
	const mask = attrMask or 0
	local entries = {}
	for _, entry in machine.vfs:list(directory or self.cwd) or {} do
		if matchesFcb(pattern, padded11(entry.name)) and matchesSearchAttr(entry, mask) then
			entries[#entries + 1] = entry
		end
	end
	self.find = { entries = entries, index = 0, fcbMode = fcbMode }
end

local function nextFind(self: Dos, machine: Host): boolean
	const find = self.find
	if not find then
		return false
	end
	find.index += 1
	const entry = find.entries[find.index]
	if not entry then
		return false
	end
	writeFindEntry(self, machine, entry, find.fcbMode)
	return true
end

Dos.FN[0x11] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- find first (FCB)
	const fcb = lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[3]
	-- DOS 4+ extended FCB: FF, 5 reserved, attribute, drive, then name/ext.
	-- MS-DOS Executive passes one of these, so the name starts at +8 and the
	-- search attribute at +6; a normal FCB keeps it at +0Ch.
	const extended = machine.mem:read8(fcb) == 0xFF
	const nameBase = if extended then fcb + 8 else fcb + 1
	const attr = machine.mem:read8(if extended then fcb + 6 else fcb + 0x0C)
	local pattern = {}
	for index = 0, 10 do
		pattern[index + 1] = string.char(machine.mem:read8(nameBase + index))
	end
	beginFind(self, machine, table.concat(pattern):gsub("%*", "?"), true, nil, attr)
	cpu:wb(0, if nextFind(self, machine) then 0 else 0xFF)
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x12] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- find next (FCB)
	cpu:wb(0, if nextFind(self, machine) then 0 else 0xFF)
	ok(cpu)
end

Dos.FN[0x36] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, _machine: Host) -- get free disk space
	local drive = band(cpu.r[3], 0xFF)
	if drive == 0 then
		drive = self.defaultDrive + 1
	end
	if drive < 1 or drive > 3 then
		fail(cpu, 0x0F)
		return
	end
	-- The machine has one fixed disk (C:). A: and B: have no media: real DOS
	-- answers AX=FFFFh (invalid drive). WSWAP/DSWAP pick the swap drive by free
	-- space, so reporting identical space for A: made them swap to A:\ and
	-- DSWAP then died with "path not found" (error 3) on A:\WINDOWS.
	if drive < 3 then
		setAX(cpu, 0xFFFF)
		return
	end
	setAX(cpu, 4) -- sectors per cluster
	cpu.r[4] = 0x7000 -- free clusters
	cpu.r[2] = 512 -- bytes per sector
	cpu.r[3] = 0x9000 -- total clusters
	ok(cpu)
end

-- AH=1B/1C: allocation information for the default/specified drive. Win 3.1
-- KRNL286 calls 1Ch during startup; DS:BX points at the FAT media-ID byte.
const MEDIA_ID_OFF = 0x01D1
local function allocationInfo(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host, drive: number)
	if drive == 0 then
		drive = self.defaultDrive + 1
	end
	if drive < 1 or drive > 3 then
		cpu:wb(0, 0xFF) -- AL = FFh: invalid drive
		return
	end
	machine.mem:write8(lshift(Dos.DATA_SEG, 4) + MEDIA_ID_OFF, 0xF8) -- fixed disk
	cpu:wb(0, 4) -- sectors per cluster
	cpu.r[2] = 512 -- CX = bytes per sector
	cpu.r[3] = 0x9000 -- DX = clusters on the drive
	cpu.r[4] = MEDIA_ID_OFF -- DS:BX -> media ID byte
	cpu.ds = Dos.DATA_SEG
end

Dos.FN[0x1B] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- allocation info, default drive
	allocationInfo(self, cpu, machine, 0)
end

Dos.FN[0x1C] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- allocation info, drive DL
	allocationInfo(self, cpu, machine, band(cpu.r[3], 0xFF))
end

Dos.FN[0x4E] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- find first (DTA)
	const raw = self:readRawAsciz(cpu)
	const matched = { string.match(raw, "^(.*)\\([^\\]*)$") }
	local directory = matched[1]
	const pattern = matched[2] or raw
	if directory == "" then
		directory = "C:\\"
	end
	beginFind(self, machine, fcbPattern(pattern), false, directory, band(cpu.r[2], 0xFF))
	if nextFind(self, machine) then
		setAX(cpu, 0)
		ok(cpu)
	else
		fail(cpu, 0x12)
	end
end

Dos.FN[0x4F] = function(self: Dos, cpu: any, machine: Host) -- find next (DTA)
	if nextFind(self, machine) then
		setAX(cpu, 0)
		ok(cpu)
	else
		fail(cpu, 0x12)
	end
end

return Dos

-- graphs_dfs: depth-first and breadth-first walks, cycle detection, topo order
local graph = {
  a = { "b", "c" },
  b = { "d" },
  c = { "d", "e" },
  d = { "f" },
  e = { "f" },
  f = {},
}
local function sortedNeighbours(node)
  local list = {}
  for i, v in ipairs(graph[node] or {}) do list[i] = v end
  table.sort(list)
  return list
end

local visited, order = {}, {}
local function dfs(node)
  if visited[node] then return end
  visited[node] = true
  order[#order + 1] = node
  for _, next in ipairs(sortedNeighbours(node)) do dfs(next) end
end
dfs("a")
print(table.concat(order, ""))
print(visited.f, visited.e)

local queue, seen, bfs = { "a" }, { a = true }, {}
local head = 1
while head <= #queue do
  local node = queue[head]
  head = head + 1
  bfs[#bfs + 1] = node
  for _, next in ipairs(sortedNeighbours(node)) do
    if not seen[next] then
      seen[next] = true
      queue[#queue + 1] = next
    end
  end
end
print(table.concat(bfs, ""))

-- topological order via post-order reversal
local post, mark = {}, {}
local function visit(node)
  if mark[node] == "done" then return end
  mark[node] = "open"
  for _, next in ipairs(sortedNeighbours(node)) do visit(next) end
  mark[node] = "done"
  post[#post + 1] = node
end
visit("a")
local topo = {}
for i = #post, 1, -1 do topo[#topo + 1] = post[i] end
print(table.concat(topo, ""))

local cyclic = { x = { "y" }, y = { "x" } }
local state, found = {}, false
local function detect(node)
  if state[node] == "open" then found = true return end
  if state[node] == "done" then return end
  state[node] = "open"
  for _, next in ipairs(cyclic[node] or {}) do detect(next) end
  state[node] = "done"
end
detect("x")
print("cycle", found)

--!strict
-- Executables.lua -- DOS .COM / .MZ loaders with PSP construction and relocations.

const band, bor, lshift, rshift = bit32.band, bit32.bor, bit32.lshift, bit32.rshift

const Executables = {}

export type Entry = {
	seg: number,
	off: number,
	movable: boolean?,
}

export type Module = {
	name: string?,
	segBases: { [number]: number },
	entries: { [number]: Entry },
	resident: { [string]: number },
	importedNames: { [number]: string },
	dgroup: number?,
	entrySeg: number,
	entryOff: number,
	ssIdx: number,
	sp: number,
}

type SegmentInfo = {
	sector: number,
	length: number,
	flags: number,
	minAlloc: number,
}

local function writeEnv(mem: any, envSeg: number, programPath: string?, parentEnvSeg: number?)
	const envBase = lshift(envSeg, 4)
	local position = 0
	if parentEnvSeg and parentEnvSeg ~= 0 then
		const src = lshift(parentEnvSeg, 4)
		local read = 0
		local write = 0
		while read < 0x3F0 do
			local chars: { string } = {}
			while read < 0x3F0 do
				const byte = mem:read8(src + read)
				read += 1
				if byte == 0 then
					break
				end
				chars[#chars + 1] = string.char(byte)
			end
			if #chars == 0 then
				break -- environment terminator
			end
			local entry = table.concat(chars)
			-- WIN.COM needs windir with a trailing separator to find KERNEL,
			-- but KERNEL's profile code appends its own separator. Children
			-- (KERNEL, USER, apps) must see the Windows directory without it,
			-- or every SYSTEM.INI path becomes C:\WINDOWS\\SYSTEM.INI and the
			-- profile lookup silently falls back to defaults (NETWORK.DRV).
			if
				string.sub(string.lower(entry), 1, 7) == "windir="
				and string.sub(entry, -1) == "\\"
			then
				entry = string.sub(entry, 1, -2)
			end
			mem:writeString(envBase + write, entry)
			write += #entry + 1
		end
		position = write
		if position == 0 then
			mem:write8(envBase, 0) -- empty environment still needs its terminator
			position = 1
		end
	else
		const envVars = {
			-- WIN.COM scans for lowercase "windir=" and appends "kernel.exe"
			-- / "system\kernel.exe" directly to the value, so it needs the slash
			"windir=C:\\WINDOWS\\",
			"WINDIR=C:\\WINDOWS\\",
			"PATH=C:\\WINDOWS;C:\\WINDOWS\\SYSTEM",
			"COMSPEC=C:\\WINDOWS\\COMMAND.COM",
		}
		for _, entry in envVars do
			mem:writeString(envBase + position, entry)
			position += #entry + 1
		end
		mem:write8(envBase + position, 0) -- extra NUL
	end
	-- DOS trailer: extra NUL, word count (1), then the program's full path.
	-- KERNEL reads the word after the double NUL and opens the path that follows.
	mem:write8(envBase + position, 0)
	mem:write16(envBase + position + 1, 1)
	mem:writeString(envBase + position + 3, programPath or "C:\\")
end

local function buildPSP(
	mem: any,
	pspSeg: number,
	programPath: string?,
	envSeg: number?,
	parentEnvSeg: number?
)
	const base = lshift(pspSeg, 4)
	mem:write16(base + 0, 0x20CD) -- INT 20h at PSP:0000 (so a bare RET terminates)
	mem:write8(base + 0x80, 0) -- empty command tail
	mem:write8(base + 0x81, 0x0D)

	-- environment block below the PSP (or a separately allocated block)
	const resolvedEnv = envSeg or (pspSeg - 0x40)
	writeEnv(mem, resolvedEnv, programPath, parentEnvSeg)
	mem:write16(base + 0x2C, resolvedEnv) -- PSP:2Ch -> environment segment

	-- terminate / ctrl-break / critical-error vectors (DOS fills these in):
	-- terminate points at the INT 20h at PSP:0000; the other two at IRET stubs
	mem:write16(base + 0x0A, 0x0000)
	mem:write16(base + 0x0C, pspSeg)
	mem:write16(base + 0x0E, 68) -- ctrl-break stub (F100:0044)
	mem:write16(base + 0x10, 0xF100)
	mem:write16(base + 0x12, 72) -- critical-error stub (F100:0048)
	mem:write16(base + 0x14, 0xF100)
end

function Executables.loadCOM(
	machine: any,
	bytes: buffer,
	pspSeg: number?,
	programPath: string?,
	envSeg: number?,
	parentEnvSeg: number?,
	stackParas: number?
): number
	const segment = pspSeg or 0x1000
	const mem = machine.mem
	buildPSP(mem, segment, programPath, envSeg, parentEnvSeg)
	mem:copyFrom(lshift(segment, 4) + 0x100, bytes)
	const cpu = machine.cpu
	cpu.cs, cpu.ds, cpu.es, cpu.ss = segment, segment, segment, segment
	cpu.ip = 0x100
	-- The stack must live inside the program's MCB block. Direct loads get the
	-- initial 0xFF-paragraph PSP block; EXEC COMs get their allocated block.
	const stackTop = math.min((stackParas or 0xFF) * 16 - 2, 0xFFFE)
	cpu.r[5] = stackTop
	machine.pspSeg = segment
	machine.terminated[segment] = nil -- a freshly loaded program is live again
	machine.exitCode = nil
	return segment
end

function Executables.loadMZ(
	machine: any,
	bytes: buffer,
	programPath: string?,
	pspSeg: number?,
	envSeg: number?,
	parentEnvSeg: number?,
	programParas: number?
): number
	const mem = machine.mem
	local function u8(off: number): number
		return buffer.readu8(bytes, off)
	end
	local function u16(off: number): number
		return bor(u8(off), lshift(u8(off + 1), 8))
	end

	if u8(0) ~= 0x4D or u8(1) ~= 0x5A then
		error("not an MZ executable (bad magic)")
	end
	const cblp = u16(2) -- bytes on last page
	const cp = u16(4) -- pages in file
	const crlc = u16(6) -- relocation count
	const cparhdr = u16(8) -- header size in paragraphs
	const ss = u16(0x0E)
	const sp = u16(0x10)
	const ip = u16(0x14)
	const cs = u16(0x16)
	const lfarlc = u16(0x18) -- relocation table offset

	-- cp/cblp describe the WHOLE FILE size; the load image excludes the header
	local fileLen = cp * 512
	if cblp > 0 then
		fileLen -= 512 - cblp
	end
	const headerLen = cparhdr * 16
	const imageLen = math.max(fileLen - headerLen, 0)

	const segment = pspSeg or 0x1000
	const imageParas = math.ceil(imageLen / 16)
	-- Standard DOS loads an MZ image at PSP+0x10. Bound NE (3.0a KERNEL/GDI)
	-- self-relocates and needs the image mapped at the top of its program
	-- block, but EXEPACK-packed real-mode images (3.1 DOSX) compute their own
	-- load segment as PSP+0x10 and reject anything else as corrupt.
	const neOff = if imageLen >= 0x40 then buffer.readu32(bytes, 0x3C) else 0
	const boundNE = neOff + 1 < buffer.len(bytes)
		and buffer.readu8(bytes, neOff) == 0x4E
		and buffer.readu8(bytes, neOff + 1) == 0x45
	const imageBase = if boundNE
			and programParas
			and programParas >= 0x10 + imageParas
		then segment + programParas - imageParas
		else segment + 0x10
	const loadSeg = imageBase

	buildPSP(mem, segment, programPath, envSeg, parentEnvSeg)
	const image = buffer.create(imageLen)
	buffer.copy(image, 0, bytes, headerLen, imageLen)
	mem:copyFrom(lshift(loadSeg, 4), image)

	-- apply relocations: word at (loadSeg + seg):off += loadSeg
	for index = 0, crlc - 1 do
		const off = u16(lfarlc + index * 4)
		const seg = u16(lfarlc + index * 4 + 2)
		const addr = lshift(loadSeg + seg, 4) + off
		mem:write16(addr, band(mem:read16(addr) + loadSeg, 0xFFFF))
	end

	const cpu = machine.cpu
	cpu.ds = segment
	cpu.es = segment
	cpu.ss = loadSeg + ss
	cpu.r[5] = sp
	cpu.cs = loadSeg + cs
	cpu.ip = ip
	machine.pspSeg = segment
	machine.terminated[segment] = nil -- a freshly loaded program is live again
	machine.exitCode = nil
	return segment
end

-- NE (Windows 1.x/2.x/3.x real-mode) loader -- REAL format, verified against
-- Windows 3.0a KERNEL/USER/GDI:
--   MZ at 0, e_lfanew (u32 @0x3C) -> NE header:
--   +04 enttab +06 cbenttab +0C flags +0E autodata +14 csip(dword: ip,cs)
--   +18 sssp(dword: sp,ss) +1C cseg +1E cmod +22 segtab +24 rsrctab
--   +26 restab +28 modtab +2A imptab +2C nrestab(dword) +30 cmovent
--   +32 align (sector = 1<<align)
--   Segment entries: [sector:2][len:2][flags:2][minAlloc:2]; flags 0x0100 =
--   relocation data follows the segment image (count word + 8-byte records:
--   [addrType:1][relocType:1][offset:2][target1:2][target2:2]).
--   Entry table bundles: [count:1][segIdx:1] then count entries:
--   fixed = [flags:1][off:2]; segIdx 0xFF = movable = [flags:1][skip:2][seg:1][off:2].

-- parse the entry table into ordinal -> { seg = 1-based seg index, off = offset }
local function parseEntryTable(
	u8: (off: number) -> number,
	neOff: number,
	enttab: number,
	cbenttab: number
): { [number]: Entry }
	const entries: { [number]: Entry } = {}
	local ordinal = 0
	local position = 0
	while position < cbenttab do
		const count = u8(neOff + enttab + position)
		if count == 0 then
			break
		end
		const segIndex = u8(neOff + enttab + position + 1)
		position += 2
		if segIndex == 0 then
			-- ordinal-space bundle: ordinals exist but have no entry data
			ordinal += count
		else
			for _ = 1, count do
				ordinal += 1
				if segIndex == 0xFF then
					-- movable: flags(1) + INT-3F hint(2) + seg(1) + off(2)
					const seg = u8(neOff + enttab + position + 3)
					const off = bor(
						u8(neOff + enttab + position + 4),
						lshift(u8(neOff + enttab + position + 5), 8)
					)
					entries[ordinal] = { seg = seg, off = off, movable = true }
					position += 6
				else
					const off = bor(
						u8(neOff + enttab + position + 1),
						lshift(u8(neOff + enttab + position + 2), 8)
					)
					entries[ordinal] = { seg = segIndex, off = off }
					position += 3
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return entries
end

-- A DOS EXEC of a Windows "bound" executable (MZ stub + NE image) maps the
-- whole file at loadSeg; the tiny MZ stub then jumps straight to the NE entry
-- with segments at their file offsets. Relocations are the loader's job
-- (WIN.COM does this in real Windows), so apply them in place here. All
-- fixups in KERNEL.EXE are internal; imports would need the thunk machinery.
function Executables.relocateBoundNE(
	machine: any,
	bytes: buffer,
	loadSeg: number,
	headerParas: number
): boolean
	const mem = machine.mem
	local function u8(off: number): number
		return buffer.readu8(bytes, off)
	end
	local function u16(off: number): number
		return bor(u8(off), lshift(u8(off + 1), 8))
	end
	local function u32(off: number): number
		return bor(u16(off), lshift(u16(off + 2), 16))
	end

	const neOff = u32(0x3C)
	if u8(neOff) ~= 0x4E or u8(neOff + 1) ~= 0x45 then
		return false
	end
	local function n16(off: number): number
		return u16(neOff + off)
	end

	const enttab, cbenttab = n16(4), n16(6)
	const cseg = n16(0x1C)
	const segtab = n16(0x22)
	const align = n16(0x32)
	const unit = lshift(1, align)
	const imageSeg = loadSeg - headerParas

	const segBases: { [number]: number } = {}
	for index = 1, cseg do
		const entry = segtab + (index - 1) * 8
		segBases[index] = imageSeg + math.floor(n16(entry) * unit / 16)
	end
	const entries = parseEntryTable(u8, neOff, enttab, cbenttab)

	for index = 1, cseg do
		const entry = segtab + (index - 1) * 8
		const sector, length, segFlags = n16(entry), n16(entry + 2), n16(entry + 4)
		if length > 0 and band(segFlags, 0x0100) ~= 0 then
			const relocOff = sector * unit + length
			const count = u16(relocOff)
			for r = 0, count - 1 do
				const record = relocOff + 2 + r * 8
				const addrType = band(u8(record), 0x7F)
				const relocType = u8(record + 1)
				const fixOff = u16(record + 2)
				const target1 = u16(record + 4)
				const target2 = u16(record + 6)
				const rtype = band(relocType, 3)
				local tgtSeg: number, tgtOff: number
				if rtype == 0 then
					if band(target1, 0xFF) == 0xFF then
						const target = entries[target2]
						if not target then
							error(("bound NE fixup: entry %d unresolvable"):format(target2))
						end
						tgtSeg, tgtOff = segBases[target.seg], target.off
					else
						tgtSeg, tgtOff = segBases[target1], target2
					end
				elseif rtype == 1 or rtype == 2 then
					error("bound NE fixup: imports unsupported in a bound image")
				end -- rtype 3: OSFIXUP, skip
				if rtype ~= 3 then
					const addr = lshift(segBases[index], 4) + fixOff
					local chain = mem:read16(addr)
					if addrType == 2 then
						mem:write16(addr, tgtSeg)
					elseif addrType == 3 or addrType == 11 then
						mem:write16(addr, tgtOff)
						mem:write16(addr + 2, tgtSeg)
					else
						error(("bound NE fixup: unsupported address type %d"):format(addrType))
					end
					local guard = 0
					while chain ~= 0xFFFF and chain ~= fixOff and guard < 1000 do
						guard += 1
						const caddr = lshift(segBases[index], 4) + chain
						const follow = mem:read16(caddr)
						if addrType == 2 then
							mem:write16(caddr, tgtSeg)
						else
							mem:write16(caddr, tgtOff)
							mem:write16(caddr + 2, tgtSeg)
						end
						chain = follow
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- load one NE image (executable or DLL): segments + fixups + module registry.
-- Registers itself on machine.winImages when named.
function Executables.loadNEImage(machine: any, bytes: buffer, moduleName: string?): Module
	const mem = machine.mem
	local function u8(off: number): number
		return buffer.readu8(bytes, off)
	end
	local function u16(off: number): number
		return bor(u8(off), lshift(u8(off + 1), 8))
	end
	local function u32(off: number): number
		return bor(u16(off), lshift(u16(off + 2), 16))
	end

	if u8(0) ~= 0x4D or u8(1) ~= 0x5A then
		error("not an MZ executable (bad magic)")
	end
	const neOff = u32(0x3C)
	if u8(neOff) ~= 0x4E or u8(neOff + 1) ~= 0x45 then
		error("NE magic not found at e_lfanew")
	end
	local function n8(off: number): number
		return u8(neOff + off)
	end
	local function n16(off: number): number
		return u16(neOff + off)
	end

	const enttab, cbenttab = n16(4), n16(6)
	const flags = n16(0x0C)
	const autodata = n16(0x0E)
	const csip = u32(neOff + 0x14)
	const sssp = u32(neOff + 0x18)
	const cseg = n16(0x1C)
	const cmod = n16(0x1E)
	const segtab = n16(0x22)
	const restab = n16(0x26)
	const modtab = n16(0x28)
	const imptab = n16(0x2A)
	const align = n16(0x32)
	const unit = lshift(1, align)

	if band(flags, 0x0800) ~= 0 then
		error("NE self-loading modules are not supported")
	end

	const entries = parseEntryTable(u8, neOff, enttab, cbenttab)

	-- resident names: [len:1][name][ordinal:2]
	const resident: { [string]: number } = {}
	if restab > 0 then
		local position = restab
		while true do
			const length = n8(position)
			if length == 0 then
				break
			end
			local name = ""
			for index = 1, length do
				name ..= string.char(n8(position + index))
			end
			resident[string.upper(name)] = n16(position + length + 1)
			position = position + length + 3
		end
	end
	-- non-resident names: the table starts with a length-prefixed module
	-- description (skip it), then [len:1][name][ordinal:2] entries. Its offset
	-- at +2Ch is an absolute file offset, unlike the resident table.
	const nonResidentLength = n16(0x20)
	const nonResidentOffset = bor(n16(0x2C), lshift(n16(0x2E), 16))
	if nonResidentLength > 0 and nonResidentOffset > 0 then
		local position = nonResidentOffset
		const limit = nonResidentOffset + nonResidentLength
		const descriptionLength = u8(position)
		if descriptionLength > 0 then
			position += descriptionLength + 1
			while position < limit and u8(position) == 0 do
				position += 1
			end
		end
		while position < limit do
			const length = u8(position)
			if length == 0 then
				break
			end
			local name = ""
			for index = 1, length do
				name ..= string.char(u8(position + index))
			end
			resident[string.upper(name)] = u16(position + length + 1)
			position = position + length + 3
		end
	end

	-- imported names: module ref table words index into length-prefixed names
	const importedNames: { [number]: string } = {}
	if modtab > 0 and imptab > 0 then
		for index = 0, cmod - 1 do
			const entry = imptab + n16(modtab + index * 2)
			const length = n8(entry)
			local name = ""
			for j = 1, length do
				name ..= string.char(n8(entry + j))
			end
			importedNames[index + 1] = name
		end
	end

	-- pass 1: load all segment images into one arena block (fixups come in
	-- pass 2, after every segBase exists -- segment 1's fixups routinely
	-- reference segment 2+)
	const segBases: { [number]: number } = {}
	const segInfo: { [number]: SegmentInfo } = {}
	local totalParas = 0
	for index = 1, cseg do
		const entry = segtab + (index - 1) * 8
		const length = n16(entry + 2)
		const minAlloc = n16(entry + 6)
		totalParas += math.max(math.ceil(math.max(length, minAlloc) / 16), 1)
	end
	local current = machine:dosAlloc(totalParas + 1)
	if not current then
		error("NE load: out of conventional memory for module")
	end
	for index = 1, cseg do
		const entry = segtab + (index - 1) * 8
		const sector = n16(entry)
		const length = n16(entry + 2)
		const segFlags = n16(entry + 4)
		const minAlloc = n16(entry + 6)
		segInfo[index] = { sector = sector, length = length, flags = segFlags, minAlloc = minAlloc }
		segBases[index] = current
		if length > 0 then
			const image = buffer.create(length)
			buffer.copy(image, 0, bytes, sector * unit, length)
			mem:copyFrom(lshift(current, 4), image)
		end
		if band(segFlags, 0x0008) ~= 0 then
			-- iterated segment: repeated [repeat:2][len:2][data] blocks
			const fileOff = sector * unit
			const expanded = buffer.create(math.max(length, minAlloc, 16))
			local src, dst = 0, 0
			while src < length do
				const repeatCount = bor(u8(fileOff + src), lshift(u8(fileOff + src + 1), 8))
				const blockLen = bor(u8(fileOff + src + 2), lshift(u8(fileOff + src + 3), 8))
				src += 4
				for _ = 1, repeatCount do
					buffer.copy(expanded, dst, bytes, fileOff + src, blockLen)
					dst += blockLen
				end
				src += blockLen
			end
			mem:copyFrom(lshift(current, 4), expanded)
		end
		current += math.max(math.ceil(math.max(length, minAlloc) / 16), 1)
	end

	-- pass 2: relocations
	for index = 1, cseg do
		const info = segInfo[index]
		const length = info.length
		if length > 0 and band(info.flags, 0x0100) ~= 0 then
			const cur = segBases[index]
			const relocOff = info.sector * unit + length
			const count = u16(relocOff)
			for r = 0, count - 1 do
				const record = relocOff + 2 + r * 8
				const addrType = band(u8(record), 0x7F)
				const relocType = u8(record + 1)
				const fixOff = u16(record + 2)
				const target1 = u16(record + 4)
				const target2 = u16(record + 6)

				local tgtSeg: number, tgtOff: number
				const rtype = band(relocType, 3)
				if rtype ~= 3 then
					if rtype == 0 then -- internal
						if band(target1, 0xFF) == 0xFF then
							const target = entries[target2]
							if not target or not segBases[target.seg] then
								error(("NE fixup: own entry %d unresolvable"):format(target2))
							end
							tgtSeg, tgtOff = segBases[target.seg], target.off
						else
							tgtSeg, tgtOff = segBases[target1], target2
						end
					elseif rtype == 1 then -- import by ordinal
						const module = importedNames[target1]
						if not module then
							error(("NE fixup: import module %d missing"):format(target1))
						end
						tgtSeg, tgtOff = machine:resolveWinImport(module, target2)
					elseif rtype == 2 then -- import by name
						const nameOff = imptab + target2
						const nameLen = n8(nameOff)
						local name = ""
						for j = 1, nameLen do
							name ..= string.char(n8(nameOff + j))
						end
						const module = importedNames[target1]
						if not module then
							error(("NE fixup: import module %d missing"):format(target1))
						end
						tgtSeg, tgtOff = machine:resolveWinImportByName(module, name)
					end
					-- OSFIXUP (3): floating point, skip

					const addr = lshift(cur, 4) + fixOff
					const additive = band(relocType, 0x04) ~= 0
					if additive then
						if addrType == 0 then
							mem:write8(addr, band(mem:read8(addr) + tgtOff, 0xFF))
						else
							mem:write16(addr, band(mem:read16(addr) + tgtOff, 0xFFFF))
							if addrType == 3 or addrType == 11 then
								mem:write16(addr + 2, band(mem:read16(addr + 2) + tgtSeg, 0xFFFF))
							end
						end
					else
						-- chained: the word at the fixup location links to the next one
						local chain = mem:read16(addr)
						if addrType == 0 then
							mem:write8(addr, band(tgtOff, 0xFF))
						elseif addrType == 2 then
							mem:write16(addr, tgtSeg)
						elseif addrType == 3 or addrType == 11 then
							mem:write16(addr, tgtOff)
							mem:write16(addr + 2, tgtSeg)
						elseif addrType == 5 then
							mem:write16(addr, tgtOff)
						else
							error(("unsupported NE relocation address type %d"):format(addrType))
						end
						local guard = 0
						while chain ~= 0xFFFF and chain ~= fixOff and guard < 1000 do
							guard += 1
							const caddr = lshift(cur, 4) + chain
							const follow = mem:read16(caddr)
							if addrType == 0 then
								mem:write8(caddr, band(tgtOff, 0xFF))
							elseif addrType == 2 then
								mem:write16(caddr, tgtSeg)
							elseif addrType == 3 or addrType == 11 then
								mem:write16(caddr, tgtOff)
								mem:write16(caddr + 2, tgtSeg)
							elseif addrType == 5 then
								mem:write16(caddr, tgtOff)
							end
							if follow == chain then
								break
							end
							chain = follow
						end
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local selfName = moduleName
	if restab > 0 then
		const length = n8(restab)
		if length > 0 then
			local name = ""
			for index = 1, length do
				name ..= string.char(n8(restab + index))
			end
			selfName = name
		end
	end

	const module: Module = {
		name = moduleName,
		segBases = segBases,
		entries = entries,
		resident = resident,
		importedNames = importedNames,
		dgroup = (autodata > 0) and segBases[autodata] or nil,
		entrySeg = band(rshift(csip, 16), 0xFFFF),
		entryOff = band(csip, 0xFFFF),
		ssIdx = band(rshift(sssp, 16), 0xFFFF),
		sp = band(sssp, 0xFFFF),
	}
	if selfName then
		machine.winImages[string.upper(selfName)] = module
	end
	return module
end

-- executable wrapper: PSP + CPU entry state; DS/ES = DGROUP (Windows convention)
function Executables.loadNE(machine: any, bytes: buffer): number
	const module = Executables.loadNEImage(machine, bytes, nil)
	const mem = machine.mem
	const pspSeg = 0x1000
	machine.pspSeg = pspSeg
	machine.terminated[pspSeg] = nil
	buildPSP(mem, pspSeg)

	const cpu = machine.cpu
	cpu.ds = module.dgroup or pspSeg
	cpu.es = module.dgroup or pspSeg
	if module.entrySeg > 0 then
		cpu.cs = module.segBases[module.entrySeg]
		cpu.ip = module.entryOff
	else
		cpu.cs, cpu.ip = pspSeg, 0x100
	end
	if module.ssIdx > 0 then
		cpu.ss = module.segBases[module.ssIdx]
		cpu.r[5] = module.sp
	else
		cpu.ss = pspSeg
		cpu.r[5] = 0xFFFE
	end
	machine.exitCode = nil
	return pspSeg
end

return Executables

-- Machine.lua -- wires memory + cpu + bios + dos + vfs; run(maxSteps) slices.

const band, bnot, bor, rshift, lshift =
	bit32.band, bit32.bnot, bit32.bor, bit32.rshift, bit32.lshift

const Machine = {}
Machine.__index = Machine

const PIT_HZ = 1_193_182

export type MemBlock = {
	start: number,
	size: number,
	owner: number,
}

export type WinFn = {
	fn: (machine: Machine, cpu: any) -> (),
	args: number,
	fnId: number?,
}

export type WinModule = {
	[number]: WinFn,
}

export type WinEntry = {
	seg: number,
	off: number,
	movable: boolean?,
}

export type WinImage = {
	segBases: { [number]: number },
	entries: { [number]: WinEntry },
	resident: { [string]: number },
	dgroup: number?,
	entrySeg: number,
	entryOff: number,
	ssIdx: number,
	sp: number,
}

export type Deps = {
	Memory: any,

export type Config = {

export type Machine = {
	deps: Deps,
	config: Config,
	mem: any,
	cpu: any,
	xms: any,
	vfs: any,

	bios: any,
	dos: any,

	waiting: string?,

	nextFnId: number,
	thunkSeg: number,

	timerStubSeg: number,
	timerStubOff: number,
	picInService: number,
	picMask: number,
	mouseX: number,
	mouseY: number,
	mouseButtons: number,
	mouseVisible: boolean,
	mouseMinX: number,
	mouseMaxX: number,
	mouseMinY: number,
	mouseMaxY: number,

	mouseDeltaY: number,
	mouseMickeyX: number,
	mouseMickeyY: number,
	mouseCountX: number,
	mouseCountY: number,
	mouseHandler: { seg: number, off: number }?,
	mouseDeviceHandler: { seg: number, off: number }?,
	mousePs2Enabled: boolean,
	mouseSampleRate: number,

	mouseScaling: number,
	mousePacketSize: number,

	mouseIrqActive: boolean,

	mouseConfigSeg: number,
	mouseConfigOff: number,
	mouseCleanupSeg: number,
	mouseCleanupOff: number,
	mouseIrqStubSeg: number,
	mouseIrqStubOff: number,
	keyboardQueue: { number },
	keyboardData: number?,
	keyboardOutputFull: boolean,
	keyboardPending: boolean,
	keyboardEnabled: boolean,
	shiftHeld: boolean,
	keyboardIrqActive: boolean,

	speakerEnabled: boolean,

	run: (self: Machine, maxSteps: number?) -> number,
	exit: (self: Machine, code: number) -> (),
	logChar: (self: Machine, ch: number) -> (),
	logString: (self: Machine, message: string) -> (),

	pushKeys: (self: Machine, keys: string) -> (),
	bridgeDosKey: (self: Machine, scan: number) -> (),

	setMouse: (self: Machine, x: number, y: number, buttons: number) -> (),
