const FONT_BYTES = table.concat(FONT_HEX, "")

local function decodeFont(): { [number]: { number } }
	local glyphs: { [number]: { number } } = {}
	for code = 32, 126 do
		const rows = table.create(8, 0) :: { number }
		const base = (code - 32) * 16 + 1
		for row = 0, 7 do
			const first = base + row * 2
			rows[row] = tonumber(string.sub(FONT_BYTES, first, first + 1), 16) or 0
		end
		glyphs[code] = rows
	end
	return glyphs
end

const FONT = decodeFont()

local function dac6To8(value: number): number
	const component = band(value, 0x3F)
	return bor(lshift(component, 2), rshift(component, 4))
end

local function rgbaWord(r: number, g: number, b: number): number
	return bor(bor(bor(r, lshift(g, 8)), lshift(b, 16)), 0xFF000000)
end

local function apertureOffset(addr: number): number
	if addr >= APERTURE_BASE then
		return band(addr - APERTURE_BASE, 0xFFFF)
	end
	return band(addr, 0xFFFF)
end

local function rotateRight(value: number, count: number): number
	if count == 0 then
		return band(value, 0xFF)
	end
	return band(bor(rshift(value, count), lshift(value, 8 - count)), 0xFF)
end

local function applyDataFunction(data: number, latch: number, fn: number): number
	if fn == 1 then
		return band(data, latch)
	elseif fn == 2 then
		return bor(data, latch)
	elseif fn == 3 then
		return bxor(data, latch)
	end
	return data
end

const Vga = {}
Vga.__index = Vga

Vga.APERTURE_BASE = APERTURE_BASE
Vga.APERTURE_SIZE = APERTURE_SIZE
Vga.PLANE_SIZE = PLANE_SIZE

-- Cheap routing predicate for a future Memory/CPU aperture hook.
function Vga.containsAddress(addr: number): boolean
	const physical = band(addr, 0xFFFFF)
	return physical >= APERTURE_BASE and physical < APERTURE_BASE + APERTURE_SIZE
end

export type Vga = typeof(setmetatable(
	{} :: {
		mem: Memory,
		modeNumber: number,
		info: ModeInfo,
		crtc: { number },
		crtcIndex: number,
		crtcProtected: boolean,
		seq: { number },
		seqIndex: number,
		gfx: { number },
		gfxIndex: number,
		attr: { number },
		attrIndex: number,
		attrFlipFlop: boolean,
		attrPas: boolean,
		misc: number,
		feature: number,
		dac: buffer,
		dacWriteIndex: number,
		dacReadIndex: number,
		dacWriteComponent: number,
		dacReadComponent: number,
		dacMask: number,
		planes: { buffer },
		chain4: buffer,
		latches: { number },
		rgba: buffer,
		widthPx: number,
		heightPx: number,
		dirty: boolean,
		dirtyX0: number,
		dirtyY0: number,
		dirtyX1: number,
		dirtyY1: number,
		statusPhase: boolean,
		paletteDirty: boolean,
		paletteRGBA: { number },
		color16RGBA: { number },
		latched: { [number]: number },
	},
	Vga
))

function Vga.new(mem: Memory): Vga
	const self = setmetatable({}, Vga) :: any
	self.mem = mem
	self.modeNumber = 0x03
	self.info = MODES[0x03] :: ModeInfo
	self.crtc = table.create(25, 0) :: { number }
	self.crtcIndex = 0
	self.crtcProtected = false
	self.seq = table.create(5, 0) :: { number }
	self.seqIndex = 0
	self.gfx = table.create(9, 0) :: { number }
	self.gfxIndex = 0
	self.attr = table.create(21, 0) :: { number }
	self.attrIndex = 0
	self.attrFlipFlop = true
	self.attrPas = true
	self.misc = 0
	self.feature = 0
	self.dac = buffer.create(256 * 3)
	self.dacWriteIndex = 0
	self.dacReadIndex = 0
	self.dacWriteComponent = 0
	self.dacReadComponent = 0
	self.dacMask = 0xFF
	self.planes = {
		buffer.create(PLANE_SIZE),
		buffer.create(PLANE_SIZE),
		buffer.create(PLANE_SIZE),
		buffer.create(PLANE_SIZE),
	}
	self.chain4 = buffer.create(PLANE_SIZE)
	self.latches = table.create(4, 0) :: { number }
	self.rgba = buffer.create(1) -- replaced by setMode
	self.widthPx = 640
	self.heightPx = 480
	self.dirty = false
	self.dirtyX0 = 0
	self.dirtyY0 = 0
	self.dirtyX1 = 0
	self.dirtyY1 = 0
	self.statusPhase = false
	self.paletteDirty = true
	self.paletteRGBA = table.create(256, 0) :: { number }
	self.color16RGBA = table.create(16, 0) :: { number }
	self.latched = {}
	self:resetPalette()
	self:setMode(0x03)
	return self
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- mode state

function Vga.mode(self: Vga): number
	return self.modeNumber
end

function Vga.modeInfo(self: Vga): ModeInfo
	return self.info
end

function Vga.width(self: Vga): number
	return self.widthPx
end

function Vga.height(self: Vga): number
	return self.heightPx
end

function Vga.stride(self: Vga): number
	return self.widthPx * 4
end

function Vga.isTextMode(self: Vga): boolean
	return self.info.kind == "text"
end

function Vga.isChain4(self: Vga): boolean
	return band(self.seq[4], 0x08) ~= 0
end

function Vga.isOddEven(self: Vga): boolean
	return not self:isChain4() and band(self.seq[4], 0x04) == 0
end

function Vga.isBlanked(self: Vga): boolean
	return not self.attrPas or band(self.seq[1], 0x20) ~= 0 or band(self.misc, 0x02) == 0
end

function Vga.readCrtc(self: Vga, index: number): number
	return band(self.crtc[band(index, 0x1F)] or 0, 0xFF)
end

function Vga.readSeq(self: Vga, index: number): number
	return band(self.seq[band(index, 0x07)] or 0, 0xFF)
end

function Vga.readGfx(self: Vga, index: number): number
	return band(self.gfx[band(index, 0x0F)] or 0, 0xFF)
end

function Vga.readAttr(self: Vga, index: number): number
	return band(self.attr[band(index, 0x1F)] or 0, 0xFF)
end

function Vga.readDac(self: Vga, index: number): (number, number, number)
	const base = band(index, 0xFF) * 3
	return buffer.readu8(self.dac, base),
		buffer.readu8(self.dac, base + 1),
		buffer.readu8(self.dac, base + 2)
end

function Vga.setMode(self: Vga, mode: number): boolean
	const key = band(mode, 0xFF)
	const info = MODES[key]
	const registers = MODE_REGISTERS[key]
	if info == nil or registers == nil then
		return false
	end

	self.modeNumber = key
	self.info = info
	self.crtcProtected = false
	for index = 0, 24 do
		self.crtc[index] = registers.crtc[index + 1] or 0
	end
	for index = 0, 4 do
		self.seq[index] = registers.seq[index + 1] or 0
	end
	for index = 0, 8 do
		self.gfx[index] = registers.gfx[index + 1] or 0
	end
	for index = 0, 20 do
		self.attr[index] = registers.attr[index + 1] or 0
	end

	self.misc = registers.misc
	self.feature = 0
	self.crtcIndex = 0
	self.seqIndex = 0
	self.gfxIndex = 0
	self.attrIndex = 0
	self.attrFlipFlop = true
	self.attrPas = true
	self.dacWriteIndex = 0
	self.dacReadIndex = 0
	self.dacWriteComponent = 0
	self.dacReadComponent = 0
	self.dacMask = 0xFF
	self.statusPhase = false
	self.crtcProtected = band(self.crtc[0x11], 0x80) ~= 0

	for plane = 0, 3 do
		self.latches[plane] = 0
		buffer.fill(self.planes[plane + 1], 0, 0, PLANE_SIZE)
	end
	buffer.fill(self.chain4, 0, 0, PLANE_SIZE)

	self.widthPx = info.width
	self.heightPx = info.height
	self.rgba = buffer.create(info.width * info.height * 4)
	self:resetPalette()
	self:markAllDirty()
	return true
end

-- ------------------------------------------------------------------ palette

local function writeDacEntry(dac: buffer, index: number, red: number, green: number, blue: number)
	const base = index * 3
	buffer.writeu8(dac, base, band(red, 0x3F))
	buffer.writeu8(dac, base + 1, band(green, 0x3F))
	buffer.writeu8(dac, base + 2, band(blue, 0x3F))
end

-- BIOS mode 3/12h palette: the first 64 DAC entries are the EGA gamut. Text
-- mode maps attributes 8..15 to 0x38..0x3F and brown to 0x14, so those entries
-- must be populated even though mode 12h only uses 0x00..0x0F.
function Vga.loadEgaPalette(self: Vga)
	for index = 0, 255 do
		writeDacEntry(self.dac, index, 0, 0, 0)
	end
	for index = 0, 63 do
		if index == 0x14 then
			writeDacEntry(self.dac, index, 42, 21, 0)
		elseif index >= 0x38 then
			const rgb = EGA_RGB[index - 0x38 + 9]
			writeDacEntry(self.dac, index, rgb[1], rgb[2], rgb[3])
		else
			const rgb = EGA_RGB[index % 16 + 1]
			writeDacEntry(self.dac, index, rgb[1], rgb[2], rgb[3])
		end
	end
	self.paletteDirty = true
end

-- Mode 13h/8bpp default: EGA 0..15, 16 grey levels, a 6x6x6 colour cube,
-- then eight black entries (the BIOS 256-colour table).
function Vga.loadVga256Palette(self: Vga)
	for index = 0, 255 do
		if index < 16 then
			const rgb = EGA_RGB[index + 1]
			writeDacEntry(self.dac, index, rgb[1], rgb[2], rgb[3])
		elseif index < 32 then
			const grey = math.floor((index - 16) * 63 / 15 + 0.5)
			writeDacEntry(self.dac, index, grey, grey, grey)
		elseif index < 248 then
			const cube = index - 32
			const red = CUBE_LEVELS[math.floor(cube / 36) + 1]
			const green = CUBE_LEVELS[math.floor(cube / 6) % 6 + 1]
			const blue = CUBE_LEVELS[cube % 6 + 1]
			writeDacEntry(self.dac, index, red, green, blue)
		else
			writeDacEntry(self.dac, index, 0, 0, 0)
		end
	end
	self.paletteDirty = true
end

function Vga.resetPalette(self: Vga)
	if self.info.kind == "linear" then
		self:loadVga256Palette()
	else
		self:loadEgaPalette()
	end
end

function Vga.ensurePalette(self: Vga)
	if not self.paletteDirty then
		return
	end
	for index = 0, 255 do
		const base = index * 3
		const red = dac6To8(buffer.readu8(self.dac, base))
		const green = dac6To8(buffer.readu8(self.dac, base + 1))
		const blue = dac6To8(buffer.readu8(self.dac, base + 2))
		self.paletteRGBA[index + 1] = rgbaWord(red, green, blue)
	end
	for index = 0, 15 do
		const dacIndex = band(band(self.attr[index], 0x3F), self.dacMask)
		self.color16RGBA[index + 1] = self.paletteRGBA[dacIndex + 1]
	end
	self.paletteDirty = false
end

-- 8-bit RGB for a DAC index (the snapshot path uses the same expansion).
function Vga.paletteColor(self: Vga, index: number): (number, number, number)
	const red, green, blue = self:readDac(band(index, self.dacMask))
	return dac6To8(red), dac6To8(green), dac6To8(blue)
end

-- --------------------------------------------------------------- dirty rects

function Vga.markAllDirty(self: Vga)
	self.dirty = true
	self.dirtyX0 = 0
	self.dirtyY0 = 0
	self.dirtyX1 = self.widthPx
	self.dirtyY1 = self.heightPx
end

function Vga.markDirtyRect(self: Vga, x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number)
	if width <= 0 or height <= 0 then
		return
	end
	const x0 = math.max(0, math.floor(x))
	const y0 = math.max(0, math.floor(y))
	const x1 = math.min(self.widthPx, math.floor(x + width))
	const y1 = math.min(self.heightPx, math.floor(y + height))
	if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0 then
		return
	end
	if not self.dirty then
		self.dirty = true
		self.dirtyX0 = x0
		self.dirtyY0 = y0
		self.dirtyX1 = x1
		self.dirtyY1 = y1
		return
	end
	self.dirtyX0 = math.min(self.dirtyX0, x0)
	self.dirtyY0 = math.min(self.dirtyY0, y0)
	self.dirtyX1 = math.max(self.dirtyX1, x1)
	self.dirtyY1 = math.max(self.dirtyY1, y1)
end

function Vga.dirtyRect(self: Vga): DirtyRect?
	if not self.dirty then
		return nil
	end
	return {
		x = self.dirtyX0,
		y = self.dirtyY0,
		width = self.dirtyX1 - self.dirtyX0,
		height = self.dirtyY1 - self.dirtyY0,
	}
end

function Vga.consumeDirty(self: Vga): DirtyRect?
	const rect = self:dirtyRect()
	self.dirty = false
	return rect
end

function Vga.clearDirty(self: Vga)
	self.dirty = false
end

-- ------------------------------------------------------------ memory aperture

function Vga.displayStartBytes(self: Vga): number
	const words = bor(lshift(band(self.crtc[0x0C], 0xFF), 8), band(self.crtc[0x0D], 0xFF))
	return band(lshift(words, 1), 0xFFFF)
end

function Vga.planarRowBytes(self: Vga): number
	const offset = band(self.crtc[0x13], 0xFF) * 2
	if offset > 0 then
		return offset
	end
	return math.max(1, math.ceil(self.widthPx / 8))
end

function Vga.loadLatches(self: Vga, offset: number)
	for plane = 0, 3 do
		self.latches[plane] = buffer.readu8(self.planes[plane + 1], band(offset, 0xFFFF))
	end
end

function Vga.read8(self: Vga, addr: number): number
	if band(self.misc, 0x02) == 0 then
		return 0xFF
	end
	const offset = apertureOffset(addr)
	if self.info.kind == "linear" or self:isChain4() then
		return buffer.readu8(self.chain4, band(offset, 0xFFFF))
	end

	self:loadLatches(offset)

	-- Graphics Controller mode bit 3 selects colour-compare reads.
	if band(rshift(self.gfx[5], 3), 0x01) == 1 then
		const compare = band(self.gfx[2], 0x0F)
		const ignore = band(self.gfx[7], 0x0F)
		local value = 0
		for bit = 7, 0, -1 do
			const index = bor(
				band(rshift(self.latches[0], bit), 0x01),
				bor(
					lshift(band(rshift(self.latches[1], bit), 0x01), 1),
					bor(
						lshift(band(rshift(self.latches[2], bit), 0x01), 2),
						lshift(band(rshift(self.latches[3], bit), 0x01), 3)
					)
				)
			)
			if band(bxor(index, compare), band(bnot(ignore), 0x0F)) == 0 then
				value = bor(value, lshift(1, bit))
			end
		end
		return value
	end

	const plane = band(self.gfx[4], 0x03)
	return buffer.readu8(self.planes[plane + 1], band(offset, 0xFFFF))
end

function Vga.write8(self: Vga, addr: number, value: number)
	if band(self.misc, 0x02) == 0 then
		return
	end
	const offset = apertureOffset(addr)
	if self.info.kind == "linear" or self:isChain4() then
		buffer.writeu8(self.chain4, band(offset, 0xFFFF), band(value, 0xFF))
		self:markApertureDirty(offset)
		return
	end

	const data = band(value, 0xFF)
	const mode = band(self.gfx[5], 0x03)
	const mapMask = band(self.seq[2], 0x0F)
	const bitMask = band(self.gfx[8], 0xFF)

	const fn = band(rshift(self.gfx[3], 3), 0x03)
	const rotated = rotateRight(data, band(self.gfx[3], 0x07))
	for plane = 0, 3 do
		if band(mapMask, lshift(1, plane)) ~= 0 then
			const latch = self.latches[plane]
			local written: number
			if mode == 1 then
				-- Write mode 1: copy the latches; CPU data is ignored.
				written = latch
			else
				-- Modes 0/2/3 all feed a per-plane source byte through the
				-- ALU (function select) against the latch, then merge it
				-- with the latch under the bit mask.
				local source: number
				local mask = bitMask
				if mode == 2 then
					-- Write mode 2: one data bit expands to a full plane byte.
					source = band(data, lshift(1, plane)) ~= 0 and 0xFF or 0x00
				elseif mode == 3 then
					-- Write mode 3: set/reset (enable ignored) is the source;
					-- the rotated CPU data ANDed with the bit mask is the mask.
					source = band(self.gfx[0], lshift(1, plane)) ~= 0 and 0xFF or 0x00
					mask = band(rotated, bitMask)
				elseif band(self.gfx[1], lshift(1, plane)) ~= 0 then
					-- Write mode 0 with enable set/reset: the set/reset bit
					-- replaces CPU data (the ALU still applies afterwards).
					source = band(self.gfx[0], lshift(1, plane)) ~= 0 and 0xFF or 0x00
				else
					source = rotated
				end
				const result = applyDataFunction(source, latch, fn)
				written = bor(band(result, mask), band(latch, band(bnot(mask), 0xFF)))
			end
			buffer.writeu8(self.planes[plane + 1], band(offset, 0xFFFF), band(written, 0xFF))
		end
	end
	self:markApertureDirty(offset)
end

function Vga.read16(self: Vga, addr: number): number
	return bor(self:read8(addr), lshift(self:read8(addr + 1), 8))
end

function Vga.write16(self: Vga, addr: number, value: number)
	self:write8(addr, band(value, 0xFF))
	self:write8(addr + 1, band(rshift(value, 8), 0xFF))
end

function Vga.markApertureDirty(self: Vga, offset: number)
	const start = self:displayStartBytes()
	if offset < start then
		self:markAllDirty()
		return
	end
	const relative = offset - start
	if self.info.kind == "linear" or self:isChain4() then
		const x = relative % self.widthPx
		const y = math.floor(relative / self.widthPx)
		self:markDirtyRect(x, y, 1, 1)
		return
	end
	const rowBytes = self:planarRowBytes()
	const byteX = relative % rowBytes
	const y = math.floor(relative / rowBytes)
	self:markDirtyRect(byteX * 8, y, 8, 1)
end

-- Notify the device that a direct write to the aperture already happened (for
-- example a test writing planes, or a future Memory fast path). Normal guest
-- writes must go through vga:write8 so the write-mode logic runs.
function Vga.noteWrite(self: Vga, addr: number, length: number)
	if length <= 0 then
		return
	end
	const start = self:displayStartBytes()
	const first = apertureOffset(addr)
	if first < start then
		self:markAllDirty()
		return
	end
	const relativeFirst = first - start
	const relativeLast = relativeFirst + length - 1
	if relativeLast > 0xFFFF then
		self:markAllDirty()
		return
	end

	if self.info.kind == "linear" or self:isChain4() then
		const y0 = math.floor(relativeFirst / self.widthPx)
		const y1 = math.floor(relativeLast / self.widthPx)
		if y0 == y1 then
			self:markDirtyRect(relativeFirst % self.widthPx, y0, length, 1)
		else
			self:markDirtyRect(0, y0, self.widthPx, y1 - y0 + 1)
		end
		return
	end

	const rowBytes = self:planarRowBytes()
	const y0 = math.floor(relativeFirst / rowBytes)
	const y1 = math.floor(relativeLast / rowBytes)
	if y0 == y1 then
		const byteX0 = relativeFirst % rowBytes
		const byteX1 = relativeLast % rowBytes
		self:markDirtyRect(byteX0 * 8, y0, (byteX1 - byteX0 + 1) * 8, 1)
	else
		self:markDirtyRect(0, y0, self.widthPx, y1 - y0 + 1)
	end
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- port access

function Vga.in8(self: Vga, port: number): number
	const address = band(port, 0xFFFF)

	if address == 0x3C0 then
		return band(self.attr[self.attrIndex] or 0, 0xFF)
	elseif address == 0x3C1 then
		return band(self.attr[self.attrIndex] or 0, 0xFF)
	elseif address == 0x3C2 or address == 0x3CC then
		return band(self.misc, 0xFF)
	elseif address == 0x3C4 then
		return self.seqIndex
	elseif address == 0x3C5 then
		return band(self.seq[self.seqIndex] or 0, 0xFF)
	elseif address == 0x3C6 then
		return self.dacMask
	elseif address == 0x3C7 then
		return self.dacReadIndex
	elseif address == 0x3C8 then
		return self.dacWriteIndex
	elseif address == 0x3C9 then
		const base = self.dacReadIndex * 3 + self.dacReadComponent
		const value = buffer.readu8(self.dac, base)
		self.dacReadComponent += 1
		if self.dacReadComponent >= 3 then
			self.dacReadComponent = 0
			self.dacReadIndex = band(self.dacReadIndex + 1, 0xFF)
		end
		return value
	elseif address == 0x3CA then
		return self.feature
	elseif address == 0x3CE then
		return self.gfxIndex
	elseif address == 0x3CF then
		return band(self.gfx[self.gfxIndex] or 0, 0xFF)
	elseif address == 0x3D4 or address == 0x3B4 then
		return self.crtcIndex
	elseif address == 0x3D5 or address == 0x3B5 then
		return band(self.crtc[self.crtcIndex] or 0, 0xFF)
	elseif address == 0x3DA or address == 0x3BA then
		-- A toggling retrace bit lets both wait-for-set and wait-for-clear loops
		-- terminate. Attribute reads and writes share this flip-flop.
		self.attrFlipFlop = true
		self.statusPhase = not self.statusPhase
		if self.statusPhase then
			return 0x09
		end
		return 0x00
	end

	return self.latched[address] or 0xFF
end

function Vga.writeCrtc(self: Vga, value: number)
	const index = self.crtcIndex
	if index == 0x11 then
		self.crtcProtected = band(value, 0x80) ~= 0
	elseif index <= 0x07 and self.crtcProtected then
		return
	end
	self.crtc[index] = band(value, 0xFF)
	if index == 0x0C or index == 0x0D or index == 0x13 then
		self:markAllDirty()
	end
end

function Vga.writeDac(self: Vga, value: number)
	const base = self.dacWriteIndex * 3 + self.dacWriteComponent
	buffer.writeu8(self.dac, base, band(value, 0x3F))
	self.dacWriteComponent += 1
	if self.dacWriteComponent >= 3 then
		self.dacWriteComponent = 0
		self.dacWriteIndex = band(self.dacWriteIndex + 1, 0xFF)
	end
	self.paletteDirty = true
	self:markAllDirty()
end

function Vga.out8(self: Vga, port: number, value: number)
	const address = band(port, 0xFFFF)
	const byte = band(value, 0xFF)

	if address == 0x3C0 then
		if self.attrFlipFlop then
			const wasEnabled = self.attrPas
			self.attrIndex = band(byte, 0x1F)
			self.attrPas = band(byte, 0x20) ~= 0
			self.attrFlipFlop = false
			if wasEnabled ~= self.attrPas then
				self:markAllDirty()
			end
		else
			self.attr[self.attrIndex] = byte
			self.attrFlipFlop = true
			self.paletteDirty = true
			self:markAllDirty()
		end
	elseif address == 0x3C2 then
		self.misc = byte
		self:markAllDirty()
	elseif address == 0x3C4 then
		self.seqIndex = band(byte, 0x07)
	elseif address == 0x3C5 then
		self.seq[self.seqIndex] = byte
		if self.seqIndex == 1 or self.seqIndex == 4 then
			self:markAllDirty()
		end
	elseif address == 0x3C6 then
		self.dacMask = byte
		self.paletteDirty = true
		self:markAllDirty()
	elseif address == 0x3C7 then
		self.dacReadIndex = byte
		self.dacReadComponent = 0
	elseif address == 0x3C8 then
		self.dacWriteIndex = byte
		self.dacWriteComponent = 0
	elseif address == 0x3C9 then
		self:writeDac(byte)
	elseif address == 0x3CE then
		self.gfxIndex = band(byte, 0x0F)
	elseif address == 0x3CF then
		self.gfx[self.gfxIndex] = byte
	elseif address == 0x3D4 or address == 0x3B4 then
		self.crtcIndex = band(byte, 0x1F)
	elseif address == 0x3D5 or address == 0x3B5 then
		self:writeCrtc(byte)
	elseif address == 0x3DA or address == 0x3BA then
		self.feature = byte
		self.attrFlipFlop = true
	else
		self.latched[address] = byte
	end
end

-- --------------------------------------------------------------- conversion

function Vga.blankTarget(self: Vga)
	const total = self.widthPx * self.heightPx
	for index = 0, total - 1 do
		buffer.writeu32(self.rgba, index * 4, RGBA_BLACK)
	end
end

-- Convert only [x0, x1) x [y0, y1) into the retained RGBA buffer. The host
-- normally repaints a small dirty rectangle (cursor, menu, typing), so a full
-- 640x480 conversion every frame wastes most of the frame budget.
local function blitPlanar(self: Vga, x0: number, y0: number, x1: number, y1: number)
	self:ensurePalette()
	const target = self.rgba
	const width = self.widthPx
	const bytesPerRow = math.ceil(width / 8)
	const rowBytes = math.max(bytesPerRow, self:planarRowBytes())
	const start = self:displayStartBytes()
	const planeEnable = band(self.attr[18], 0x0F)
	const colors = self.color16RGBA
	const firstByte = math.floor(x0 / 8)
	const lastByte = math.floor((x1 - 1) / 8)

	for y = y0, y1 - 1 do
		const rowBase = band(start + y * rowBytes, 0xFFFF)
		for byteX = firstByte, lastByte do
			const offset = band(rowBase + byteX, 0xFFFF)
			const p0 = band(planeEnable, 0x01) ~= 0 and buffer.readu8(self.planes[1], offset) or 0
			const p1 = band(planeEnable, 0x02) ~= 0 and buffer.readu8(self.planes[2], offset) or 0
			const p2 = band(planeEnable, 0x04) ~= 0 and buffer.readu8(self.planes[3], offset) or 0
			const p3 = band(planeEnable, 0x08) ~= 0 and buffer.readu8(self.planes[4], offset) or 0
			for bit = 7, 0, -1 do
				const x = byteX * 8 + (7 - bit)
				if x >= x0 and x < x1 then
					const index = bor(
						band(rshift(p0, bit), 0x01),
						bor(
							lshift(band(rshift(p1, bit), 0x01), 1),
							bor(
								lshift(band(rshift(p2, bit), 0x01), 2),
								lshift(band(rshift(p3, bit), 0x01), 3)
							)
						)
					)
					buffer.writeu32(target, (y * width + x) * 4, colors[index + 1])
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

local function blitLinear(self: Vga, x0: number, y0: number, x1: number, y1: number)
	self:ensurePalette()
	const target = self.rgba
	const width = self.widthPx
	const start = self:displayStartBytes()
	const colors = self.paletteRGBA
	const mask = self.dacMask

	for y = y0, y1 - 1 do
		const rowBase = start + y * width
		local dest = (y * width + x0) * 4
		for x = x0, x1 - 1 do
			const index = band(buffer.readu8(self.chain4, band(rowBase + x, 0xFFFF)), mask)
			buffer.writeu32(target, dest, colors[index + 1])
			dest += 4
		end
	end
end

function Vga.renderPlanar(self: Vga)
	blitPlanar(self, 0, 0, self.widthPx, self.heightPx)
end

function Vga.renderLinear(self: Vga)
	blitLinear(self, 0, 0, self.widthPx, self.heightPx)
end

function Vga.renderText(self: Vga)
	self:ensurePalette()
	const target = self.rgba
	const width = self.widthPx
	const start = band(self:displayStartBytes(), 0xFFFF)
	const colors = self.color16RGBA
	const blank = FONT[63] :: { number }
	const blink = band(self.attr[16], 0x08) ~= 0

	for row = 0, TEXT_ROWS - 1 do
		const sourceRow = band(start + row * TEXT_COLS * 2, 0xFFFF)
		for col = 0, TEXT_COLS - 1 do
			const cell = band(sourceRow + col * 2, 0xFFFF)
			const code = self.mem:read8(TEXT_BASE + cell)
			const attribute = self.mem:read8(TEXT_BASE + cell + 1)
			const foreground = colors[band(attribute, 0x0F) + 1]
			const backgroundBits = blink and band(rshift(attribute, 4), 0x07)
				or band(rshift(attribute, 4), 0x0F)
			const background = colors[backgroundBits + 1]
			const glyph = FONT[code] or blank
			for glyphRow = 0, 7 do
				const bits = glyph[glyphRow]
				const row0 = (row * TEXT_CELL_HEIGHT + glyphRow * 2) * width * 4
				const row1 = row0 + width * 4
				const column = (col * TEXT_CELL_WIDTH) * 4
				for glyphCol = 0, 7 do
					const set = band(bits, lshift(1, 7 - glyphCol)) ~= 0
					const color = set and foreground or background
					const pixel = column + glyphCol * 4
					buffer.writeu32(target, row0 + pixel, color)
					buffer.writeu32(target, row1 + pixel, color)
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Returns a reusable RGBA8 buffer (R,G,B,A bytes, row-major, top-down). The
-- buffer is overwritten by the next snapshotRGBA call (and replaced by
-- setMode), so copy it before retaining it across frames.
function Vga.snapshotRGBA(self: Vga): buffer
	if self:isBlanked() then
		self:blankTarget()
		return self.rgba
	end
	if self.info.kind == "text" then
		self:renderText()
	elseif self.info.kind == "linear" or self:isChain4() then
		self:renderLinear()
	else
		self:renderPlanar()
	end
	return self.rgba
end

-- Convert only the requested rectangle into the retained RGBA buffer. Hosts
-- that track consumeDirty() can pass that rectangle here; pixels outside it
-- keep the values from the previous snapshot.
function Vga.snapshotRegionRGBA(
	self: Vga,
	x: number,
	y: number,
	width: number,
	height: number
): buffer
	const x0 = math.max(0, math.floor(x))
	const y0 = math.max(0, math.floor(y))
	const x1 = math.min(self.widthPx, math.floor(x + width))
	const y1 = math.min(self.heightPx, math.floor(y + height))
	if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0 then
		return self.rgba
	end
	if self:isBlanked() then
		self:blankTarget()
		return self.rgba
	end
	if self.info.kind == "text" then
		-- The text sink reads TextScreen directly; keep the old full-frame
		-- behaviour for callers that use the VGA text fallback.
		return self:snapshotRGBA()
	end
	if self.info.kind == "linear" or self:isChain4() then
		blitLinear(self, x0, y0, x1, y1)
	else
		blitPlanar(self, x0, y0, x1, y1)
	end
	return self.rgba
end

function Vga.snapshot(self: Vga): Snapshot
	return {
		width = self.widthPx,
		height = self.heightPx,
		stride = self.widthPx * 4,
		pixels = self:snapshotRGBA(),
	}
end

-- ------------------------------------------------------------- drawing helpers

function Vga.fillRect(self: Vga, x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, color: number)
	if self.info.kind == "text" then
		return
	end
	const x0 = math.max(0, math.floor(x))
	const y0 = math.max(0, math.floor(y))
	const x1 = math.min(self.widthPx, math.floor(x + width))
	const y1 = math.min(self.heightPx, math.floor(y + height))
	if x1 <= x0 or y1 <= y0 then
		return
	end
	const index = band(color, 0xFF)

	if self.info.kind == "linear" or self:isChain4() then
		const start = self:displayStartBytes()
		for row = y0, y1 - 1 do
			const rowBase = start + row * self.widthPx
			for column = x0, x1 - 1 do
				buffer.writeu8(self.chain4, band(rowBase + column, 0xFFFF), index)
			end
		end
		self:markDirtyRect(x0, y0, x1 - x0, y1 - y0)
		return
	end

	-- Use write mode 0 with set/reset for all planes: the CPU data is ignored,
	-- and the bit mask carves partial edge bytes out of the latches.
	const savedReset = self.gfx[0]
	const savedEnable = self.gfx[1]
	const savedRotate = self.gfx[3]
	const savedMode = self.gfx[5]
	const savedMask = self.gfx[8]
	const savedMapMask = self.seq[2]
	const savedLatches = table.create(4, 0) :: { number }
	for plane = 0, 3 do
		savedLatches[plane] = self.latches[plane]
	end

	self.gfx[0] = index
	self.gfx[1] = 0x0F
	self.gfx[3] = 0x00
	self.gfx[5] = 0x00
	self.gfx[8] = 0xFF
	self.seq[2] = 0x0F

	const rowBytes = math.max(math.ceil(self.widthPx / 8), self:planarRowBytes())
	const start = self:displayStartBytes()
	const firstByte = math.floor(x0 / 8)
	const lastByte = math.floor((x1 - 1) / 8)
	for row = y0, y1 - 1 do
		const rowBase = band(start + row * rowBytes, 0xFFFF)
		for byteX = firstByte, lastByte do
			local mask = 0
			for bit = 0, 7 do
				const pixelX = byteX * 8 + bit
				if pixelX >= x0 and pixelX < x1 then
					mask = bor(mask, lshift(1, 7 - bit))
				end
			end
			const offset = band(rowBase + byteX, 0xFFFF)
			self.gfx[8] = mask
			self:read8(APERTURE_BASE + offset)
			self:write8(APERTURE_BASE + offset, 0)
		end
	end

	self.gfx[0] = savedReset
	self.gfx[1] = savedEnable
	self.gfx[3] = savedRotate
	self.gfx[5] = savedMode
	self.gfx[8] = savedMask
	self.seq[2] = savedMapMask
	for plane = 0, 3 do
		self.latches[plane] = savedLatches[plane]
	end
	self:markDirtyRect(x0, y0, x1 - x0, y1 - y0)
end

function Vga.writeText(self: Vga, row: number, column: number, text: string, attribute: number)
	if row < 0 or row >= TEXT_ROWS or column < 0 or column >= TEXT_COLS then
		return
	end
	const length = math.min(#text, TEXT_COLS - column)
	for index = 1, length do
		const cell = TEXT_BASE + (row * TEXT_COLS + column + index - 1) * 2
		self.mem:write8(cell, string.byte(text, index) :: number)
		self.mem:write8(cell + 1, band(attribute, 0xFF))
	end
end

function Vga.fillTextPattern(self: Vga)
	-- Disable blink so the diagnostic colour-bar row can show all 16 backgrounds.
	self.attr[16] = band(self.attr[16], band(bnot(0x08), 0xFF))
	for row = 0, TEXT_ROWS - 1 do
		for col = 0, TEXT_COLS - 1 do
			const cell = TEXT_BASE + (row * TEXT_COLS + col) * 2
			self.mem:write8(cell, 32)
			self.mem:write8(cell + 1, 0x07)
		end
	end
	self:writeText(2, 24, "RVDM VGA DIAGNOSTIC", 0x1F)
	self:writeText(4, 16, "MODE 03H TEXT FALLBACK 80X25", 0x0F)
	self:writeText(6, 16, "MODE 12H 640X480X16 PLANAR", 0x0A)
	self:writeText(7, 16, "MODE 13H 320X200X256 LINEAR", 0x0B)
	self:writeText(9, 12, "PLANES 0-3 / DAC 6-BIT / CRTC 3D4", 0x0E)
	self:writeText(11, 16, "C:\\WINDOWS> WIN", 0x0F)
	for col = 0, TEXT_COLS - 1 do
		const cell = TEXT_BASE + (20 * TEXT_COLS + col) * 2
		self.mem:write8(cell, 32)
		self.mem:write8(cell + 1, bor(lshift(col % 16, 4), 0x0F))
	end
	self:markAllDirty()
end

function Vga.fillTestPattern(self: Vga)
	-- Diagnostics should be visible even after a guest left the display blanked.
	self.attrPas = true
	self.seq[1] = band(self.seq[1], band(bnot(0x20), 0xFF))
	self.misc = bor(self.misc, 0x02)

	if self.info.kind == "text" then
		self:fillTextPattern()
		return
	end

	if self.info.kind == "linear" or self:isChain4() then
		const width = self.widthPx
		const height = self.heightPx
		self:fillRect(0, 0, width, height, 0)
		for index = 0, 15 do
			self:fillRect(index * 20, 0, 20, 160, index)
		end
		for x = 0, width - 1 do
			const shade = math.floor(x * 255 / (width - 1))
			self:fillRect(x, 160, 1, 32, shade)
		end
		for cellY = 0, 4 do
			for cellX = 0, width / 8 - 1 do
				const color = (cellX + cellY) % 2 == 0 and 15 or 0
				self:fillRect(cellX * 8, 192 + cellY * 8, 8, 8, color)
			end
		end
		self:fillRect(0, 0, width, 2, 15)
		self:fillRect(0, height - 2, width, 2, 15)
		self:fillRect(0, 0, 2, height, 15)
		self:fillRect(width - 2, 0, 2, height, 15)
		self:markAllDirty()
		return
	end

	const width = self.widthPx
	const height = self.heightPx
	self:fillRect(0, 0, width, height, 0)
	for index = 0, 15 do
		self:fillRect(index * 40, 0, 40, 360, index)
	end
	for row = 360, 471, 8 do
		for col = 0, width / 8 - 1 do
			const color = (math.floor(row / 8) + col) % 2 == 0 and 15 or 0
			self:fillRect(col * 8, row, 8, 8, color)
		end
	end
	for index = 0, 15 do
		self:fillRect(index * 40, 472, 40, 4, index)
	end
	self:fillRect(0, 0, width, 4, 15)
	self:fillRect(0, height - 4, width, 4, 15)
	self:fillRect(0, 0, 4, height, 15)
	self:fillRect(width - 4, 0, 4, height, 15)
	self:markAllDirty()
end

return Vga

-- probe: capture-quality
-- datamodel: Client
-- params: level=21
-- purpose: Force the render quality for a capture, then put it back. Studio left in the background runs at about
--   15 fps; with quality on Automatic that collapses the draw distance, so distant geometry (a skyline, the far
--   wall) is missing from Play captures even though it exists. Run with level=21 before capturing and with
--   level=0 afterwards to restore the owner's setting. The reply also reports the frame rate, so a flat ~15 fps
--   tells you timings measured in this session are inflated about four times.
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local level = {{level}}
local ok, message = pcall(function()
	local rendering = settings().Rendering
	if level == 0 then
		-- The saved level lives in a workspace attribute: _G is not shared between separate command sessions.
		local saved = workspace:GetAttribute("ForgeSavedQuality")
		if saved then
			rendering.QualityLevel = Enum.QualityLevel[saved]
			workspace:SetAttribute("ForgeSavedQuality", nil)
		end
		return (saved and "restored to " or "nothing saved, still ") .. tostring(rendering.QualityLevel)
	end
	if workspace:GetAttribute("ForgeSavedQuality") == nil then
		workspace:SetAttribute("ForgeSavedQuality", rendering.QualityLevel.Name)
	end
	rendering.QualityLevel = Enum.QualityLevel["Level" .. string.format("%02d", level)]
	return "quality " .. tostring(rendering.QualityLevel) .. " (was " .. tostring(workspace:GetAttribute("ForgeSavedQuality")) .. ")"
end)
local frames, t0 = 0, os.clock()
while os.clock() - t0 < 2 do
	RunService.Heartbeat:Wait()
	frames += 1
end
local fps = frames / 2
local note = fps < 20 and " - Studio looks throttled (background window): boot and frame timings are not real" or ""
return (ok and message or ("could not change quality: " .. tostring(message))) .. string.format(" | %.0f fps%s", fps, note)

--!strict
-- Xms.lua -- minimal XMS 3.0 driver (HIMEM entry point, A20, HMA, EMB moves).
-- WIN.CNF probes INT 2Fh AX=4300/4310 and then calls the far entry; DOSX uses
-- the same interface after the CPU/version gate. No HIMEM.SYS binary needed.

const band, bor, lshift, rshift = bit32.band, bit32.bor, bit32.lshift, bit32.rshift

const Xms = {}
Xms.__index = Xms

-- Reserved hypervisor segment: F100 hosts the IVT/timer/mouse stubs up to
-- 0x6D, so the XMS far entry goes at 0xC0 and cannot overlap a loaded program
-- (the DOS loader places images below the 0xA000 arena top, but a segment as
-- low as F200 looked "free" only until WSWAP happened to land there).
const ENTRY_SEG = 0xF100
const ENTRY_OFF = 0x00C0
const HMA_START = 0x100000
const HMA_SIZE = 0x10000
const EXT_START = HMA_START + HMA_SIZE

export type Block = {
	start: number,
	size: number,
}

export type Xms = {
	machine: any,
	a20: boolean,
	hmaInUse: boolean,
	blocks: { [number]: Block },
	nextHandle: number,
	entrySeg: number,
	entryOff: number,
	FN: { [number]: (self: Xms, cpu: any) -> () },
	enabled: (self: Xms) -> boolean,
	int2f: (self: Xms) -> boolean,
	dispatch: (self: Xms) -> (),
	releaseAll: (self: Xms) -> (),
}

function Xms.new(machine: any): Xms
	const self = setmetatable({}, Xms) :: any
	self.machine = machine
	-- HIMEM.SYS enables A20 while it initialises and leaves it on; real DOS
	-- extended-memory users (WSWAP) rely on that. 8086 keeps the 20-bit wrap.
	self.a20 = machine.cpu.level >= 1
	machine.mem.a20 = self.a20
	self.hmaInUse = false
	self.blocks = {}
	self.nextHandle = 1
	self.entrySeg = ENTRY_SEG
	self.entryOff = ENTRY_OFF
	-- Far entry: INT 9Fh (inline-dispatched by the machine's stub) ; RETF.
	machine.mem:write8(lshift(ENTRY_SEG, 4) + ENTRY_OFF, 0xCD)
	machine.mem:write8(lshift(ENTRY_SEG, 4) + ENTRY_OFF + 1, 0x9F)
	machine.mem:write8(lshift(ENTRY_SEG, 4) + ENTRY_OFF + 2, 0xCB)
	return self
end

function Xms.enabled(self: Xms): boolean
	return self.machine.cpu.level >= 1 -- 286+
end

-- INT 2Fh installation check / driver entry. Returns true when handled.
function Xms.int2f(self: Xms): boolean
	const cpu = self.machine.cpu
	if not self:enabled() then
		return false
	end
	const ax = cpu.r[1]
	if ax == 0x4300 then
		cpu:wb(0, 0x80)
		cpu:wr(3, 0x0100)
		return true
	elseif ax == 0x4310 then
		cpu.es = self.entrySeg
		cpu:wr(3, self.entryOff)
		return true
	end
	return false
end

local function setMemA20(self: Xms, on: boolean)
	self.a20 = on
	self.machine.mem.a20 = on
end

local function freeList(self: Xms): { Block }
	local list: { Block } = {}
	for _, block in pairs(self.blocks) do
		list[#list + 1] = block
	end
	table.sort(list, function(a: Block, b: Block): boolean
		return a.start < b.start
	end)
	return list
end

local function memoryTotals(self: Xms): (number, number)
	const memSize = self.machine.mem.size
	local cursor = EXT_START
	local largest, total = 0, 0
	for _, block in ipairs(freeList(self)) do
		const gap = block.start - cursor
		if gap > largest then
			largest = gap
		end
		total += gap
		cursor = block.start + block.size
	end
	const tail = memSize - cursor
	if tail > largest then
		largest = tail
	end
	total += tail
	return math.floor(largest / 1024), math.floor(total / 1024)
end

local function allocate(self: Xms, bytes: number): (number?, number?)
	local cursor = EXT_START
	const memSize = self.machine.mem.size
	local gaps: { Block } = {}
	for _, block in ipairs(freeList(self)) do
		if block.start - cursor > 0 then
			gaps[#gaps + 1] = { start = cursor, size = block.start - cursor }
		end
		cursor = block.start + block.size
	end
	if memSize - cursor > 0 then
		gaps[#gaps + 1] = { start = cursor, size = memSize - cursor }
	end
	-- Highest gap first. DOSX standard mode locks its hold and places the PM
	-- image at the very bottom of extended memory (image at start + 0x920 on a
	-- 4 MiB machine); once that hold is released at the kernel handoff, a
	-- low-first allocator would hand WSWAP's swap block the same bytes and
	-- zero the PM code, sending the kernel marching into zeros.
	for index = #gaps, 1, -1 do
		const gap = gaps[index]
		if gap.size >= bytes then
			const start = gap.start + gap.size - bytes
			const handle = self.nextHandle
			self.nextHandle += 1
			self.blocks[handle] = { start = start, size = bytes }
			return handle, start
		end
	end
	return nil, nil
end

local function readDword(mem: any, addr: number): number
	return bor(mem:read16(addr), lshift(mem:read16(addr + 2), 16))
end

local function copyLinear(mem: any, dst: number, src: number, length: number)
	for index = 0, length - 1 do
		mem:write8(dst + index, mem:read8(src + index))
	end
end

Xms.FN = {}

Xms.FN[0x00] = function(_self: Xms, cpu: any) -- get version
	cpu:wr(0, 0x0300)
	cpu:wr(3, 0x0100)
end

Xms.FN[0x01] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- request HMA (DX = KB)
	if self.hmaInUse then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	self.hmaInUse = true
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x02] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- release HMA
	self.hmaInUse = false
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x03] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- enable A20
	setMemA20(self, true)
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x04] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- disable A20
	setMemA20(self, false)
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x05] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- local enable A20
	setMemA20(self, true)
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x06] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- local disable A20
	setMemA20(self, false)
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x07] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- query A20
	cpu:wr(0, self.a20 and 1 or 0)
end

Xms.FN[0x08] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- query free memory
	-- XMS spec: AX = total free KB, DX = largest free block KB.
	const largest, total = memoryTotals(self)
	cpu:wr(0, total)
	cpu:wr(2, largest)
end

Xms.FN[0x09] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- allocate EMB (DX = KB)
	const handle = allocate(self, cpu.r[3] * 1024)
	if not handle then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
	cpu:wr(2, handle) -- XMS 09: DX = handle, AX = 1
end

Xms.FN[0x0A] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- free EMB
	if self.blocks[cpu.r[3]] then
		self.blocks[cpu.r[3]] = nil
		cpu:wr(0, 1)
	else
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
	end
end

Xms.FN[0x0B] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- move extended memory block
	const mem = self.machine.mem
	const base = lshift(cpu.ds, 4) + cpu.r[7] -- DS:SI -> move structure
	const length = readDword(mem, base)
	const srcHandle = mem:read16(base + 4)
	const srcOffset = readDword(mem, base + 6)
	const dstHandle = mem:read16(base + 10)
	const dstOffset = readDword(mem, base + 12)
	-- XMS 0Bh: handle 0 means a real-mode segment:offset packed as a DWORD
	-- (segment in the high word), not a linear address. WSWAP depends on it.
	local function realAddress(offset: number): number
		return lshift(rshift(offset, 16), 4) + band(offset, 0xFFFF)
	end
	local src
	local dst
	if srcHandle == 0 then
		src = realAddress(srcOffset)
	else
		const block = self.blocks[srcHandle]
		if not block or srcOffset + length > block.size then
			cpu:wr(0, 0)
			return
		end
		src = block.start + srcOffset
	end
	if dstHandle == 0 then
		dst = realAddress(dstOffset)
	else
		const block = self.blocks[dstHandle]
		if not block or dstOffset + length > block.size then
			cpu:wr(0, 0)
			return
		end
		dst = block.start + dstOffset
	end
	-- XMS owns A20 during a move: the guest's current gate state must not fold
	-- destinations that live in extended memory (DOSX disables A20 while it
	-- prepares its GDT, then copies the table into an EMB with 0Bh).
	const savedA20 = mem.a20
	mem.a20 = true
	copyLinear(mem, dst, src, length)
	mem.a20 = savedA20
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
end

Xms.FN[0x0C] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- lock EMB
	const block = self.blocks[cpu.r[3]]
	if not block then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
	cpu:wr(3, band(block.start, 0xFFFF))
	cpu:wr(2, band(rshift(block.start, 16), 0xFFFF))
end

Xms.FN[0x0D] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- unlock EMB
	cpu:wr(0, self.blocks[cpu.r[3]] and 1 or 0)
end

Xms.FN[0x0E] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- get EMB info
	const block = self.blocks[cpu.r[3]]
	if not block then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
	cpu:wr(3, 0) -- BL=0 locked blocks, BH=0 total blocks
	cpu:wr(2, band(block.size / 1024, 0xFFFF)) -- DX = size KB
end

Xms.FN[0x88] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- query any extended memory
	-- XMS 3.0 "any and all" pool: every KB above the 1 MB line (the HMA is not
	-- an EMB, but the v3.0 pool starts at the 1 MB mark). AX = largest free
	-- block KB, DX = total free KB; no v3.0 large EMB allocator exists yet, so
	-- largest equals total.
	const kb = band(math.floor((self.machine.mem.size - HMA_START) / 1024), 0xFFFF)
	cpu:wr(0, kb)
	cpu:wr(2, kb)
end

Xms.FN[0x89] = function(self: Xms, cpu: any) -- allocate any extended memory
	const handle = allocate(self, cpu.r[3] * 1024)
	if not handle then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	cpu:wr(0, 1)
	cpu:wr(2, handle)
end

-- A new image cannot inherit another process's extended-memory handles. Real
-- DOS leaves them allocated, but Windows 3.1's WSWAP keeps its swap block and
-- returns to WIN.CNF without freeing it, which would leave DOSX with no XMS.
-- Releasing on EXEC matches what a well-behaved DOS session needs.
function Xms.releaseAll(self: Xms)
	self.blocks = {}
	self.hmaInUse = false
end

function Xms.dispatch(self: Xms)
	const cpu = self.machine.cpu
	const fn = band(rshift(cpu.r[1], 8), 0xFF)
	const handler = self.FN[fn]
	if not handler then
		cpu:wr(0, 0)
		return
	end
	handler(self, cpu)
end

return Xms

-- probe: console
-- datamodel: any
-- params: limit=30 include="error" since=0
-- purpose: The output log, deduplicated and counted, newest last. include = "error" (errors only), "warn" (errors
--   and warnings) or "all". since = only the last N seconds (0 = whole session) - use it right after a change so old
--   errors do not read as new. Zero NEW errors is the gate.
local LIMIT, include, since = {{limit}}, {{include}}, {{since}}
local cutoff = if since > 0 then os.time() - since else 0
local want = {
	[Enum.MessageType.MessageError] = true,
	[Enum.MessageType.MessageWarning] = include ~= "error",
	[Enum.MessageType.MessageOutput] = include == "all",
	[Enum.MessageType.MessageInfo] = include == "all",
}
local seen, order = {}, {}
for _, e in game:GetService("LogService"):GetLogHistory() do
	if want[e.messageType] and (e.timestamp or 0) >= cutoff then
		local key = e.message:gsub("%d+%.%d+", "#"):sub(1, 220)
		if not seen[key] then
			seen[key] = { n = 0, kind = e.messageType.Name:gsub("Message", ""), text = e.message:sub(1, 300) }
			table.insert(order, key)
		end
		seen[key].n += 1
	end
end
local out = { string.format("%d distinct %s message(s)%s", #order, include, if since > 0 then " in the last " .. since .. " s" else "") }
for i = math.max(1, #order - LIMIT + 1), #order do
	local s = seen[order[i]]
	table.insert(out, string.format("%-7s x%-3d %s", s.kind, s.n, s.text))
end
return table.concat(out, "\n")

-- probe: device-layout
-- datamodel: Edit
-- params: devices={} forms={"Phone","Tablet","Console"} minTarget=44 keep=false
-- purpose: Edit-mode layout check across real device presets through StudioDeviceSimulatorService (plugin
--   context: execute_luau has it). For each device (names in devices, else the smallest preset of each form in
--   forms) it sets the device, reads the viewport and reports StarterGui elements off-screen and buttons smaller
--   than minTarget pixels. Then it stops simulation unless keep=true (keep the last device for a screen_capture).
--   UI built at runtime is not in StarterGui: set the device in Edit, then Play and capture (setters error in
--   the Play server). Source: Roblox's rbx-device-simulator-lua skill (get_roblox_skill).
local svc = game:GetService("StudioDeviceSimulatorService")
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")
local WANT, FORMS, MIN, KEEP = {{devices}}, {{forms}}, {{minTarget}}, {{keep}}

local infos = {}
for _, id in svc:GetDeviceListAsync() do
	local ok, info = pcall(function()
		return svc:GetDeviceInfoAsync(id)
	end)
	if ok then
		table.insert(infos, info)
	end
end
local chosen = {}
if #WANT > 0 then
	for _, name in WANT do
		for _, info in infos do
			if info.Name == name then
				table.insert(chosen, info)
			end
		end
	end
else
	for _, form in FORMS do
		local best
		for _, info in infos do
			if info.DeviceForm.Name == form and (not best or info.Width * info.Height < best.Width * best.Height) then
				best = info
			end
		end
		if best then
			table.insert(chosen, best)
		end
	end
end

local function check(vp)
	local issues = {}
	for _, sg in StarterGui:GetChildren() do
		if sg:IsA("ScreenGui") and sg.Enabled then
			for _, obj in sg:GetDescendants() do
				if obj:IsA("GuiObject") and obj.Visible then
					local p, s = obj.AbsolutePosition, obj.AbsoluteSize
					local path = sg.Name .. string.sub(obj:GetFullName(), #sg:GetFullName() + 1)
					if p.X < -2 or p.Y < -2 or p.X + s.X > vp.X + 2 or p.Y + s.Y > vp.Y + 2 then
						table.insert(issues, string.format("  OFF-SCREEN %s (%.0f,%.0f)-(%.0f,%.0f)", path, p.X, p.Y, p.X + s.X, p.Y + s.Y))
					end
					if (obj:IsA("TextButton") or obj:IsA("ImageButton")) and (s.X < MIN or s.Y < MIN) then
						table.insert(issues, string.format("  SMALL TARGET %s %.0fx%.0f", path, s.X, s.Y))
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return issues
end

local out = { string.format("device-layout: %d preset(s) available, %d checked", #infos, #chosen) }
for i, info in chosen do
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		svc:SetDeviceAsync(info.DeviceId)
	end)
	task.wait(0.3)
	if not ok then
		table.insert(out, string.format("%s: could not set (%s)", info.Name, tostring(err)))
	else
		local vp = workspace.CurrentCamera.ViewportSize
		local issues = check(vp)
		table.insert(out, string.format("%s (%s %dx%d): viewport %.0fx%.0f, %d issue(s)", info.Name, info.DeviceForm.Name,
			info.Width, info.Height, vp.X, vp.Y, #issues))
		for j = 1, math.min(#issues, 15) do
			table.insert(out, issues[j])
		end
	end
	if i < #chosen or not KEEP then
		pcall(function()
			svc:StopSimulationAsync()
		end)
		task.wait(0.2)
	end
end
table.insert(out, KEEP and "kept the last device active: capture now, then StopSimulationAsync()" or "simulation stopped: Studio back to its own viewport")
return table.concat(out, "\n")

-- probe: goto
-- datamodel: Server
-- params: x=0 y=10 z=0 anchor=true name=""
-- purpose: Move a player's character to a spot so that area streams in and can be inspected or captured. With
--   StreamingEnabled a camera pinned far from the character shows an empty world: content streams around the
--   character, not the camera, and RequestStreamAroundAsync from the client is not enough. `anchor=true` holds the
--   character in place and makes it unkillable while you look; run again with anchor=false to release it.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local want = {{name}}
local plr
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do
	if want == "" or p.Name == want or p.DisplayName == want then
		plr = p
		break
	end
end
if not plr or not plr.Character then
	return "no player character to move"
end
local char = plr.Character
local root = char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
local hum = char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
if not root or not hum then
	return "character has no HumanoidRootPart/Humanoid yet"
end
local target = Vector3.new({{x}}, {{y}}, {{z}})
pcall(function()
	plr:RequestStreamAroundAsync(target, 5)
end)
local hold = {{anchor}}
if hold then
	if char:GetAttribute("ForgeGotoHealth") == nil then
		char:SetAttribute("ForgeGotoHealth", hum.MaxHealth)
	end
	hum.MaxHealth, hum.Health = 1e6, 1e6
else
	local old = char:GetAttribute("ForgeGotoHealth")
	if old then
		hum.MaxHealth, hum.Health = old, old
		char:SetAttribute("ForgeGotoHealth", nil)
	end
end
char:PivotTo(CFrame.new(target))
root.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.zero
root.Anchored = hold
task.wait(2)
local at = char:GetPivot().Position
return string.format("%s at (%.0f, %.0f, %.0f) anchored=%s - now camera-pin on the Client and capture", plr.Name, at.X, at.Y, at.Z, tostring(hold))

--!strict
-- Lookup and cloning of art models under ReplicatedStorage.ArtAssets.
-- An art path is 1-4 segments of PascalCase names, for example "Buildings/MarketStarter".
local ArtLibrary = {}

local MAX_SEGMENTS = 4

function ArtLibrary.isValidPath(path: string): boolean
	if type(path) ~= "string" or path == "" then
		return false
	end
	local count = 0
	for segment in string.gmatch(path .. "/", "([^/]*)/") do
		count += 1
		if count > MAX_SEGMENTS or string.match(segment, "^%u%w*$") == nil then
			return false
		end
	end
	return count >= 1
end

-- Returns the template Model, or nil and one of InvalidArtPath, MissingArtAsset,
-- InvalidArtAsset. Legacy CC0 models may lack a PrimaryPart; Blender art needs one.
function ArtLibrary.find(root: Instance?, artPath: string): (Model?, string?)
	if not ArtLibrary.isValidPath(artPath) then
		return nil, "InvalidArtPath"
	end
	local current: Instance? = root
	if current == nil then
		return nil, "MissingArtAsset"
	end
	for segment in string.gmatch(artPath .. "/", "([^/]*)/") do
		current = (current :: Instance):FindFirstChild(segment)
		if current == nil then
			return nil, "MissingArtAsset"
		end
	end
	local leaf = current :: Instance
	if not leaf:IsA("Model") then
		return nil, "InvalidArtAsset"
	end
	local model = leaf :: Model
	if model:GetAttribute("ArtSource") == "blender" and model.PrimaryPart == nil then
		return nil, "InvalidArtAsset"
	end
	return model, nil
end

-- Clones a template for placement. Blender art keeps its authored collision; legacy
-- models collide everywhere, as before.
function ArtLibrary.prepareClone(template: Model): Model
	local model = template:Clone()
	local keepCollision = template:GetAttribute("ArtSource") == "blender"
	for _, descendant in model:GetDescendants() do
		if descendant:IsA("BasePart") then
			descendant.Anchored = true
			if not keepCollision then
				descendant.CanCollide = true
			end
		end
	end
	model:SetAttribute("ArtAssetId", template.Name)
	return model
end

return ArtLibrary

--   oversized children paint in mid-air, one-sided) and AlwaysOnTop SurfaceGuis (did not render in testing).
--   Run this FIRST for any "flat wall / screen effect seen from one side only" report.
local root = {{root}}
local out, guis = {}, {}
local function consider(g)
	if g:IsA("SurfaceGui") or g:IsA("BillboardGui") then guis[g] = true end
end
for _, d in root:GetDescendants() do consider(d) end
local lp = game:GetService("Players").LocalPlayer
if lp and lp:FindFirstChild("PlayerGui") then
	for _, d in lp.PlayerGui:GetDescendants() do consider(d) end
end
local nOver, nTop = 0, 0
for g in guis do
	if g:IsA("SurfaceGui") and g.AlwaysOnTop then
		nTop += 1
		if nTop <= 10 then table.insert(out, "ALWAYSONTOP " .. g:GetFullName()) end
	end
	if not g.ClipsDescendants then
		for _, c in g:GetDescendants() do
			if c:IsA("GuiObject") and c.Visible and c.Parent == g then
				local p, s = c.Position, c.Size
				local x0, y0 = p.X.Scale - c.AnchorPoint.X * s.X.Scale, p.Y.Scale - c.AnchorPoint.Y * s.Y.Scale
				if x0 < -0.01 or y0 < -0.01 or x0 + s.X.Scale > 1.01 or y0 + s.Y.Scale > 1.01 then
					nOver += 1
					if nOver <= 20 then
						table.insert(out, string.format("OVERFLOW %s  (x %.2f..%.2f, y %.2f..%.2f of canvas 0..1)", c:GetFullName(), x0, x0 + s.X.Scale, y0, y0 + s.Y.Scale))
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
end
table.insert(out, 1, string.format("guis scanned %d | overflowing children %d | AlwaysOnTop SurfaceGuis %d", (function() local n = 0 for _ in guis do n += 1 end return n end)(), nOver, nTop))
if nOver > 0 then table.insert(out, "FIX: set ClipsDescendants = true on those SurfaceGuis (or keep children inside 0..1).") end
return table.concat(out, "\n")

-- probe: hide
-- datamodel: Edit
-- params: target=workspace.Model
-- purpose: Bisect a visual artefact. Moves one instance (and everything under it) out of the world into
--   ServerStorage.ProbeHidden and remembers where it came from. Capture again from the SAME camera pose: if the
--   artefact is gone it lives under that instance; restore and hide half its children next. Always run `restore`.
local target = {{target}}
assert(target and target.Parent, "target not found or already detached")
local SS = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
local bin = SS:FindFirstChild("ProbeHidden") or Instance.new("Folder")
bin.Name, bin.Parent = "ProbeHidden", SS
local link = Instance.new("ObjectValue")
link.Name, link.Value = "Origin", target.Parent
local holder = Instance.new("Folder")
holder.Name = target.Name
link.Parent = holder
holder.Parent = bin
local path = target:GetFullName()
target.Parent = holder
return "hidden " .. path .. " (run the restore probe when done)"

local function readNumbers(container: Instance, name: string): ()
	local value = container:FindFirstChild(name)

	-- First check if the child exists
	if not value then
		error(container:GetFullName() .. " has no child called " .. name, 1)
	end

	-- Then check if it is a NumberValue
	if not value:IsA("NumberValue") then
		error(value:GetFullName() .. " is a " .. value.ClassName .. " not a NumberValue.", 1)
	end

	-- Return the NumberValue.Value property
	return value.Value
end

function TankConfig.read(tank: Model): (Config, { [any]: any })
	local hullSettings = tank:FindFirstChild("HullSettings")
	if not hullSettings then
		error(tank:GetFullName() .. "is missing HullSettings.", 1)
	end
	local result = readNumbers(hullSettings, "MovementSpeed")
	return { movementSpeed = result }
end

return TankConfig

--!nonstrict
-- TestApps.lua -- Win16 helpers for the bundled test binaries, registered as
-- high ordinals on KERNEL: 300 PrintString(seg:off), 301 PrintWordHex(word).

const band = bit32.band

const TestApps = {}

-- extends the already-registered KERNEL module; imports resolve "KERNEL"#300
function TestApps.register(machine: any)
	const exports = machine.winModules.KERNEL
	assert(exports, "register KERNEL exports before TestApps")

	local function arg(cpu: any, index: number): number
		return machine.mem:read16(
			machine.mem.phys(cpu.ss, band(cpu.r[5] + 6 + (index - 1) * 2, 0xFFFF))
		)
	end

	const definitions = {
		[300] = {
			args = 4,
			fn = function(host, cpu)
				const offset = arg(cpu, 1)
				const segment = arg(cpu, 2)
				local parts: { string } = {}
				for index = 0, 255 do
					const ch = host.mem:read8(host.mem.phys(segment, offset + index))
					if ch == 0x24 then
						break
					end
					parts[#parts + 1] = (ch >= 32 and ch < 127) and string.char(ch) or " "
				end
				host.bios:write(table.concat(parts) .. "\r\n")
				cpu:wr(0, 0)
			end,
		},
		[301] = {
			args = 2,
			fn = function(host, cpu)
				const value = arg(cpu, 1)
				host.bios:write(("%04X\r\n"):format(band(value, 0xFFFF)))
			end,
		},
	}

	for ordinal, definition in pairs(definitions) do
		exports[ordinal] = definition
	end
	machine:defineWinModule("KERNEL", exports)
end

return TestApps

-- probe: perf
-- datamodel: any
-- params: seconds=3
-- purpose: A quick performance snapshot: frame time over a short window, memory, and the instance counts that
--   usually explain a slow place. Compare before and after a change; one snapshot alone means little.
--   Studio throttles an unfocused window to about 66 ms a frame: a flat frame near that is labelled, because it
--   is Studio's cap, not the game's cost (bring Studio to the front and measure again).
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local Stats = game:GetService("Stats")
local frames, worst, best, t0 = 0, 0, math.huge, os.clock()
local conn = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)
	frames += 1
	worst = math.max(worst, dt)
	best = math.min(best, dt)
end)
task.wait({{seconds}})
conn:Disconnect()
local elapsed = os.clock() - t0
local parts, scripts, guis, emitters, lights = 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
for _, d in workspace:GetDescendants() do
	if d:IsA("BasePart") then parts += 1
	elseif d:IsA("BaseScript") then scripts += 1
	elseif d:IsA("LayerCollector") then guis += 1
	elseif d:IsA("ParticleEmitter") then emitters += 1
	elseif d:IsA("Light") then lights += 1 end
end
local avg = elapsed / math.max(frames, 1)
-- Flat and near 66 ms: what an unfocused Studio window looks like. A game that really costs 66 ms looks the
-- same, so this is a label to re-measure in front, not a verdict.
local throttled = avg > 0.055 and avg < 0.08 and (worst - best) < 0.015
return (if throttled then "LIKELY UNFOCUSED-STUDIO THROTTLE (flat ~66 ms frames): not the game's cost; bring Studio to the front and re-run | " else "") .. string.format(
	"heartbeat avg %.1f ms (%.0f fps), worst %.1f ms | memory %.0f MB | instances %d | workspace: parts %d, scripts %d, world guis %d, emitters %d, lights %d",
	elapsed / math.max(frames, 1) * 1000, frames / elapsed, worst * 1000, Stats:GetTotalMemoryUsageMb(),
	Stats.InstanceCount, parts, scripts, guis, emitters, lights)

local Occupancy: { [any]: any } = {}

-- Defines Occupancy.VALUE_NAME and the Restore type definition.
Occupancy.VALUE_NAME = "Occupant"
export type Restore = {
  transparency: { [Instance] : number },
  collide: { [BasePart] : boolean },
  query: { [BasePart] : boolean },
  walkSpeed: number,
  jumpHeight: number,
  nameDisplay: Enum.HumanoidDisplayDistanceType,
 weld: WeldConstraint?
}

-- Defines restores table
local restores: { [Model]: Restore } = {}

function Occupancy.value(tank: Model): Instance
	-- Check if an "Occupant" ObjectValue already exists.
	local existing = tank:FindFirstChild(Occupancy.VALUE_NAME)
	if existing and existing:IsA("ObjectValue") then
		return existing
	end
	local value: ObjectValue = Instance.new("ObjectValue")
	value.Name = Occupancy.VALUE_NAME
	value.Parent = tank
	return value
end

function Occupancy.hide(character: Model, hull: BasePart): boolean
	-- First check if the restores table already has
	if restores[character] then
		return false
	end

	-- Check if there's a Humanoid and a HumaoidRootPart on the player character.
	local humanoid = (character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid") :: Humanoid?)
	local root = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not humanoid or not root or not root:IsA("BasePart") then
		return false
	end

	-- Create the initial "restore" table for the player
	local restore: { [any]: any } = {
		transparency = {},
		collide = {},
		query = {},
		walkSpeed = humanoid.WalkSpeed,
		jumpHeight = humanoid.JumpHeight,
		nameDisplay = humanoid.DisplayDistanceType,
		weld = nil,
	}

	--[[
		Go through all instances in the array and cache it's original state. Decals and Textures only have their initial transparency cached, while BaseParts also have their CanCollide and CanQuery state cached.

	]]
	for key, part: BasePart in pairs(character:GetDescendants()) do
		if part:IsA("BasePart") then
			local Cast = (part :: BasePart)
			restore.transparency[Cast] = Cast.Transparency
			restore.collide[Cast] = Cast.CanCollide
			restore.query[Cast] = Cast.CanQuery
			Cast.Transparency = 1
			Cast.CanCollide = false
			Cast.CanQuery = false

		-- Handle Decals and Textures here
		elseif part:IsA("Decal") or part:IsA("Texture") then
			restore.transparency[part] = part.Transparency
			part.Transparency = 1
		end
	end

	-- Handle Humanoid settings that can't be iterated over
	humanoid.WalkSpeed = 0
	humanoid.JumpHeight = 0
	humanoid.DisplayDistanceType = Enum.HumanoidDisplayDistanceType.None

	-- Create the binding weld here for the player to be connected to the hull.
	root.CFrame = hull.CFrame
	local weld: WeldConstraint = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
	weld.Name = "TankOccupant"
	weld.Part0 = root
	weld.Part1 = hull
	weld.Parent = root

	-- Finish handling the character restore points and bind the new restore table to the global restores table.
	restore.weld = weld
	restores[character] = restore
	return true
end

function Occupancy.show(character: Model, exitAt: CFrame): ()
	local restore: { [any]: any } = restores[character]

	-- If a character restore can't be found, do nothing
	if not restore then
		return
	end

	-- Remove the Restore table for a character
	restores[character] = nil

	-- Destroy the weld
	if restores.weld then
		restores.weld:Destroy()
	end

	-- Reset all instance transparencies captured in the restore table.
	for instance: Instance, value: number in pairs(restores.transparency) do
		if instance.Parent then
			instance.Transparency = value
		end
	end

	-- Reset all BasePart CanCollides captured in the restore table.
	for part: BasePart, value: boolean in pairs(restores.collide) do
		if part.Parent then
			part.CanCollide = value
		end
	end

	-- Reset all BasePart CanQuerys captured in the restore table.
	for part: BasePart, value: boolean in pairs(restores.query) do
		if part.Parent then
			part.CanQuery = value
		end
	end

	-- Reset the Humanoid State
	local humanoid = (character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid") :: Humanoid?)
	if humanoid then
		humanoid.WalkSpeed = restore.walkSpeed
		humanoid.JumpHeight = restore.jumpHeight
		humanoid.DisplayDistanceType = restore.nameDisplay
	end

	-- Set the character's root back to the exit CFrame position.
	local root = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if root and root:IsA("BasePart") then
		root.CFrame = exitAt
	end
end

-- Is the given character currently riding in a tank?
function Occupancy.isHidden(character: Model): ()
	return restores[character] ~= nil
end

return Occupancy

--!strict
-- Emulator.client -- runs the Vdm machine on the CLIENT (full frame budget,
-- zero replication), renders into a Windows 3.0-style host window and feeds
-- keyboard/PS/2 input.

const ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
const RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
const UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
const Players = game:GetService("Players")
const StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")

const SoundService = game:GetService("SoundService")
const Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

const Vdm = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Vdm"))
const VdmUi = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("VdmUi")
const Fixtures = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("VdmFixtures")
const BOOT_WINDOWS = ReplicatedStorage:GetAttribute("VdmBootWindows") == true

const Cleaner = require(VdmUi:WaitForChild("Cleaner"))
const Window = require(VdmUi:WaitForChild("Window"))
const Theme = require(VdmUi:WaitForChild("Theme"))
const ScreenSink = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("ScreenSink"))
const VgaSink = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("VgaSink"))
const KeyboardMap = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("KeyboardMap"))

const GUEST_WIDTH = 640
const GUEST_HEIGHT = 480
const TITLE_HEIGHT = Theme.Sizes.TitleBar
const STATUS_HEIGHT = Theme.Sizes.StatusBar
const MIN_WINDOW_SCALE = 1
const MAX_WINDOW_SCALE = 3
-- Measured against MOUSE.DRV 3.0's PS/2 path at 640x480x16 (2026-11-06, five
-- point affine fit, slope 1.0): the rendered guest arrow sits exactly 58 px
-- below the tracked cursor position after an anchor, in every guest state we
-- can observe. The driver is real guest code, so the host compensates here:
-- injecting y - 58 makes the rendered arrow coincide with the host pointer.
const MOUSE_DRV_Y_BIAS = 58

const cleaner = Cleaner.new()

-- PC speaker host bridge: the guest beep is a state change on PIT channel 2
-- gated by port 0x61. Roblox has no raw audio synthesis, so each guest
-- on-edge/frequency change retriggers one short stock beep. This is optional:
-- if the asset cannot play, the emulator still runs silently.
const speakerBeep = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("Sound"))
speakerBeep.Name = "PcSpeaker"
speakerBeep.SoundId = "rbxasset://sounds/electronicpingshort.wav"
speakerBeep.Volume = 0.35
speakerBeep.RollOffMode = Enum.RollOffMode.Inverse
speakerBeep.Parent = SoundService
local lastSpeakerSequence = 0
local lastBeepAt = 0

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- host scene
-- The emulator is the experience: cover the default baseplate/skybox with an
-- opaque desktop and remove the character/spawn so the window is all that is
-- visible while the GUI still loads normally.
local function disableCoreGui()
	pcall(function()
		StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.All, false)
	end)
	for _, kind in
		{
			Enum.CoreGuiType.Backpack,
			Enum.CoreGuiType.Chat,
			Enum.CoreGuiType.EmotesMenu,
			Enum.CoreGuiType.Health,
			Enum.CoreGuiType.PlayerList,
		}
	do
		pcall(function()
			StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(kind, false)
		end)
	end
	pcall(function()
		StarterGui:SetCore("TopbarEnabled", false)
	end)
	pcall(function()
		StarterGui:SetCore("ChatActive", false)
	end)
	pcall(function()
		StarterGui:SetCore("ResetButtonCallback", false)
	end)
	-- CoreGui finishes initialising a few frames after the client script
	-- starts; the topbar can reappear if the call is only made once.
	task.spawn(function()
		for _ = 1, 12 do
			task.wait(0.5)
			pcall(function()
				StarterGui:SetCore("TopbarEnabled", false)
			end)
			pcall(function()
				StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.All, false)
			end)
		end
	end)
end

local function clearWorld()
	for _, child in Workspace:GetChildren() do
		if child:IsA("SpawnLocation") or (child:IsA("BasePart") and child.Name == "Baseplate") then
			child:Destroy()
		end
	end
end

disableCoreGui()
clearWorld()
cleaner:Connect(Workspace.ChildAdded, function(child: Instance)
	if child:IsA("SpawnLocation") or (child:IsA("BasePart") and child.Name == "Baseplate") then
		child:Destroy()
	end
end)

const playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")
const screenGui = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("ScreenGui"))
screenGui.Name = "VdmGui"
screenGui.ResetOnSpawn = false
screenGui.IgnoreGuiInset = true
screenGui.ZIndexBehavior = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling
screenGui.Parent = playerGui

const holder = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("Frame"))
holder.Name = "Desktop"
holder.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
holder.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)
holder.BorderSizePixel = 0
holder.Parent = screenGui

-- Remove the local character as soon as it appears too. A server-side
-- CharacterAutoLoads=false would also work, but the client must keep working
-- when the place does not ship a server script.
const localPlayer = Players.LocalPlayer
local function removeCharacter(character: Model)
	character:Destroy()
end
if localPlayer.Character then
	removeCharacter(localPlayer.Character)
end
cleaner:Connect(localPlayer.CharacterAdded, removeCharacter)

const camera = Workspace.CurrentCamera
if camera then
	camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable
	camera.CFrame = CFrame.new(0, 8, 20) * CFrame.Angles(math.rad(-8), 0, 0)
end

-- --------------------------------------------------------------- host window
local function viewportSize(): Vector2
	-- the real desktop frame is the truth: in Studio the camera viewport can
	-- differ from the ScreenGui area, which pushed the window to the top
	const area = holder.AbsoluteSize
	if area.X > 0 and area.Y > 0 then
		return area
	end
	const current = Workspace.CurrentCamera
	if current then
		return current.ViewportSize
	end
	return Vector2.new(1280, 720)
end

local function fitWindow(): UDim2
	const viewport = viewportSize()
	-- the ScreenGui covers the full viewport (IgnoreGuiInset), so the only
	-- reservation is a small margin
	const availableWidth = math.max(320, viewport.X - 32)
	const availableHeight = math.max(240, viewport.Y - 32)
	local best = 0
	for scale = MIN_WINDOW_SCALE, MAX_WINDOW_SCALE do
		const width = GUEST_WIDTH * scale
		const height = GUEST_HEIGHT * scale + TITLE_HEIGHT + STATUS_HEIGHT
		if width <= availableWidth and height <= availableHeight then
			best = scale
		end
	end
	if best > 0 then
		return UDim2.fromOffset(
			GUEST_WIDTH * best,
			GUEST_HEIGHT * best + TITLE_HEIGHT + STATUS_HEIGHT
		)
	end
	const scale = math.max(
		0.1,
		math.min(
			availableWidth / GUEST_WIDTH,
			(availableHeight - TITLE_HEIGHT - STATUS_HEIGHT) / GUEST_HEIGHT
		)
	)
	return UDim2.fromOffset(
		math.max(320, math.floor(GUEST_WIDTH * scale)),
		math.max(240, math.floor(GUEST_HEIGHT * scale) + TITLE_HEIGHT + STATUS_HEIGHT)
	)
end

const window = Window.new("Windows 3.0a", fitWindow())
window.Gui.ZIndex = 2
window.Gui.Parent = holder

const display = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("Frame"))
display.Name = "Display"
display.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -STATUS_HEIGHT)
display.BackgroundColor3 = Theme.Colors.Screen
display.BorderSizePixel = 0

const sink = ScreenSink.new(cleaner, display)

const videoHost = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("Frame"))

statusLabel.BackgroundTransparency = 1
statusLabel.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(22, 0)
statusLabel.Size = UDim2.new(0.55, -22, 1, 0)

statusLabel.TextSize = 12

statusLabel.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left

statusLabel.ZIndex = 4
statusLabel.Parent = statusBar

statusDetail.Name = "Detail"
statusDetail.BackgroundTransparency = 1
statusDetail.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.55, 0)
statusDetail.Size = UDim2.new(0.45, -10, 1, 0)
statusDetail.Font = Theme.Fonts.Ui
statusDetail.TextSize = 12
statusDetail.TextColor3 = Theme.Colors.TextDim
statusDetail.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Right
statusDetail.Text = ""
statusDetail.ZIndex = 4

local function setStatus(text: string, detail: string, color: Color3)
	if statusLabel.Text ~= text then
		statusLabel.Text = text
	end
	if statusDetail.Text ~= detail then
		statusDetail.Text = detail
	end
	statusDot.BackgroundColor3 = color
end

local function refit()
	window.Gui.Size = fitWindow()
	window:ClampToViewport()
end
cleaner:Connect(holder:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"), refit)
const statusCamera = Workspace.CurrentCamera
if statusCamera then
	cleaner:Connect(statusCamera:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"), refit)
end

-- ------------------------------------------------------------------- machine
const machine = Vdm.Machine.new({
	Memory = Vdm.Memory,
	Cpu = Vdm.Cpu,
	Vfs = Vdm.Vfs,
	Bios = Vdm.Bios,
	Dos = Vdm.Dos,
	TextScreen = Vdm.TextScreen,
	Executables = Vdm.Executables,
	Vga = Vdm.Vga,
	Xms = Vdm.Xms,
	logger = function(message: string)
		print("[Vdm] " .. message)
	end,
})
-- Automation/debug surface (Studio MCP probes): never used by the UI.
-- _G is per script context in Studio, so the machine is shared through a
-- BindableFunction: Invoke("mouse", x, y), Invoke("sync"), Invoke("state").
const machineBridge = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("BindableFunction"))
machineBridge.Name = "VdmMachineBridge"
machineBridge.OnInvoke = function(command: string, a: number?, b: number?)
	if command == "mouse" then
		machine:setMouse(a or 0, b or 0, machine.mouseButtons)
		return true
	elseif command == "sync" then
		return machine:syncMouse()
	elseif command == "click" then
		machine:setMouse(machine.mouseX, machine.mouseY, 1)
		task.wait(0.1)
		machine:setMouse(machine.mouseX, machine.mouseY, 0)
		return true
	end
	return {
		mouseX = machine.mouseX,
		mouseY = machine.mouseY,
		buttons = machine.mouseButtons,
		ps2 = machine.mousePs2Enabled,
		packets = #machine.mousePackets,
		mickeyX = machine.mouseMickeyX,
		mickeyY = machine.mouseMickeyY,
		minX = machine.mouseMinX,
		minY = machine.mouseMinY,
		maxX = machine.mouseMaxX,
		maxY = machine.mouseMaxY,
	}
end
machineBridge.Parent = playerGui
if BOOT_WINDOWS then
	const WinBoot = require(Fixtures:WaitForChild("WinBoot"))
	const DriversA = require(Fixtures:WaitForChild("WinBootDriversA"))
	const DriversB = require(Fixtures:WaitForChild("WinBootDriversB"))
	machine.vfs:ensureDir("C:\\WINDOWS")
	machine.vfs:ensureDir("C:\\WINDOWS\\SYSTEM")
	machine.vfs:writeFile("C:\\WINDOWS\\WIN.COM", WinBoot.winCom)
	machine.vfs:writeFile("C:\\WINDOWS\\KERNEL.EXE", WinBoot.kernel)
	machine.vfs:writeFile("C:\\WINDOWS\\COMMAND.COM", require(Fixtures:WaitForChild("Command")))
	machine.vfs:writeFile("C:\\WINDOWS\\WIN.INI", WinBoot.winIni)
	machine.vfs:writeFile("C:\\WINDOWS\\SYSTEM.INI", WinBoot.systemIni)

		const data = WinBoot.decode(encoded)

		const data = WinBoot.decode(encoded)

	end

	const bigManifest = Fixtures:FindFirstChild("WinBootBig")

			for name, chunks in require(bigManifest) do

					parts[#parts + 1] = require(Fixtures:WaitForChild(chunkName))
				end
				const data = WinBoot.decode(table.concat(parts))

		end)
		if not ok then
			warn("[Vdm] WinBoot big files: " .. tostring(err))
