--!strict
--[[
	The tank's tunables, read out of the model rather than typed in here.

	`HullSettings` is a `Configuration` folder the model already carries, and the
	point of reading it is that this demo and the Roswaal graph version have to
	agree on where a number comes from. A constant hard-coded in one and read
	from a `NumberValue` in the other is not the same program, and the comparison
	would be measuring the wrong thing.

	Only what the demo uses. `HP`, and the whole of `TurretSettings`, come back
	when damage and firing do — reading values nothing consumes would make the
	module look like it does more than it does.
]]

local TankConfig = {}

export type Config = {
	--- Studs per second at full throttle.
	movementSpeed: number,
}

--[[
	Numbers the model has no home for.

	Each is a candidate for a new `NumberValue` in `HullSettings`, and the reason
	none has been added is that adding one is Studio work and these want tuning
	against a running tank first. When they settle they should move, and this
	table should shrink.
]]
local TUNING = {
	--- Degrees per second the hull yaws at full steer.
	turnRate = 45,
	--- Seconds from a standstill to full speed. Sixty tons does not leap.
	accelerationTime = 5,
	--- Seconds from full speed back to a standstill. Much shorter than
	--- accelerating: a tank has brakes and does not have much power. Was 2.5,
	--- which coasted about two and a half tank lengths after letting go and felt
	--- like ice rather than like weight.
	brakingTime = 1.2,
	--- Reverse tops out at this fraction of forward speed.
	reverseFraction = 0.45,
	--- Degrees per second the turret traverses. Slow on purpose: a turret that
	--- snaps to the camera is a turret nobody believes weighs sixty tons.
	traverseRate = 30,
	--- Degrees per second the gun elevates.
	elevationRate = 16,
	--- The gun's own limits, in degrees. Set by the author for the demo rather
	--- than taken from the real vehicle.
	minElevation = -7,
	maxElevation = 10,
	--- How far above the ground the tracks sit, to stop them clipping into it.
	groundClearance = 0.05,
	--- How close you have to be for the prompt to appear. The tank is 22 studs
	--- long, so this is "standing beside it" rather than "across the field".
	promptDistance = 18,
}

export type Tuning = typeof(TUNING)

TankConfig.tuning = TUNING

--[[
	Reads a `NumberValue` out of a `Configuration`.

	Deliberately loud. A missing setting is a model that does not match the code,
	and the failure it causes if allowed through — a tank that will not move
	because its speed defaulted to zero — is far harder to trace back here than
	an error naming the value on the first frame.
]]
local function readNumber(container: Instance, name: string): number
	local value = container:FindFirstChild(name)
	if not value then
		error(`{container:GetFullName()} has no "{name}"`, 0)
	end
	if not value:IsA("NumberValue") then
		error(`{value:GetFullName()} is a {value.ClassName}, expected a NumberValue`, 0)
	end
	return value.Value
end

function TankConfig.read(tank: Model): Config
	local hullSettings = tank:FindFirstChild("HullSettings")
	if not hullSettings then
		error(`{tank:GetFullName()} is missing HullSettings`, 0)
	end
	return { movementSpeed = readNumber(hullSettings, "MovementSpeed") }
end

return TankConfig

local bin = game:GetService("ServerStorage"):FindFirstChild("ProbeHidden")

for _, holder in bin:GetChildren() do

	for _, c in holder:GetChildren() do

-- GAME_BLENDER overrides the default install path. Returns nil when no executable exists.
function Blender.resolve(): string?
	local override = process.env.GAME_BLENDER
	local path = if override ~= nil and override ~= "" then override else Config.DEFAULT_BLENDER
	if fs.isFile(path) then
		return path
	end
	return nil
end

-- blender -b --factory-startup [<blend>] --python <script> -- <extra...>
function Blender.arguments(blend: string?, script: string, extra: { string }): { string }
	local args = { "-b", "--factory-startup" }
	if blend ~= nil then
		table.insert(args, blend)
	end
	table.insert(args, "--python")
	table.insert(args, script)
	table.insert(args, "--")
	for _, value in ipairs(extra) do
		table.insert(args, value)
	end
	return args
end

function Blender.run(blender: string, blend: string?, script: string, extra: { string }): Result
	local result = process.exec(blender, Blender.arguments(blend, script, extra))
	return { ok = result.ok, code = result.code, stdout = result.stdout, stderr = result.stderr }
end

-- The first line of `blender --version`, for example "Blender 5.2.2 LTS".
function Blender.version(blender: string): string?
	local ok, result = pcall(process.exec, blender, { "--version" })
	if not ok or not result.ok then
		return nil
	end
	return string.match(result.stdout, "^([^\r\n]+)")
end

-- The ART_* status lines a Blender script printed (errors carry their code first).
function Blender.artLines(result: Result): { string }
	local lines = {}
	for line in string.gmatch(result.stdout .. "\n" .. result.stderr, "[^\r\n]+") do
		if string.sub(line, 1, 4) == "ART_" then
			table.insert(lines, line)
		end
	end
	return lines
end

return Blender

-- PERFORMANCE OF THIS SOFTWARE.

--!strict
--[[
	Who is driving, and what happens to the body they left outside.

	## Why an ObjectValue rather than a remote

	`Occupant` is an `ObjectValue` inside the tank holding the driving `Player`,
	or nothing. The server sets it; every client watches it. That is one
	replicated property instead of an enter event, an exit event, a late-joiner
	catch-up, and the bug where a client that joined mid-drive never learns the
	tank is occupied.

	It is also **visible in the explorer while the game runs**, which is worth
	more than it sounds for a demo somebody is evaluating: you can see who is in
	the tank without reading a line of code.

	## Hiding rather than replacing

	Hidden means invisible, non-colliding **and unqueryable** — see `hide` for why
	the third one is not cosmetic.

	The character is hidden and welded to the hull, not deleted and not swapped
	for a rig. Deleting it means respawning on exit, with everything that hangs
	off `CharacterAdded` running again; a driver rig means building one. Hiding
	is reversible by construction — every value this changes, it wrote down
	first — and it keeps the player's own character as the thing that gets back
	out.
]]

local Occupancy = {}

Occupancy.VALUE_NAME = "Occupant"

--- What was changed on the way in, so getting out can put it back.
type Restore = {
	transparency: { [Instance]: number },
	collide: { [BasePart]: boolean },
	query: { [BasePart]: boolean },
	walkSpeed: number,
	jumpHeight: number,
	nameDisplay: Enum.HumanoidDisplayDistanceType,
	weld: WeldConstraint?,
}

local restores: { [Model]: Restore } = {}

--- The value the server writes and the clients watch. Created on demand.
function Occupancy.value(tank: Model): ObjectValue
	local existing = tank:FindFirstChild(Occupancy.VALUE_NAME)
	if existing and existing:IsA("ObjectValue") then
		return existing
	end
	local value = Instance.new("ObjectValue")
	value.Name = Occupancy.VALUE_NAME
	value.Parent = tank
	return value
end

--[[
	Puts the character inside the tank: invisible, non-colliding, along for the
	ride.

	The weld is what carries it, and it matters that the hull is anchored — a
	`WeldConstraint` to an anchored part makes the character kinematic, so it
	travels exactly with the tank and contributes no physics of its own.
]]
function Occupancy.hide(character: Model, hull: BasePart): boolean
	if restores[character] then
		return false
	end
	local humanoid = character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid")
	local root = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not humanoid or not root or not root:IsA("BasePart") then
		return false
	end

	local restore: Restore = {
		transparency = {},
		collide = {},
		query = {},
		walkSpeed = humanoid.WalkSpeed,
		jumpHeight = humanoid.JumpHeight,
		nameDisplay = humanoid.DisplayDistanceType,
		weld = nil,
	}

	for _, part in character:GetDescendants() do
		if part:IsA("BasePart") then
			restore.transparency[part] = part.Transparency
			restore.collide[part] = part.CanCollide
			restore.query[part] = part.CanQuery
			part.Transparency = 1
			part.CanCollide = false
			-- `CanQuery`, and not only `CanCollide`. A raycast hits a part with
			-- collisions off — the two flags answer different questions — and the
			-- tank drops a probe from above itself every frame to find the ground.
			-- With the driver welded at the hull's centre, that probe lands on
			-- their head, the hull is placed a ride height above *that*, and the
			-- driver rises with it: the tank climbs about five studs a frame and
			-- flies into the sky with the player still in it.
			part.CanQuery = false
		elseif part:IsA("Decal") or part:IsA("Texture") then
			restore.transparency[part] = part.Transparency
			part.Transparency = 1
		end
	end

	humanoid.WalkSpeed = 0
	humanoid.JumpHeight = 0
	-- The name tag would otherwise float over an empty tank.
	humanoid.DisplayDistanceType = Enum.HumanoidDisplayDistanceType.None

	root.CFrame = hull.CFrame
	local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
	weld.Name = "TankOccupant"
	weld.Part0 = root
	weld.Part1 = hull
	weld.Parent = root
	restore.weld = weld

	restores[character] = restore
	return true
end

--[[
	Puts them back, beside the tank rather than inside it.

	Every restored value was read on the way in rather than assumed, because a
	game that had already changed a character's `WalkSpeed` would otherwise find
	Roswaal's demo had reset it to 16 on the way out.
]]
function Occupancy.show(character: Model, exitAt: CFrame)
	local restore = restores[character]
	if not restore then
		return
	end
	restores[character] = nil

	if restore.weld then
		restore.weld:Destroy()
	end
	for instance, value in restore.transparency do
		if instance.Parent then
			(instance :: any).Transparency = value
		end
	end
	for part, value in restore.collide do
		if part.Parent then
			part.CanCollide = value
		end
	end
	for part, value in restore.query do
		if part.Parent then
			part.CanQuery = value
		end
	end

	local humanoid = character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid")
	if humanoid then
		humanoid.WalkSpeed = restore.walkSpeed
		humanoid.JumpHeight = restore.jumpHeight
		humanoid.DisplayDistanceType = restore.nameDisplay
	end

	local root = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if root and root:IsA("BasePart") then
		root.CFrame = exitAt
	end
end

--- Whether this character is currently riding inside something.
function Occupancy.isHidden(character: Model): boolean
	return restores[character] ~= nil
end

return Occupancy

-- Cleaner.lua -- trove-style cleanup: Add collects instances, connections,
-- functions or cleanup-capable objects; Clean() disposes in reverse order.

const Cleaner = {}
Cleaner.__index = Cleaner

export type Disposable = Instance | RBXScriptConnection | (() -> ()) | any
export type Cleaner = {
	Add: <T>(self: Cleaner, item: T) -> T,
	Connect: (self: Cleaner, signal: RBXScriptSignal, fn: (...any) -> ()) -> RBXScriptConnection,
	Clean: (self: Cleaner) -> (),
}

local function dispose(item: any)
	const kind = typeof(item)
	if kind == "RBXScriptConnection" then
		if item.Connected then
			item:Disconnect()
		end
	elseif kind == "Instance" then
		item:Destroy()
	elseif kind == "function" then
		item()
	elseif kind == "table" then
		if type(item.Clean) == "function" then
			item:Clean()
		elseif type(item.Destroy) == "function" then
			item:Destroy()
		end
	end
end

function Cleaner.new(): Cleaner
	return setmetatable({ _items = {}, _cleaned = false }, Cleaner) :: any
end

function Cleaner.Add<T>(self: Cleaner, item: T): T
	assert(not (self :: any)._cleaned, "Cleaner:Clean already ran")
	const items = (self :: any)._items
	items[#items + 1] = item
	return item
end

function Cleaner.Connect(
	self: Cleaner,
	signal: RBXScriptSignal,
	fn: (...any) -> ()
): RBXScriptConnection
	return self:Add(signal:Connect(fn))
end

function Cleaner.Clean(self: Cleaner)
	const state = self :: any
	if state._cleaned then
		return
	end
	state._cleaned = true
	for index = #state._items, 1, -1 do
		dispose(state._items[index])
	end
	table.clear(state._items)
end

return Cleaner

-- probe: save-check
-- datamodel: Edit
-- params: attrs={"QaSlot"} prefixes={"Stage","Debug"} roots={game:GetService("ServerStorage"),workspace,game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")}
-- purpose: Before save_place: is anything in the Edit place that a test or stage left behind? Lists the named
--   test attributes (attrs) and any attribute starting with one of prefixes on the roots, and says whether a
--   playtest is running. Ends with "safe to save_place: yes" or "no" and why. RobloxForge cannot block the MCP's
--   save_place itself: run this first, and clear what it lists. Set attrs to your project's own slot names.
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local ATTRS, PREFIXES, ROOTS = {{attrs}}, {{prefixes}}, {{roots}}
local named = {}
for _, a in ATTRS do
	named[a] = true
end
local found = {}
for _, root in ROOTS do
	for name, value in root:GetAttributes() do
		local hit = named[name]
		if not hit then
			for _, prefix in PREFIXES do
				if string.sub(name, 1, #prefix) == prefix then
					hit = true
					break
				end
			end
		end
		if hit then
			table.insert(found, string.format("%s.%s = %s", root:GetFullName(), name, tostring(value)))
		end
	end
end
table.sort(found)
local playing = RunService:IsRunning()
local why = {}
if playing then
	table.insert(why, "a playtest is running (save from Edit after Stop)")
end
if #found > 0 then
	table.insert(why, #found .. " test attribute(s) set: clear them in Edit first")
end
local out = { "save-check:" }
for _, line in found do
	table.insert(out, "  " .. line)
end
table.insert(out, "safe to save_place: " .. (if #why == 0 then "yes" else "no - " .. table.concat(why, "; ")))
return table.concat(out, "\n")

--!strict
--[[
	What the driver sends, and the check on it.

	Getting *in* is not here: that is a `ProximityPrompt`, which is already a
	server-side event with the player attached, so an enter remote would be a
	second way to do a thing the engine does properly.

	## Why the aim is a direction

	The turret follows where the camera is looking, and a camera pointed at the
	sky is not looking *at* anything. Sending the point the view happens to hit
	would make the gun swing to the horizon whenever the camera cleared the
	scenery, which reads as the turret losing its mind. A unit direction is what
	the turret is actually matching.
]]

local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local Remotes = {}

export type Input = {
	--- −1..1, along the hull's own forward.
	throttle: number,
	--- −1..1, positive turns right.
	steer: number,
	--- Unit vector, in world space: where the camera is looking.
	aim: Vector3,
}

local INPUT = "TankInput"
local EXIT = "TankExit"

local function event(name: string): RemoteEvent
	if RunService:IsServer() then
		local existing = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(name)
		if existing and existing:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
			return existing
		end
		local remote = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
		remote.Name = name
		remote.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
		return remote
	end
	return ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild(name) :: RemoteEvent
end

function Remotes.input(): RemoteEvent
	return event(INPUT)
end

--- Getting out. Carries nothing; who sent it is the whole message.
function Remotes.exit(): RemoteEvent
	return event(EXIT)
end

--[[
	Whether a packet is the shape this build expects.

	A client can send anything at all, so every field is checked before it
	reaches the controller. `aim` in particular ends up in the turret joint's
	`C0`, and a NaN there leaves the model drawn at no position anybody can
	find — `v ~= v` is the only test for one.
]]
function Remotes.valid(packet: unknown): boolean
	if typeof(packet) ~= "table" then
		return false
	end
	local input = packet :: Input
	if typeof(input.throttle) ~= "number" or input.throttle ~= input.throttle then
		return false
	end
	if typeof(input.steer) ~= "number" or input.steer ~= input.steer then
		return false
	end
	if typeof(input.aim) ~= "Vector3" or input.aim ~= input.aim then
		return false
	end
	-- A zero vector has no direction to follow and would normalise to NaN.
	return input.aim.Magnitude > 1e-4
end

return Remotes

--!nonstrict
-- Components.lua -- small themed building blocks. Every creator takes a Cleaner
-- and parents to a given container; all instances register for cleanup.
-- Theme defaults apply FIRST so caller props always win.

const Theme = require(script.Parent.Theme)

const Components = {}

export type InstanceProps = { [string]: any }

local function base<T>(instance: T, defaults: InstanceProps, props: InstanceProps?, cleaner: any): T
	const target = instance :: any
	for key, value in defaults do
		target[key] = value
	end
	for key, value in props or {} do
		target[key] = value
	end
	cleaner:Add(instance)
	return instance
end

function Components.Panel(cleaner: any, parent: Instance, props: InstanceProps?): Frame
	const frame = base(Instance.new("Frame"), {
		BackgroundColor3 = Theme.Colors.Surface,
		BorderSizePixel = 0,
	}, props, cleaner)
	const corner = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("UICorner"))
	corner.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, Theme.Sizes.Corner)
	corner.Parent = frame
	frame.Parent = parent
	return frame
end

function Components.Label(cleaner: any, parent: Instance, props: InstanceProps?): TextLabel
	const label = base(Instance.new("TextLabel"), {
		BackgroundTransparency = 1,
		Font = Theme.Fonts.Ui,
		TextSize = Theme.Sizes.BodyText,
		TextColor3 = Theme.Colors.Text,
		Text = "",
	}, props, cleaner)
	label.Parent = parent
	return label
end

function Components.Button(
	cleaner: any,
	parent: Instance,
	text: string,
	onClick: (() -> ())?
): TextButton
	const button = base(Instance.new("TextButton"), {
		Text = text,
		Font = Theme.Fonts.UiBold,
		TextSize = Theme.Sizes.BodyText,
		TextColor3 = Theme.Colors.Text,
		BackgroundColor3 = Theme.Colors.SurfaceRaised,
		BorderSizePixel = 0,
		AutoButtonColor = true,
	}, nil, cleaner)
	const corner = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("UICorner"))
	corner.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, Theme.Sizes.Corner)
	corner.Parent = button
	if onClick then
		cleaner:Connect(button.MouseButton1Click, onClick)
	end
	button.Parent = parent
	return button
end

return Components

-- probe: scene-audit
-- datamodel: any
-- params: root=workspace
-- purpose: One-pass health check of a place for the traps that most often break agent-built games. Every line is a
--   lead to read, not a verdict.
local root = {{root}}
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local counts, leads = {}, {}
local function bump(k) counts[k] = (counts[k] or 0) + 1 end
local function lead(k, inst, why)
	bump(k)
	if counts[k] <= 3 then table.insert(leads, string.format("[%s] %s - %s", k, inst:GetFullName(), why)) end
end
local function inCharacter(inst)
	local m = inst:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
	while m do
		if Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(m) or m:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") then return true end
		m = m:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
	end
	return false
end
for _, d in root:GetDescendants() do
	if d:IsA("BasePart") then
		bump("parts")
		if not d.Anchored and not inCharacter(d) and #d:GetJoints() == 0 then lead("loose", d, "unanchored and unwelded: it will fall or drift") end
		if d.CanCollide and d.Transparency >= 0.99 and not inCharacter(d) then lead("invisible-wall", d, "invisible but collidable") end
		if d.Size.Magnitude > 2048 then lead("huge", d, "very large part: physics/streaming cost") end
	elseif d:IsA("LocalScript") and not inCharacter(d) then
		lead("localscript-in-world", d, "LocalScripts do not run in Workspace unless inside a player's character")
	elseif d:IsA("Sound") and d.SoundId == "" then
		lead("silent-sound", d, "Sound with no SoundId")
	elseif (d:IsA("ImageLabel") or d:IsA("ImageButton")) and d.Image == "" and d.BackgroundTransparency >= 1 then
		lead("blank-image", d, "image element with no Image and no background: draws nothing")
	elseif d:IsA("Decal") and d.Texture == "" then
		lead("blank-decal", d, "Decal with no Texture")
	elseif d:IsA("SurfaceGui") and not d.ClipsDescendants then
		bump("surfacegui-unclipped")
	elseif d:IsA("PointLight") or d:IsA("SpotLight") or d:IsA("SurfaceLight") then
		bump("lights")
		if d.Shadows then bump("shadow-lights") end
	elseif d:IsA("ParticleEmitter") and d.Enabled then
		bump("emitters")
	end
end
for _, s in game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):GetDescendants() do
	if s:IsA("Script") and s.RunContext == Enum.RunContext.Legacy then lead("script-in-replicated", s, "server Scripts do not run in ReplicatedStorage") end
end
for _, s in game:GetService("ServerScriptService"):GetDescendants() do
	if s:IsA("LocalScript") then lead("localscript-on-server", s, "LocalScripts never run in ServerScriptService") end
end
local summary = {}
for k, v in counts do table.insert(summary, k .. "=" .. v) end
table.sort(summary)
table.insert(leads, 1, "counts: " .. table.concat(summary, "  "))
table.insert(leads, 2, "StreamingEnabled=" .. tostring(workspace.StreamingEnabled) .. "  Gravity=" .. workspace.Gravity)
if (counts["shadow-lights"] or 0) > 40 then table.insert(leads, "PERF: more than 40 shadow-casting lights") end
if (counts["surfacegui-unclipped"] or 0) > 0 then table.insert(leads, "NOTE: unclipped SurfaceGuis - run gui-overflow if anything shows where it should not") end
return table.concat(leads, "\n")

--!nonstrict
-- Turns the raw Roblox import of a Blender export into the normalized art Model.
-- Headless (Lune): it trusts neither the importer's axes nor its units; it derives scale
-- and yaw from report.json and fails with ART_AXIS_MISMATCH when no yaw fits.
local roblox = require("@lune/roblox")
local AssetSpec = require("./AssetSpec")
local Config = require("./Config")
local Paths = require("./Paths")

local CFrame, Color3, Content, Enum, Instance, Vector3 =
	roblox.CFrame, roblox.Color3, roblox.Content, roblox.Enum, roblox.Instance, roblox.Vector3

local Normalize = {}

local function vectorOf(values: { number }): any
	return Vector3.new(values[1], values[2], values[3])
end

local function rawBounds(meshParts: { any }): (any, any)
	local low, high = nil, nil
	for _, part in ipairs(meshParts) do
		local half = part.Size / 2
		for _, sx in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
			for _, sy in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
				for _, sz in ipairs({ -1, 1 }) do
					local corner = part.CFrame * Vector3.new(half.X * sx, half.Y * sy, half.Z * sz)
					low = if low == nil
						then corner
						else Vector3.new(
							math.min(low.X, corner.X),
							math.min(low.Y, corner.Y),
							math.min(low.Z, corner.Z)
						)
					high = if high == nil
						then corner
						else Vector3.new(
							math.max(high.X, corner.X),
							math.max(high.Y, corner.Y),
							math.max(high.Z, corner.Z)
						)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return low, high
end

-- Tries one yaw candidate: every part centre and size must land on its report object.
local function fits(
	pairsList: { any },
	yaw: number,
	scale: number,
	rawCentre: any,
	reportCentre: any,
	tolerance: number
)
	local rotation = CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(yaw), 0)
	for _, pair in ipairs(pairsList) do
		local part, object = pair.part, pair.object
		local mapped = rotation * ((part.CFrame.Position - rawCentre) * scale) + reportCentre
		local center = vectorOf(object.center)
		if
			math.abs(mapped.X - center.X) > tolerance
			or math.abs(mapped.Y - center.Y) > tolerance
			or math.abs(mapped.Z - center.Z) > tolerance
		then
			return false
		end
		local _, _, _, r00, r01, r02, r10, r11, r12, r20, r21, r22 = (rotation * part.CFrame):GetComponents()
		local size = part.Size * scale
		local extents = {
			math.abs(r00) * size.X + math.abs(r01) * size.Y + math.abs(r02) * size.Z,
			math.abs(r10) * size.X + math.abs(r11) * size.Y + math.abs(r12) * size.Z,
			math.abs(r20) * size.X + math.abs(r21) * size.Y + math.abs(r22) * size.Z,
		}
		for axis = 1, 3 do
			if math.abs(extents[axis] - object.size[axis]) > tolerance then
				return false
			end
		end
	end
	return true
end

local function materialOf(name: string): any
	local ok, material = pcall(function()
		return Enum.Material[name]
	end)
	return if ok then material else nil
end

-- Returns model, nil, nil, { yaw, scale } or nil, code, detail.
function Normalize.normalize(
	raw: { any },
	report: any,
	spec: any,
	palette: any,
	importYaw: number
): (any, string?, string?, any)
	-- 1. Scripts are never allowed in art; 2. only MeshParts survive.
	local meshParts = {}
	local function visit(instance: any): string?
		if instance:IsA("LuaSourceContainer") then
			return instance.Name
		end
		if instance:IsA("MeshPart") then
			table.insert(meshParts, instance)
		end
		return nil
	end
	for _, root in ipairs(raw) do
		local found = visit(root)
		if found then
			return nil, "ART_SCRIPT_FOUND", found
		end
		for _, descendant in ipairs(root:GetDescendants()) do
			found = visit(descendant)
			if found then
				return nil, "ART_SCRIPT_FOUND", found
			end
		end
	end

	-- 3. Match MeshParts to report objects by name, then check palette keys.
	local remaining = {}
	for _, object in ipairs(report.objects) do
		remaining[object.name] = object
	end
	local matched = {}
	for _, part in ipairs(meshParts) do
		local object = remaining[part.Name]
		if object == nil then
			return nil, "ART_UNKNOWN_PART", part.Name
		end
		remaining[part.Name] = nil
		table.insert(matched, { part = part, object = object })
	end
	for _, object in ipairs(report.objects) do
		if remaining[object.name] ~= nil then
			return nil, "ART_MISSING_PART", object.name
		end
	end
	for _, pair in ipairs(matched) do
		local partName, key = string.match(pair.object.name, "^(.-)__(.+)$")
		local entry = key and palette[key]
		if partName == nil or entry == nil or materialOf(entry.material) == nil then
			return nil, "ART_UNKNOWN_PALETTE", tostring(key or pair.object.name)
		end
		pair.partName = partName
		pair.entry = entry
	end

	-- 4. Budget.
	local maxTriangles, maxMeshParts = AssetSpec.limits(spec)
	if report.triangles > maxTriangles then
		return nil, "ART_BUDGET", string.format("triangles %d > %d", report.triangles, maxTriangles)
	end
	if #meshParts > maxMeshParts then
		return nil, "ART_BUDGET", string.format("meshParts %d > %d", #meshParts, maxMeshParts)
	end

	-- Required attachments are checked before anything is built.
	for _, name in ipairs(AssetSpec.requiredAttachments(spec)) do
		if report.attachments[name] == nil then
			return nil, "ART_MISSING_ATTACHMENT", name
		end
	end

	-- 5. Scale from the Y extent, then the first yaw that maps every part onto the report.
	local low, high = rawBounds(meshParts)
	local rawSize = high - low
	if rawSize.Y <= 1e-6 then
		return nil, "ART_AXIS_MISMATCH", "raw model has no height"
	end
	local scale = report.size[2] / rawSize.Y
	local rawCentre = (low + high) / 2
	local reportCentre = (vectorOf(report.bboxMin) + vectorOf(report.bboxMax)) / 2
	local tolerance =
		math.max(Config.MATCH_ABS, Config.MATCH_REL * math.max(report.size[1], report.size[2], report.size[3]))
	local candidates, seen = {}, {}
	for _, yaw in ipairs({ importYaw, 0, 90, 180, 270 }) do
		if not seen[yaw] then
			seen[yaw] = true
			table.insert(candidates, yaw)
		end
	end
	local detected = nil
	for _, yaw in ipairs(candidates) do
		if fits(matched, yaw, scale, rawCentre, reportCentre, tolerance) then
			detected = yaw
			break
		end
	end
	if detected == nil then
		return nil, "ART_AXIS_MISMATCH", string.format("no yaw of %s fits the report", table.concat(candidates, ", "))
	end
	local rotation = CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(detected), 0)

	-- 6. Build the normalized model.
	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = Paths.leaf(spec.artPath)
	local artRoot = Instance.new("Part")
	artRoot.Name = "ArtRoot"
	artRoot.Size = Vector3.new(Config.ART_ROOT_SIZE, Config.ART_ROOT_SIZE, Config.ART_ROOT_SIZE)
	artRoot.CFrame = CFrame.identity
	artRoot.Transparency = 1
	artRoot.CanCollide = false
	artRoot.CanQuery = false
	artRoot.CanTouch = false
	artRoot.Anchored = true
	artRoot.Parent = model
	model.PrimaryPart = artRoot

	local hasColliders = #report.colliders > 0
	for _, pair in ipairs(matched) do
		local part = pair.part
		local position = rotation * ((part.CFrame.Position - rawCentre) * scale) + reportCentre
		local rawRotation = part.CFrame.Rotation
		local size = part.Size * scale
		part:ClearAllChildren()
		part.Parent = nil
		part.Name = pair.partName
		part.Size = size
		part.CFrame = CFrame.new(position) * rotation * rawRotation
		part.Color = Color3.fromRGB(pair.entry.rgb[1], pair.entry.rgb[2], pair.entry.rgb[3])
		part.Material = materialOf(pair.entry.material)
		part.TextureContent = Content.none
		part.Anchored = true
		part.CastShadow = true
		part.CollisionFidelity = Enum.CollisionFidelity.Box
		part.CanCollide = not hasColliders
		part.Parent = model
	end

	for _, collider in ipairs(report.colliders) do
		local box = Instance.new("Part")
		box.Name = "Collider_" .. collider.name
		box.Size = vectorOf(collider.size)
		box.CFrame = CFrame.new(vectorOf(collider.center))
		box.Transparency = 1
		box.CanCollide = true
		box.CanQuery = false
		box.CanTouch = false
		box.Anchored = true
		box.Parent = model
	end

	local names = {}
	for name in pairs(report.attachments) do
		table.insert(names, name)
	end
	table.sort(names)
	for _, name in ipairs(names) do
		local attachment = Instance.new("Attachment")
		attachment.Name = name
		attachment.Position = vectorOf(report.attachments[name])
		attachment.Parent = artRoot
	end

	model:SetAttribute("ArtAssetId", Paths.leaf(spec.artPath))
	model:SetAttribute("ArtPath", spec.artPath)
	model:SetAttribute("ArtSource", "blender")
	model:SetAttribute("ArtVersion", spec.version)
	model:SetAttribute("ArtTier", spec.tier)
	return model, nil, nil, { yaw = detected, scale = scale }
end

return Normalize

--!strict
--[[
	Finding the parts and joints the controller drives, once, and saying so
	loudly when one is missing.

	The rig is surveyed in `examples/m103/NOTES.md`; this is that survey turned
	into code. Three joints matter and everything else on the tank is decoration
	hanging off one of two roots:

		Hull.Hull --[Main]--> Turret.Main --[Mantlet]--> Weapon.Mantlet
		                                                     |
		                                                  [Gun] --> Weapon.Gun

	Traverse turns the `Main` joint, elevation turns the `Mantlet` joint, and the
	`Gun` joint is never touched — the barrel rides the mantlet, which is the
	whole reason the mantlet is in the chain.

	Both are turned by writing **`C0`**, composed onto the rest pose captured
	here. The obvious property is `Transform`, which exists for exactly this and
	which the animation system uses — but `Transform` is not a replicated
	property, so a turret turned that way on the server is a turret the people
	watching may not see move. `C0` replicates, and a demo that only works in one
	window is not a demo.

	## Why this is a separate module

	Because the failure it guards against is silence. A `FindFirstChild` chain
	written inline returns `nil` and the controller then does nothing at all,
	with no error and no clue: a tank that sits still looks exactly like a tank
	whose input is not arriving. Resolving the whole rig up front turns that into
	one message naming the part that is missing.
]]

local Rig = {}

export type Tank = {
	model: Model,
	--- Anchored, and what approach C writes a CFrame to every frame.
	hull: BasePart,
	--- The invisible pivot the turret's decoration hangs from.
	turret: BasePart,
	mantlet: BasePart,
	gun: BasePart,
	--- Rotated about Y to traverse.
	traverse: Motor6D,
	--- Rotated about X to elevate. The mantlet and the gun both follow it.
	elevate: Motor6D,
	--[[
		Each joint's `C0` as the model was built, before anything turned it.

		Aiming multiplies the rotation onto these rather than onto whatever the
		joint currently holds, so the angles are absolute and a frame that is
		skipped or repeated cannot make the turret drift. Composing onto the
		current value would integrate every rounding error the run produces.
	]]
	traverseRest: CFrame,
	elevateRest: CFrame,
	leftTrack: BasePart,
	rightTrack: BasePart,
	--[[
		How far the hull's centre sits above the bottom of its tracks.

		Measured from the model rather than written down, because the tank has
		already been rescaled once — every offset in it doubled between two
		saves — and a hard-coded ride height would have survived that silently
		and left the tank buried to its sponsons.
	]]
	rideHeight: number,
	--- Half the distance between the two tracks, for the turning arithmetic.
	halfTrackWidth: number,
	--- +1 if LeftTrack really is on the model's left. Read, not assumed.
	leftSign: number,
}

local function need(parent: Instance, name: string, class: string): Instance
	local child = parent:FindFirstChild(name)
	if not child then
		error(`{parent:GetFullName()} has no "{name}"`, 0)
	end
	if not child:IsA(class) then
		error(`{child:GetFullName()} is a {child.ClassName}, expected a {class}`, 0)
	end
	return child
end

function Rig.resolve(model: Model): Tank
	local hullModel = need(model, "Hull", "Model")
	local turretModel = need(model, "Turret", "Model")
	local weapon = need(turretModel, "Weapon", "Model")

	local hull = need(hullModel, "Hull", "BasePart") :: BasePart
	local turret = need(turretModel, "Main", "BasePart") :: BasePart
	local mantlet = need(weapon, "Mantlet", "BasePart") :: BasePart
	local gun = need(weapon, "Gun", "BasePart") :: BasePart
	local leftTrack = need(hullModel, "LeftTrack", "BasePart") :: BasePart
	local rightTrack = need(hullModel, "RightTrack", "BasePart") :: BasePart
	local traverse = need(hull, "Main", "Motor6D") :: Motor6D
	local elevate = need(turret, "Mantlet", "Motor6D") :: Motor6D

	local rig: Tank = {
		model = model,
		hull = hull,
		turret = turret,
		mantlet = mantlet,
		gun = gun,
		traverse = traverse,
		elevate = elevate,
		traverseRest = traverse.C0,
		elevateRest = elevate.C0,
		leftTrack = leftTrack,
		rightTrack = rightTrack,
		rideHeight = (hull.Position.Y - leftTrack.Position.Y) + leftTrack.Size.Y / 2,
		halfTrackWidth = (rightTrack.Position - leftTrack.Position).Magnitude / 2,
		-- Which side each track is on comes from the hull's own axes rather than
		-- from the name. The model has been rebuilt twice already, and a tank
		-- whose tracks scroll the wrong way when it turns is a bug nobody thinks
		-- to look for in a variable called `leftTrack`.
		leftSign = if hull.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(leftTrack.Position).X < 0 then 1 else -1,
	}

	-- The joints were built in Studio and could be pointed anywhere. Checking
	-- costs nothing on the one frame it runs and catches a rig edit that looks
	-- right in the explorer and moves the wrong part.
	local function drives(joint: Motor6D): string
		return if joint.Part1 then joint.Part1.Name else "nothing"
	end
	if rig.traverse.Part1 ~= turret then
		error(`the Main joint drives {drives(rig.traverse)}, not Turret.Main`, 0)
	end
	if rig.elevate.Part1 ~= mantlet then
		error(`the Mantlet joint drives {drives(rig.elevate)}, not Weapon.Mantlet`, 0)
	end

	-- The chain's last link, which nothing writes to and everything depends on.
	-- It was wrong once — the gun hung off `Main` and pivoted about its own
	-- middle — and the symptom was a barrel that swung out of its mantlet, which
	-- reads as an elevation bug rather than as a parenting one.
	local gunJoint = need(mantlet, "Gun", "Motor6D") :: Motor6D
	if gunJoint.Part0 ~= mantlet or gunJoint.Part1 ~= gun then
		error(`the Gun joint does not hang Weapon.Gun off Weapon.Mantlet`, 0)
	end

	if not hull.Anchored then
		error(`{hull:GetFullName()} must stay anchored — approach C writes its CFrame directly`, 0)
	end

	return rig
end

--[[
	What the tank's own raycasts should pass through: all of it.

	The whole model rather than a list of parts, because it carries a query-only
	`CollisionBox` around the hull as well as the parts you can see. The ground
	probe drops from above the tank, so anything of the tank's left in the filter
	is something the probe lands on — and the tank then rides on its own turret.
]]
function Rig.ownParts(rig: Tank): { Instance }
	return { rig.model }
end

return Rig

--!nonstrict
-- State.lua -- minimal observable value: Get/Set/Subscribe for UI bindings.

const State = {}
State.__index = State

export type State<T> = {
	Get: (self: State<T>) -> T,
	Set: (self: State<T>, value: T) -> (),
	Subscribe: (self: State<T>, fn: (T) -> ()) -> () -> (),
}

function State.new<T>(initial: T): State<T>
	return setmetatable({ _value = initial, _subs = {} }, State) :: any
end

function State.Get<T>(self: State<T>): T
	return (self :: any)._value
end

function State.Set<T>(self: State<T>, value: T)
	const state = self :: any
	if state._value == value then
		return
	end
	state._value = value
	for _, callback in table.clone(state._subs) do
		callback(value)
	end
end

function State.Subscribe<T>(self: State<T>, fn: (T) -> ()): () -> ()
	const state = self :: any
	state._subs[#state._subs + 1] = fn
	fn(state._value)
	return function()
		const index = table.find(state._subs, fn)
		if index then
			table.remove(state._subs, index)
		end
	end
end

return State

-- probe: sound-audit
-- datamodel: Client
-- params: seconds=4 extra=""
-- purpose: Which sounds will actually play? Collects every SoundId the place refers to (Sound instances, plus ids
--   written in script sources and any comma-separated `extra` ids), loads each one muted and reports the ones that
--   never load. A missing sound raises no error - it is just silent - so "the gun sounds are gone" needs this.
--   It also flags rbxasset:// files that are not stock Roblox content: those live in the versioned Studio install
--   folder, vanish on every Studio update and never exist for real players.
local SoundService = game:GetService("SoundService")
local ids, order = {}, {}
local function add(id)
	if type(id) == "string" and id ~= "" and not ids[id] then
		ids[id] = true
		order[#order + 1] = id
	end
end
local roots = { workspace, SoundService, game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"), game:GetService("ReplicatedFirst"),
	game:GetService("StarterGui"), game:GetService("StarterPack"), game:GetService("StarterPlayer") }
for _, root in roots do
	for _, d in root:GetDescendants() do
		if d:IsA("Sound") then
			add(d.SoundId)
		elseif d:IsA("LuaSourceContainer") then
			local ok, src = pcall(function()
				return d.Source
			end)
			if ok and type(src) == "string" then
				for _, ext in { "wav", "mp3", "ogg" } do
					for id in src:gmatch("rbxasset://[%w_/%.%- ]+%." .. ext) do
						add(id)
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
end
for id in string.gmatch({{extra}}, "[^,]+") do
	add((id:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")))
end
local probes = {}
for _, id in order do
	local s = Instance.new("Sound")
	s.Name, s.SoundId, s.Volume = "ForgeSoundAudit", id, 0
	s.Parent = SoundService
	probes[id] = s
end
task.wait({{seconds}})
local missing, localOnly, loaded = {}, {}, 0
for _, id in order do
	local s = probes[id]
	if s.IsLoaded and s.TimeLength > 0 then
		loaded += 1
	else
		missing[#missing + 1] = id
	end
	-- Stock content sits directly in sounds/; a subfolder is something a tool copied into this install.
	if id:match("^rbxasset://sounds/[^/]+/") then
		localOnly[#localOnly + 1] = id
	end
	s:Destroy()
end
local out = { string.format("%d sound ids, %d load, %d do NOT load", #order, loaded, #missing) }
for _, id in missing do
	out[#out + 1] = "NOT LOADED  " .. id
end
if #localOnly > 0 then
	out[#out + 1] = string.format(
		"%d id(s) are local Studio content (rbxasset://sounds/<folder>/...): wiped by a Studio update and absent for players; upload them as audio assets before shipping. First: %s",
		#localOnly, localOnly[1])
end
return table.concat(out, "\n")

--!nonstrict
-- Open Cloud Assets upload and Asset Delivery download for the art pipeline.
-- HTTP and sleeping are injected as deps = { request, sleep } so tests can fake them.
--   request({ url, method, headers, body }) -> { status, body, headers } or nil, message
--   sleep(seconds)
-- Every function returns a result, or nil plus a code and a detail. The API key goes only
-- into request headers; it is scrubbed from every returned detail.
local serde = require("@lune/serde")
local Config = require("./Config")

local OpenCloud = {}

export type Session = { apiKey: string, creator: { userId: string?, groupId: string? } }

local MAX_BODY_DETAIL = 200

local function clip(session: Session, body: any): string
	local text = tostring(body or "")
	if session.apiKey ~= "" then
		local escaped = string.gsub(session.apiKey, "%p", "%%%0")
		text = string.gsub(text, escaped, "***")
	end
	if #text > MAX_BODY_DETAIL then
		text = string.sub(text, 1, MAX_BODY_DETAIL)
	end
	return text
end

local function header(response: any, name: string): string?
	for key, value in pairs(response.headers or {}) do
		if string.lower(key) == name then
			return value
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function decode(text: string): any
	local ok, value = pcall(serde.decode, "json", text)
	return if ok and type(value) == "table" then value else nil
end

local function randomHex(length: number): string
	local digits = {}
	for index = 1, length do
		digits[index] = string.format("%x", math.random(0, 15))
	end
	return table.concat(digits)
end

local function multipart(boundary: string, requestJson: string, fbx: string): string
	return table.concat({
		"--" .. boundary,
		'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="request"',
		"Content-Type: application/json",
		"",
		requestJson,
		"--" .. boundary,
		'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="fileContent"; filename="model.fbx"',
		"Content-Type: model/fbx",
		"",
		fbx,
		"--" .. boundary .. "--",
		"",
	}, "\r\n")
end

local function assetIdText(value: any): string?
	if type(value) == "number" then
		return string.format("%.0f", value)
	end
	if type(value) == "string" and value ~= "" then
		return value
	end
	return nil
end

-- POST the FBX, then poll the operation until the model asset id is known.
function OpenCloud.upload(
	deps: any,
	session: Session,
	artPath: string,
	displayName: string,
	fbx: string
): (string?, string?, string?)
	local boundary = "gameart" .. randomHex(16)
	local requestJson = serde.encode("json", {
		assetType = "Model",
		displayName = displayName,
		description = "the game art: " .. artPath,
		creationContext = { creator = session.creator },
	})
	local retries = 0
	local response
	while true do
		local transportError
		response, transportError = deps.request({
			url = Config.ASSETS_URL,
			method = "POST",
			headers = {
				["x-api-key"] = session.apiKey,
				["Content-Type"] = "multipart/form-data; boundary=" .. boundary,
			},
			body = multipart(boundary, requestJson, fbx),
		})
		if response == nil then
			-- The upload may have reached Roblox: never retry, check the Creator Dashboard.
			return nil, "ART_UPLOAD_AMBIGUOUS", clip(session, transportError)
		end
		if response.status == 429 and retries < Config.MAX_RATE_RETRIES then
			retries += 1
			deps.sleep(tonumber(header(response, "retry-after")) or Config.RATE_LIMIT_WAIT)
		else
			break
		end
	end
	if response.status ~= 200 then
		return nil, "ART_UPLOAD_FAILED", string.format("%s %s", tostring(response.status), clip(session, response.body))
	end

	local operation = decode(response.body)
	if operation == nil then
		return nil, "ART_UPLOAD_FAILED", "200 " .. clip(session, response.body)
	end
	local operationId = operation.operationId or string.match(tostring(operation.path or ""), "operations/(.+)$")
	for _ = 1, Config.MAX_POLLS do
		if operation.done == true then
			if operation.error ~= nil then
				return nil, "ART_UPLOAD_FAILED", clip(session, serde.encode("json", operation.error))
			end
			local assetId = assetIdText(operation.response and operation.response.assetId)
			if assetId == nil then
				return nil, "ART_UPLOAD_FAILED", "operation finished without an assetId"
			end
			return assetId, nil, nil
		end
		if operationId == nil then
			return nil, "ART_UPLOAD_FAILED", "no operation id in the upload response"
		end
		deps.sleep(Config.POLL_SECONDS)
		local poll = deps.request({
			url = Config.OPERATIONS_URL .. operationId,
			method = "GET",
			headers = { ["x-api-key"] = session.apiKey },
		})
		if poll ~= nil then
			if poll.status ~= 200 then
				return nil, "ART_UPLOAD_FAILED", string.format("%s %s", tostring(poll.status), clip(session, poll.body))
			end
			operation = decode(poll.body) or { done = false }
		end
	end
	return nil,
		"ART_UPLOAD_TIMEOUT",
		string.format("operation %s not done after %d polls", tostring(operationId), Config.MAX_POLLS)
end

-- Delivery API: the JSON answer names a CDN location that holds the processed model bytes.
function OpenCloud.download(deps: any, session: Session, assetId: string): (string?, string?, string?)
	local lastStatus = "no response"
	for attempt = 1, Config.DOWNLOAD_RETRIES do
		local delivery = deps.request({
			url = Config.DELIVERY_URL .. assetId,
			method = "GET",
			headers = { ["x-api-key"] = session.apiKey },
		})
		if delivery ~= nil then
			lastStatus = tostring(delivery.status)
			local location = delivery.status == 200 and decode(delivery.body)
			if location and type(location.location) == "string" then
				local file = deps.request({ url = location.location, method = "GET", headers = {} })
				if file ~= nil then
					lastStatus = tostring(file.status)
					if file.status == 200 then
						return file.body, nil, nil
					end
				end
			end
		end
		if attempt < Config.DOWNLOAD_RETRIES then
			deps.sleep(Config.DOWNLOAD_WAIT)
		end
	end
	return nil, "ART_DOWNLOAD_FAILED", string.format("asset %s, last status %s", assetId, lastStatus)
end

-- "user:123" or "group:456" -> the creator table of the upload request.
function OpenCloud.parseCreator(text: string?): { userId: string?, groupId: string? }?
	local kind, id = string.match(text or "", "^(%l+):(%d+)$")
	if kind == "user" then
		return { userId = id }
	elseif kind == "group" then
		return { groupId = id }
	end
	return nil
end

return OpenCloud

-- OTHER TORTIOUS ACTION, ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE USE OR
-- PERFORMANCE OF THIS SOFTWARE.

--!strict
--[[
	The M103, driven server-side. Approach C, as settled in
	`examples/m103/NOTES.md`: the hull stays anchored and has its `CFrame`
	written each frame onto whatever a downward raycast finds, and the turret and
	gun are joints whose rotation is written.

	**This is the baseline.** It exists to be rebuilt as a Roswaal graph and
	compared — so it is written the way a competent Roblox developer would write
	it, not the way a graph would force. Where an idiom has no obvious equivalent
	in nodes, there is a `-- graph:` note beside it; those notes are the raw
	material for `docs/demo/CONVERSION-LOG.md` and are the actual point of the
	exercise.

	## The shape a developer expects

	Walk up, a prompt appears, press E, and you are behind the tank with the gun
	pointed where you look. That is the tank demo everybody has already played,
	and matching it is deliberate: the demo has to be recognisable before
	anything it demonstrates is worth reading.

	## Why the server

	The hull is anchored, so the server writing its `CFrame` replicates for free,
	and so do the two joints. No physics, no ownership handoff.

	**There is no client-side prediction, on purpose.** A shipping game would
	drive the hull locally and reconcile; that is a networking exercise, it
	roughly doubles the code, and none of it says anything about whether a node
	graph can express a tank. In Studio, where this runs, the round trip is not
	visible.

	## What is deliberately not here

	- **Firing, damage and armour penetration.** Cut on the author's call: the
	  demo is about getting in and driving, and a gun would be a second system to
	  convert that repeats what the turret already proves.
	- **More than one tank, and more than one seat.** One model, one driver.
]]

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

-- Waited for, then indexed directly. `require(x:WaitForChild(...))` returns
-- `any`, and the types these modules export -- `Remotes.Input`, `Rig.Tank` --
-- would then not exist as far as the typechecker is concerned, quietly turning
-- every annotation below into a comment.
local Tank = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Tank")
Tank:WaitForChild("Config")
Tank:WaitForChild("Occupancy")
Tank:WaitForChild("Remotes")
Tank:WaitForChild("Rig")

local Config = require(ReplicatedStorage.Tank.Config)
local Occupancy = require(ReplicatedStorage.Tank.Occupancy)
local Remotes = require(ReplicatedStorage.Tank.Remotes)
local Rig = require(ReplicatedStorage.Tank.Rig)

local TANK_NAME = "M103"

--- How far above the tank the ground probe starts, and how far below it looks.
local PROBE_UP = 20
local PROBE_DOWN = 200

--- Seconds for the hull to take up most of a change in ground slope.
local SLOPE_SMOOTHING = 0.12

local model = workspace:WaitForChild(TANK_NAME) :: Model
local rig = Rig.resolve(model)
local config = Config.read(model)
local tuning = Config.tuning

local inputRemote = Remotes.input()
local exitRemote = Remotes.exit()
local occupantValue = Occupancy.value(model)

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- State
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

--- Turret angle relative to the hull, and gun angle relative to the turret.
local turretYaw = 0
local gunPitch = 0

--- Where each track's texture has scrolled to, in studs.
local leftScroll = 0
local rightScroll = 0

--- The surface normal the hull is currently sitting on, eased toward the real one.
local groundNormal = Vector3.yAxis

--- Studs per second along the hull's forward. Signed; negative is reverse.
local speed = 0

--- What an unoccupied tank is asking for: nothing. The aim is never read while
--- there is no driver — the turret holds where it was left — but the field has
--- to hold a direction rather than a zero vector.
local idle: Remotes.Input = {
	throttle = 0,
	steer = 0,
	aim = rig.hull.CFrame.LookVector,
}
local latest = idle

local raycast = RaycastParams.new()
raycast.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
raycast.IgnoreWater = true

--[[
	The tank, and whoever is riding in it.

	The driver is welded at the hull's centre, which is directly under the ground
	probe — so as far as this raycast is concerned they *are* part of the tank.
	`Occupancy` also turns their `CanQuery` off, and either measure alone is
	enough; both are here because the first thing anyone will want back is a
	driver you can shoot, and turning `CanQuery` on again should not silently
	make the tank fly.

	Reassigned rather than mutated: `FilterDescendantsInstances` hands back a
	copy, so appending to what it returns changes nothing at all.
]]
local function filterOut(rider: Model?)
	local list = Rig.ownParts(rig)
	if rider then
		table.insert(list, rider)
	end
	raycast.FilterDescendantsInstances = list
end

filterOut(nil)

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Getting in and out
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

local prompt = Instance.new("ProximityPrompt")
prompt.Name = "EnterTank"
prompt.ActionText = "Drive"
prompt.ObjectText = "M103"
prompt.KeyboardKeyCode = Enum.KeyCode.E
prompt.HoldDuration = 0
prompt.MaxActivationDistance = tuning.promptDistance
-- The hull is a mesh wearing a turret and a lot of trim, so half the places you
-- would stand have something between you and the prompt's anchor. Requiring
-- line of sight makes it flicker as you walk around the tank.
prompt.RequiresLineOfSight = false
prompt.Parent = rig.hull

--- The `Player` driving, or nil. `occupantValue` is the copy clients can see.
local driver: Player? = nil

local function characterOf(player: Player): Model?
	local character = player.Character
	return if character and character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid") then character else nil
end

--- Beside the left track, facing away, on the ground the tank is standing on.
local function exitCFrame(): CFrame
	local beside = rig.hull.CFrame * CFrame.new(-(rig.halfTrackWidth + 4), 0, 0)
	return CFrame.lookAt(beside.Position, beside.Position - rig.hull.CFrame.RightVector * 10)
end

local function leave()
	local player = driver
	driver = nil
	latest = idle
	occupantValue.Value = nil
	prompt.Enabled = true
	filterOut(nil)
	if not player then
		return
	end
	local character = characterOf(player)
	if character then
		Occupancy.show(character, exitCFrame())
	end
end

prompt.Triggered:Connect(function(player: Player)
	if driver ~= nil then
		return
	end
	local character = characterOf(player)
	if not character then
		return
	end
	if not Occupancy.hide(character, rig.hull) then
		return
	end
	driver = player
	latest = idle
	occupantValue.Value = player
	prompt.Enabled = false
	filterOut(character)
end)

exitRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player)
	if player == driver then
		leave()
	end
end)

-- Every way a driver stops being one without pressing anything. Missing any of
-- these leaves a tank nobody can get into and a prompt that never comes back.
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	if player == driver then
		leave()
	end
end)

local function watch(player: Player)
	player.CharacterRemoving:Connect(function()
		if player == driver then
			leave()
		end
	end)
end

for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
	watch(player)
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(watch)

inputRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, packet)
	-- graph: two guards, and a graph that omits either is exploitable rather
	-- than merely wrong. Worth watching whether the node version makes them easy
	-- to forget.
	if player ~= driver then
		return
	end
	if not Remotes.valid(packet) then
		return
	end
	local input = packet :: Remotes.Input
	latest = {
		throttle = math.clamp(input.throttle, -1, 1),
		steer = math.clamp(input.steer, -1, 1),
		aim = input.aim.Unit,
	}
end)

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Maths
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[[
	Moves `current` toward `target` by at most `maxStep`, the short way round.

	The wrap is the part that matters. Without it a turret crossing the rear arc
	takes the long way and sweeps 350 degrees to reach something two degrees off
	its left shoulder.
]]
local function stepAngle(current: number, target: number, maxStep: number): number
	local delta = (target - current + math.pi) % (2 * math.pi) - math.pi
	return current + math.clamp(delta, -maxStep, maxStep)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The frame
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[[
	Winds `speed` toward what the throttle is asking for.

	A tank does not have a speed, it has a *throttle*, and the difference is the
	whole feel of driving one: sixty tons takes five seconds to reach full pace
	and rather less to lose it, so letting go of W coasts rather than stops.

	Two rates rather than one, because accelerating and braking are different
	systems on a real vehicle and behave differently — and because a tank that
	slowed as reluctantly as it sped up would be miserable to park.
]]
local function accelerate(dt: number): number
	local top = config.movementSpeed
		* (if latest.throttle < 0 then tuning.reverseFraction else 1)
	local target = latest.throttle * top

	-- Braking is anything that reduces the gap to zero: letting off, and also
	-- pushing the other way, which on a tank is the same set of brakes before it
	-- is a gear change.
	local closing = math.abs(target) < math.abs(speed) or target * speed < 0
	local seconds = if closing then tuning.brakingTime else tuning.accelerationTime
	local rate = config.movementSpeed / math.max(seconds, 1e-3)

	local step = rate * dt
	if math.abs(target - speed) <= step then
		return target
	end
	return speed + (if target > speed then step else -step)
end

local function drive(dt: number): number
	local hullCF = rig.hull.CFrame

	-- Positive steer turns right, which is a *negative* rotation about Y.
	local yawRate = -math.rad(tuning.turnRate) * latest.steer
	local heading = (hullCF * CFrame.Angles(0, yawRate * dt, 0)).LookVector
	local flat = Vector3.new(heading.X, 0, heading.Z)
	-- Only reachable if the tank is somehow nose-down; keeping the old heading
	-- is better than normalising a zero vector into NaN and losing the model.
	flat = if flat.Magnitude > 1e-4 then flat.Unit else hullCF.LookVector

	speed = accelerate(dt)
	local nextPos = hullCF.Position + flat * (speed * dt)

	local hit = workspace:Raycast(
		nextPos + Vector3.yAxis * PROBE_UP,
		Vector3.yAxis * -(PROBE_UP + PROBE_DOWN),
		raycast
	)

	-- No ground found means the tank has driven off the edge of the world. It
	-- keeps its height rather than falling, because a demo tank that disappears
	-- has to be restarted and one that hovers can be driven back.
	local groundY = if hit then hit.Position.Y else hullCF.Position.Y - rig.rideHeight
	local targetNormal = if hit then hit.Normal else Vector3.yAxis

	-- graph: an exponential ease. `1 - 0.5^(dt/halfLife)` is the framerate-
	-- independent form; the naive `lerp(a, b, 0.1)` every frame eases at a speed
	-- that depends on how fast the machine is.
	local alpha = 1 - 0.5 ^ (dt / SLOPE_SMOOTHING)
	groundNormal = groundNormal:Lerp(targetNormal, alpha).Unit

	local right = flat:Cross(groundNormal)
	right = if right.Magnitude > 1e-4 then right.Unit else hullCF.RightVector
	local forward = groundNormal:Cross(right).Unit

	local position = Vector3.new(
		nextPos.X,
		groundY + rig.rideHeight + tuning.groundClearance,
		nextPos.Z
	)
	-- The third axis is the CFrame's *back* vector, so it is the negated
	-- forward. Passing `forward` here drives the tank in reverse, convincingly
	-- enough that the input handling gets blamed first.
	rig.hull.CFrame = CFrame.fromMatrix(position, right, groundNormal, -forward)

	return yawRate
end

--[[
	Turns the turret and raises the gun toward where the camera is looking.

	Both are rate-limited rather than snapped, and that limit is most of what
	makes a turret feel like it has mass: the camera arrives instantly, the gun
	takes a moment to catch up, and the lag between them *is* the tank.
]]
local function aimTurret(dt: number)
	local hullCF = rig.hull.CFrame

	-- Traverse: the aim direction's bearing in the hull's own space.
	local localAim = hullCF:VectorToObjectSpace(latest.aim)
	local desiredYaw = math.atan2(-localAim.X, -localAim.Z)
	turretYaw = stepAngle(turretYaw, desiredYaw, math.rad(tuning.traverseRate) * dt)
	rig.traverse.C0 = rig.traverseRest * CFrame.Angles(0, turretYaw, 0)

	-- Elevation: the same direction, measured in the *turret's* space, so the
	-- traverse the gun has already been given is not counted twice.
	local turretCF = hullCF * CFrame.Angles(0, turretYaw, 0)
	local localGun = turretCF:VectorToObjectSpace(latest.aim)
	local flatRange = math.sqrt(localGun.X * localGun.X + localGun.Z * localGun.Z)
	local desiredPitch = math.clamp(
		math.atan2(localGun.Y, flatRange),
		math.rad(tuning.minElevation),
		math.rad(tuning.maxElevation)
	)
	gunPitch = stepAngle(gunPitch, desiredPitch, math.rad(tuning.elevationRate) * dt)
	rig.elevate.C0 = rig.elevateRest * CFrame.Angles(gunPitch, 0, 0)
end

--[[
	Advances one track's textures by `distance` and returns where it got to.

	Every `Texture` on the part, because the tread wraps four faces of it and
	they have to stay in step; the tile size is read from the first one, since
	they were laid out together and disagreeing would be a modelling fault rather
	than something to accommodate.
]]
local function scroll(track: BasePart, distance: number, accumulated: number): number
	local tile = 0
	for _, child in track:GetChildren() do
		if child:IsA("Texture") then
			tile = child.StudsPerTileV
			break
		end
	end
	if tile <= 0 then
		return accumulated
	end
	-- Wrapped every frame rather than left to grow. A float that has been
	-- accumulating studs for an hour loses the precision the tread pitch needs,
	-- and the animation starts to stutter rather than to break.
	local wrapped = (accumulated + distance) % tile
	for _, child in track:GetChildren() do
		if child:IsA("Texture") then
			child.OffsetStudsV = wrapped
		end
	end
	return wrapped
end

--[[
	Scrolls the tread textures by the distance each track actually covered.

	The tracks are a shader trick — there is no track geometry and nothing
	physical to simulate — so "how far did this side travel" is the whole model.
	Turning is what makes it worth doing: a tank pivoting on the spot has one
	track running forward and the other back, and that reads instantly as a tank.
]]
local function scrollTracks(dt: number, yawRate: number)
	-- The speed the tank is actually doing, not the one the throttle is asking
	-- for. Scrolling by the request would run the treads at full pelt while the
	-- tank was still pulling away, which reads as the tracks slipping.
	local forward = speed
	-- A track offset +X from the hull's centre gains speed from a positive yaw
	-- rate, and `leftSign` says which of the two named tracks that is.
	local swing = yawRate * rig.halfTrackWidth * rig.leftSign
	leftScroll = scroll(rig.leftTrack, (forward - swing) * dt, leftScroll)
	rightScroll = scroll(rig.rightTrack, (forward + swing) * dt, rightScroll)
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Runs whether or not anyone is driving: an empty tank still settles onto the
-- ground under it, so getting out on a slope does not leave it standing at the
-- angle of the last slope it was on.
RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)
	local yawRate = drive(dt)
	-- Only while somebody is looking. An empty tank holds the turret where its
	-- last driver left it, rather than creeping back toward a heading nothing is
	-- asking for.
	if driver then
		aimTurret(dt)
	end
	scrollTracks(dt, yawRate)
end)

print(`M103 ready — walk up and press {prompt.KeyboardKeyCode.Name} to drive`)

	Danger = Color3.fromRGB(160, 0, 0),

})

const Fonts = table.freeze({
	Mono = Enum.Font.Code,
	Ui = Enum.Font.Gotham,
	UiBold = Enum.Font.GothamBold,
})

const Sizes = table.freeze({
	TitleBar = 24,
	StatusBar = 24,
	WindowTitle = 13,
	BodyText = 13,
	ScreenText = 14,
	Corner = 0,
	Padding = 8,
})

const Theme = table.freeze({
	Colors = Colors,
	Fonts = Fonts,
	Sizes = Sizes,
})

export type Theme = typeof(Theme)

return Theme

-- probe: ui-audit
-- datamodel: Client
-- params: minText=11
-- purpose: Objective UI checks on the live client: text too small to read, elements off-screen or clipped by the
--   window, ScreenGuis that reset on respawn (state lost), duplicates of one HUD. Run it at the target resolution;
--   then still LOOK at a capture - these checks cannot judge taste.
local player = game:GetService("Players").LocalPlayer
local vp = workspace.CurrentCamera.ViewportSize
local out, names = {}, {}
local small, off, total = 0, 0, 0
for _, sg in player.PlayerGui:GetChildren() do
	if sg:IsA("ScreenGui") and sg.Enabled then
		names[sg.Name] = (names[sg.Name] or 0) + 1
		if sg.ResetOnSpawn and #sg:GetDescendants() > 20 then
			table.insert(out, "RESET " .. sg.Name .. " has ResetOnSpawn = true: rebuilt (and state lost) on every respawn")
		end
		for _, g in sg:GetDescendants() do
			if g:IsA("GuiObject") and g.Visible and g.AbsoluteSize.X > 0 then
				total += 1
				local p, s = g.AbsolutePosition, g.AbsoluteSize
				if p.X + s.X < 0 or p.Y + s.Y < -40 or p.X > vp.X or p.Y > vp.Y then
					off += 1
					if off <= 5 then table.insert(out, "OFFSCREEN " .. g:GetFullName()) end
				end
				if (g:IsA("TextLabel") or g:IsA("TextButton")) and not g.TextScaled and g.Text ~= "" and g.TextTransparency < 0.9 then
					-- effective size: multiply every UIScale on the way up to the ScreenGui
					local scale, a = 1, g
					while a and a:IsA("GuiObject") do
						local u = a:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale")
						if u then scale *= u.Scale end
						a = a.Parent
					end
					if g.TextSize * scale < {{minText}} then
						small += 1
						if small <= 8 then table.insert(out, string.format("SMALLTEXT %.0fpx %s %q", g.TextSize * scale, g:GetFullName(), g.Text:sub(1, 30))) end
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
end
for n, c in names do
	if c > 1 then table.insert(out, "DUPLICATE ScreenGui " .. n .. " x" .. c .. " (a script runs twice or the gui is not cleaned up)") end
end
table.insert(out, 1, string.format("viewport %dx%d | visible gui objects %d | small text %d | off-screen %d", vp.X, vp.Y, total, small, off))
return table.concat(out, "\n")

--!strict
-- Directory layout of the art pipeline: all paths derive from --root and an art path.
local ArtLibrary = require("../../../src/shared/ArtLibrary")

local Paths = {}

Paths.DEFAULT_ROOT = "assets/art"

function Paths.isValid(artPath: string): boolean
	return ArtLibrary.isValidPath(artPath)
end

function Paths.leaf(artPath: string): string
	return string.match(artPath, "([^/]+)$") or artPath
end

function Paths.sourceDir(root: string, artPath: string): string
	return root .. "/source/" .. artPath
end

function Paths.blendFile(root: string, artPath: string): string
	return Paths.sourceDir(root, artPath) .. "/model.blend"
end

function Paths.specFile(root: string, artPath: string): string
	return Paths.sourceDir(root, artPath) .. "/asset.json"
end

function Paths.buildDir(root: string, artPath: string): string
	return root .. "/_build/" .. artPath
end

function Paths.rbxmFile(root: string, artPath: string): string
	return root .. "/rbxm/" .. artPath .. ".rbxm"
end

-- The directory part of a file path, for creating it before a write.
function Paths.parentDir(file: string): string
	return string.match(file, "^(.*)/[^/]+$") or "."
end

return Paths

--!nonstrict
-- Window.lua -- draggable Windows 3.0-style host window with title bar and
-- close button.

const UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

const Theme = require(script.Parent.Theme)
const Cleaner = require(script.Parent.Cleaner)
const Components = require(script.Parent.Components)
const State = require(script.Parent.State)

const Window = {}

export type Window = {
	Gui: Frame,
	Content: Frame,
	TitleLabel: TextLabel,
	Closed: State.State<boolean>,
	SetTitle: (self: Window, text: string) -> (),
	ClampToViewport: (self: Window) -> (),
	Clean: (self: Window) -> (),
}

local function rule(cleaner: any, parent: Instance, y: number, color: Color3): Frame
	const line = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("Frame"))
	line.Name = "Rule"
	line.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 1)
	line.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(0, y)
	line.BackgroundColor3 = color
	line.BorderSizePixel = 0
	line.Parent = parent
	return line
end

function Window.new(title: string, size: UDim2, position: UDim2?): Window
	const cleaner = Cleaner.new()

	const gui = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("Frame"))
	gui.Size = size
	gui.Position = position or UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	gui.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	gui.BackgroundColor3 = Theme.Colors.Surface
	gui.BorderSizePixel = 0
	gui.Active = true
	gui.ClipsDescendants = true

	const border = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("UIStroke"))
	border.Color = Theme.Colors.Border
	border.Thickness = 1
	border.Parent = gui

	-- Windows 3.0 title bar: navy, white caption, square controls.
	const titleBar = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("Frame"))
	titleBar.Name = "TitleBar"
	titleBar.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, Theme.Sizes.TitleBar)
	titleBar.BackgroundColor3 = Theme.Colors.Accent
	titleBar.BorderSizePixel = 0
	titleBar.Parent = gui
	rule(cleaner, titleBar, 0, Theme.Colors.BevelLight)
	rule(cleaner, titleBar, Theme.Sizes.TitleBar - 1, Theme.Colors.Border)

	const titleLabel = Components.Label(cleaner, titleBar, {
		Text = title,
		Font = Theme.Fonts.UiBold,
		TextSize = Theme.Sizes.WindowTitle,
		TextColor3 = Theme.Colors.AccentText,
		Size = UDim2.new(1, -40, 1, -2),
		Position = UDim2.fromOffset(Theme.Sizes.Padding, 0),
		TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left,
		TextYAlignment = Enum.TextYAlignment.Center,
	})

	const closed = State.new(false)
	const closeButton = Components.Button(cleaner, titleBar, "X", function()
		closed:Set(true)
	end)
	closeButton.Name = "Close"
	closeButton.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(16, 16)
	closeButton.Position = UDim2.new(1, -20, 0, 4)
	closeButton.TextColor3 = Theme.Colors.Text
	closeButton.BackgroundColor3 = Theme.Colors.SurfaceRaised
	closeButton.TextSize = 11
	const closeStroke = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("UIStroke"))
	closeStroke.Color = Theme.Colors.BevelDark
	closeStroke.Thickness = 1
	closeStroke.Parent = closeButton

	const content = cleaner:Add(Instance.new("Frame"))
	content.Name = "Content"
	content.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -Theme.Sizes.TitleBar)
	content.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(0, Theme.Sizes.TitleBar)
	content.BackgroundColor3 = Theme.Colors.Screen
	content.BorderSizePixel = 0
	content.Parent = gui

	-- Until the user drags the window it stays centred in its parent: the
	-- parent's size is not final when the window is first parented, so a one-off
	-- clamp used to pin it to the top-left corner.
	local userMoved = false
	local function clampToViewport()
		const parent = gui.Parent
		if not parent or not parent:IsA("GuiObject") then
			return
		end
		if not userMoved and position == nil then
			gui.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
			return
		end
		const size = gui.AbsoluteSize
		const area = parent.AbsoluteSize
		if size.X <= 0 or size.Y <= 0 or area.X <= 0 or area.Y <= 0 then
			return
		end
		-- Position is relative to the parent (the desktop frame), so clamp in
		-- local space instead of mixing screen insets with absolute pixels.
		const localX = gui.AbsolutePosition.X - parent.AbsolutePosition.X
		const localY = gui.AbsolutePosition.Y - parent.AbsolutePosition.Y
		const clampedX = math.clamp(localX, 0, math.max(0, area.X - size.X))
		const clampedY = math.clamp(localY, 0, math.max(0, area.Y - size.Y))
		gui.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(
			clampedX + size.X * gui.AnchorPoint.X,
			clampedY + size.Y * gui.AnchorPoint.Y
		)
	end
	task.delay(0.1, clampToViewport)
	cleaner:Connect(gui:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Parent"), function()
		const parent = gui.Parent
		if parent and parent:IsA("GuiObject") then
			cleaner:Connect(parent:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"), clampToViewport)
		end
		task.defer(clampToViewport)
	end)

	-- dragging via the title bar
	local dragging = false
	local dragStart: Vector3? = nil
	local startPosition: UDim2? = nil
	const isDragInput = function(input: InputObject): boolean
		return input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
			or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch
	end

	cleaner:Connect(titleBar.InputBegan, function(input: InputObject)
		if
			input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
			or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch
		then
			dragging = true
			userMoved = true
			dragStart = input.Position
			startPosition = gui.Position
		end
	end)
	cleaner:Connect(UserInputService.InputChanged, function(input: InputObject)
		if
			not dragging
			or not dragStart
			or not startPosition
			or not (
				input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement
				or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch
			)
		then
			return
		end
		const delta = input.Position - dragStart
		gui.Position = UDim2.new(
			startPosition.X.Scale,
			startPosition.X.Offset + delta.X,
			startPosition.Y.Scale,
			startPosition.Y.Offset + delta.Y
		)
	end)
	cleaner:Connect(UserInputService.InputEnded, function(input: InputObject)
		if isDragInput(input) then
			dragging = false
			clampToViewport()
		end
	end)

	const window: Window = {
		Gui = gui,
		Content = content,
		TitleLabel = titleLabel,
		Closed = closed,
		SetTitle = function(_self: Window, text: string)
			titleLabel.Text = text
		end,
		ClampToViewport = function(_self: Window)
			clampToViewport()
		end,
		Clean = function(_self: Window)
			cleaner:Clean()
		end,
	}

	-- closing destroys the window
	closed:Subscribe(function(value: boolean)
		if value then
			task.defer(function()
				cleaner:Clean()
			end)
		end
	end)
	return window
end
